### 8.4.4. Acknowledge notifications for crew member fails due to database conflict

Client sends initial getNotificationsRequest for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the initial request for this crew member must contain jcms_state=0.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;ISO-8859-1&quot;?&gt;
&lt;soap:Envelope xmlns:ns1=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2&quot;
  xmlns:soap=&quot;http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/&quot;&gt;
  &lt;soap:Body&gt;
    &lt;ns1:getNotificationsRequest created=&quot;2015-01-01T00:00:00&quot;
      crewId=&quot;12345A&quot; source=&quot;CheckInClient&quot; version=&quot;2&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/soap:Body&gt;
&lt;/soap:Envelope&gt;

Service responds with two notifications for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the response for this crew member contains jcms_state=125.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;soap:Envelope xmlns:soap=&quot;http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2&quot;&gt;
  &lt;soap:Body&gt;
    &lt;getNotificationsResponse version=&quot;2&quot; source=&quot;CrewCheckIn&quot; crewId=&quot;12345A&quot;&gt;
      &lt;notification startTime=&quot;2015-09-17T07:01:00Z&quot; endTime=&quot;2015-09-18T06:59:00Z&quot; type=&quot;DEASSIGNED_ACTIVITY&quot; text=&quot;Deassigned activity Reserve Off Duty - 1 day, 17SEP 00:01 - 23:59&quot;/&gt;
      &lt;notification startTime=&quot;2015-09-17T15:16:00Z&quot; endTime=&quot;2015-09-19T13:51:00Z&quot; type=&quot;ASSIGNED_TRIP&quot; text=&quot;Assigned trip 000008 - 3 days, 17SEP 08:16 - 19SEP 06:51&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;/getNotificationsResponse&gt;
  &lt;/soap:Body&gt;
&lt;/soap:Envelope&gt;

Client sends acknowledgeNotificationsRequest for crew member 12345A. The client must set
jcms_state to the value received in the getNotificationsResponse for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the request for this crew member must contain jcms_state=125, this guarantees that only
the two notifications previously received for this crew member are acknowledged.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;ISO-8859-1&quot;?&gt;
&lt;soap:Envelope xmlns:ns1=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2&quot;
  xmlns:soap=&quot;http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/&quot;&gt;
  &lt;soap:Body&gt;
    &lt;ns1:acknowledgeNotificationsRequest
      created=&quot;2015-01-01T00:00:00&quot; crewId=&quot;12345A&quot; source=&quot;CheckInClient&quot;
      version=&quot;2&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/soap:Body&gt;
&lt;/soap:Envelope&gt;

Service responds with a database conflict error for crew member 12345A. This error response indicates that
there are new notifications that the crew member has not yet seen and the acknowledgement operations was aborted.
This type of error response, with subcode=DatabaseConflictError, is returned when new notification
have been created for the crew member after getNotificationsRequest was sent but before acknowledgeNotificationsRequest
was sent.
The HTTP header of the error response for this crew member contains jcms_state=131.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;utf-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;ns1:Envelope xmlns:ns1=&quot;http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/&quot; xmlns:ns2=&quot;http://crew_checkin_soap_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com&quot;&gt;
 &lt;ns1:Body&gt;
  &lt;ns1:Fault&gt;
   &lt;faultcode&gt;
    SOAP:Server
   &lt;/faultcode&gt;
   &lt;faultstring&gt;
        Server Error
   &lt;/faultstring&gt;
   &lt;detail&gt;
    &lt;ns2:error code=&quot;TransientMessageError&quot; created=&quot;2015-01-01T00:00:00&quot; requestId=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;CrewCheckInSoap&quot; subcode=&quot;DatabaseConflictError&quot; version=&quot;1.0&quot;&gt;
     &lt;reason&gt;
            0: IOServer database conflict error. DatabaseConflictError: PlanHolderMave2Impl failed to save plan. Reason: dave::conflict_err:  CONFLICT_ERR:  Conflict detected for as_crw_not (id: O/qN6YW5QgyrLfw6gtWuiQ==, period_start: 10851, branchid: 1).
     &lt;/reason&gt;
     &lt;sourceMessage&gt;
      &lt;ns2:acknowledgeNotificationsRequest created=&quot;2015-01-01T00:00:00&quot; crewId=&quot;12345A&quot; source=&quot;CheckInClient&quot; version=&quot;1.0&quot;/&gt;
     &lt;/sourceMessage&gt;
    &lt;/ns2:error&gt;
   &lt;/detail&gt;
  &lt;/ns1:Fault&gt;
 &lt;/ns1:Body&gt;
&lt;/ns1:Envelope&gt;

In order to resolve the error, we must start over by sending a new getNotificationsRequest.
The HTTP header of the request for this crew member must contain jcms_state=131, this guarantees that the response
contains the new notifications which caused the conflict error.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;ISO-8859-1&quot;?&gt;
&lt;soap:Envelope xmlns:ns1=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2&quot;
  xmlns:soap=&quot;http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/&quot;&gt;
  &lt;soap:Body&gt;
    &lt;ns1:getNotificationsRequest created=&quot;2015-01-01T00:00:00&quot;
      crewId=&quot;12345A&quot; source=&quot;CheckInClient&quot; version=&quot;2&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/soap:Body&gt;
&lt;/soap:Envelope&gt;

Service responds with three notifications for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the response for this crew member contains jcms_state=134.

      &lt;notification startTime=&quot;2015-09-17T07:01:00Z&quot; endTime=&quot;2015-09-18T06:59:00Z&quot; type=&quot;DEASSIGNED_ACTIVITY&quot; text=&quot;Deassigned activity Reserve Off Duty - 1 day, 17SEP 00:01 - 23:59&quot;/&gt;
      &lt;notification startTime=&quot;2015-09-17T15:16:00Z&quot; endTime=&quot;2015-09-19T13:51:00Z&quot; type=&quot;ASSIGNED_TRIP&quot; text=&quot;Assigned trip 000008 - 3 days, 17SEP 08:16 - 19SEP 06:51&quot;/&gt;
      &lt;notification startTime=&quot;2015-09-17T20:35:00Z&quot; endTime=&quot;2015-09-17T21:03:00Z&quot; type=&quot;POSITION&quot; text=&quot;Changed flight YY123: assignment DH (FA)&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;/getNotificationsResponse&gt;
  &lt;/soap:Body&gt;

Client sends acknowledgeNotificationsRequest for crew member 12345A. The client must set

The HTTP header of the request for this crew member must contain jcms_state=134, this guarantees that only

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;ISO-8859-1&quot;?&gt;
&lt;soap:Envelope xmlns:ns1=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2&quot;

      version=&quot;2&quot; /&gt;

# 9. Crew Data Input

This chapter describes the interfaces that can be used to provide crew data to JCMS.
The sending system is generally regarded master for the provided information.

In JCMS the majority of crew data is valid during certain time periods. For parts of the information the validity is
actually an important part of the business data, for example it is important for planning to know if and when
qualifications will expire even if they are still valid today. Also actual documents, as passports and licenses,
have a natural validity period from when they are issued until they expire. For other information, like contacts,
the system generally only need to know what is valid right now. But for a 24/7 system it is an issue if the
information cannot be made available beforehand as it might be needed in real time.
To decouple the time of entering the information from the time of usage requires a notion of
“use these values from that point in time” which is solved inside JCMS with the same validity pattern
as we use for business validity.

Some part of the crew information is provided by systems that do not have validity information and in this
case a message implicitly has the semantics “this is what is valid now” where now is the time when the message was sent.
That is OK for all information where the validity itself is not business relevant. For that part of the data JCMS
offers a “plain mode” of transferring the data (by using the CrewDataPlain service), where it is always interpreted
as “valid now”. If the values in “plain mode” message differ from the currently valid values in JCMS, a new validity record
is created starting at the message creation time, ranging until further notice - or until any future change of the
same attribute(s) that is already registered in the system.

If the source system has validity information, then it should send the information using (“validity mode”) and message has
the semantics: “this is true for the given period of time”, where the start of the period is required and
the end could be left out (which means “until infinity”). In difference from the plain mode new values in such a
message will override any future values already present in JCMS if they overlap with the stated validity
from the message. In “validity mode” records can be explicitly terminated with terminate elements, meaning that
there is no valid value after that point in time.
For the data where the validity itself is business relevant as well as for documents the interface requires “validity mode”.

The crew member is always identified by its “crewId” which is assumed to be the same between all talking
systems and constant over the lifetime of a crew member data entry.
The crew data interface is divided into sections, each of them containing information for a certain kind of records in JCMS.
The basic section allows setting of common values, like name, gender and birth place.
Further sections deal with specialized data, the records are always identified by some additional key and
for each key there is only one valid set of values for each point in time. The general logic for updates on
that kind of information is explained above.

Latest version of this interface is 4.

Link to CrewDataInput_4_schema.json

Previous versions of this interface

Link to CrewDataValidity_3.xsd
Link to CrewDataPlain_2_1.xsd (version 2.1)

Available operations are:

pingPings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).

setCrewDataPlainUpdates information for a set of crew members where the information is valid as of now until further notice (one-way request without any response message).

setCrewDataPlainWithAckSame as setCrewDataPlain but with an acknowledge response on successful update (request/response).

updateCrewDataPlainUpdates information for a set of crew members where the information is valid as of now until further notice.
Possibly to control whether the operation should fail if the crew member, or specific information for the crew member,
already exists in JCMS (one-way request without any response message).

updateCrewDataPlainWithAckSame as updateCrewDataPlain but with an acknowledge response on successful update (request/response).

setCrewDataValidityUpdates information for a set of crew members where the information has explicit time validity, i.e. past, present and/or future records (one-way request without any response message).

setCrewDataValidityWithAckSame as setCrewDataValidity but with an acknowledge response on successful update (request/response).

updateCrewDataValidityUpdates information for a set of crew members where the information has explicit time validity, i.e. past, present and/or future records.
Possibly to control whether the operation should fail if the crew member, or specific information for the crew member,
already exists in JCMS (one-way request without any response message).

updateCrewDataValidityWithAckSame as updateCrewDataValidity but with an acknowledge response on successful update (request/response).

## 9.1. Crew data in the Jeppesen Ops Control system

A stripped down version of the interface exists for the Jeppesen Ops Control system which only requires a limited set of crew data.
With this interface the following crew data can be imported:

- Crew name and employment id
- Contacts (e.g. phone numbers and email addresses)
- Home base
- Operational rank

## 9.2. Life cycle of crew members

Crew members retiring or terminating their employment must no longer be visible to planning applications
in JCMS. What exactly defines a crew member as not available for planning may differ between installations but
typically the validity period of the CrewEmployment and/or the CrewHomebase is “closed”. It is worth pointing out
however that the Crew Data Input interface itself does not have a notion about whether a crew member is valid or not.
This means, any crew member in the database can be updated through the interface, also if they are no longer
valid from a business perspective. In any installation there should be a procedure for removing obsolete crew
members from the database, that are no longer needed by the applications inside JCMS or must be kept in the system
for legal reasons. Unless obsolete crew members have been removed, the system doesn’t provide any out-of-the-box
support for re-using crewId’s of those crew members to use with new employees.

## 9.3. Crew Data Sources

Normally the source for information in the different sections will be provided by different systems, most messages will not
contain data in all sections. The defined messages allow arbitrary combinations of sections to accommodate different
divisions of responsibility between the source systems. For this reason the “putCrew” operation is not supported,
neither in “plain mode” nor in “validity mode”. It is strongly recommended to identify a single system as the initial source
of new crew member data (for each group of crew) and only this system should use the “addCrew” operation to create
new crew member entries. All other systems should use explicit update messages to allow for out-of-sync detection.
Most often crew data is transferred in nightly batches from the HR and other systems, online configurations are possible as well.
It must be double checked then whether there is a risk of overlapping updates that would require some ordering per crew,
normally it is assumed that several messages for the same crew will not occur in the same time interval (a few minutes).

## 9.4. Removing Crew Data through the interface

It is important to note that the interface only operates on objects identified by their business keys as specified
in incoming messages. The business key of each data type is specified in the interface contract.
As an example, the business key of the CrewAddress data type is composed of the “crewId” and a “function”,
e.g. “home”, “summer home”, etc. So, if an incoming message contains only one CrewAddress record for function “home”
it does not mean that existing addresses with other functions will be removed in JCMS. (Emergency contacts is an
exception from this general principle, see Emergency Contacts below.)

There are however ways to remove crew data in JCMS through the interface. Generally, an object is removed
by the interface if only the business key fields are specified in the incoming message. If the data type contains
other required attributes (other than the business key fields), then they should be left empty (see the second one of
the Examples below). As mentioned above, in validity mode there are also terminate,  delete or clear
elements available in order to end the validity of objects. Note that specifically for seniorities, the only way to
remove a seniority value of a certain seniority group from a crew member in JCMS through this interface is by using
the terminateSeniority element. The reason why the first way is not possible is that the seniority itself is a
required attribute which cannot be set to an empty value in the message since it is of integer type.

## 9.5. Personal Information

Personal information includes the basic data and contact information (address, contact and emergency contact).
It can be provided in “plain mode” as well as in “validity mode”.
Crew addresses and contacts have in JCMS a key called “function” to allow the presence of several entries of
the same kind at the same time. For example it is possible to enter a “business” and “private” mail address or
a “home” and “summer home” land-line phone number. If the sending system doesn’t support several instances and
thus doesn’t have identification then a constant value shall be used that identifies the entry as
“coming from that system”, so that it can be updated independently from other sources. For example if the
crew calls in from a trip to report they had to acquire a new mobile phone since theirs got stolen, then
this number can be entered into another slot so it doesn’t get overwritten by the night-batch from the HR
system which might not have that information yet.

### 9.5.1. Emergency Contacts

In “plain mode”, the set of emergency contacts for a certain crew member is always sent as a complete state, i.e.
any existing emergency contacts are replaced by those given in the message. This has to do with the fact that
emergency contacts don’t have fixed “slots” as business key, in the same way as normal contacts or addresses.
If the incoming message contains any emergency contacts for a specific crew member, all existing emergency contacts
not matching any of the given name/relation combinations are removed in JCMS. Since this behavior is specific to
plain mode their complete timelines are removed, i.e. all time slices sharing the same name and relation.
In validity mode, no implicit clearing of existing emergency contacts is performed, thus the behavior in validity
mode is transparent with any other crew data type.
As explained in Removing Crew Data through the interface it is also possible to remove a specific
emergency contact by providing only the business key and excluding all other attributes. Then, the timeline of that
particular emergency contact is closed. In plain mode that means the timeline is closed at the message creation time,
i.e. the validity of the emergency contact ends at that point in time in JCMS.

Otherwise, when updating existing or creating new emergency contacts, the interface follows the ordinary standard
interface semantic of a set operation (see Naming Conventions).

### 9.5.2. Crew Contact Priority Handling

In JCMS each crew contact (except address) can have a priority describing the order of preference for these contacts
to be used (within one type, e.g. phone). If a crew message does provide a priority update, this will potentially
affect more than just one record since the logic is to re-sort the contacts of the same type so that the new
priority fits at the given position counting up from the lowest provided number. In other words, priorities of
existing contacts are shifted downwards if necessary, so that no contact has the same priority as another one of
the same type. If no priority is given when an update is provided then the priority is inherited from the updated
record. Change in priority does not affect the validity period of contact records.
If a new contact is added without an explicit priority given, then the system assigns the lowest priority at the
point in time given by the “validfrom” attribute of the contact or, the message creation time in case of a “plain mode”
message. E.g. if existing contacts of a certain type have priorities 1,2,5 then the new contact is assigned priority 6.
In the simplest case - no previously existing contacts of the same type - then, it means default value 1 is used.

Quite the same principle applies to emergency contacts. Since the priority order is a very important property for
emergency contacts it is strongly recommended that the sender always states priority starting from 1 if
that information is available.

A system that only has a ranking of primary among a list should send priority 1 for primary and leave the field
empty for all other contacts.

## 9.6. Employment and Deployment

Employment describes the contractual status of a crew member, like title rank and payroll related information.
Deployment means where and with what he/she is actually working, like the carrier and responsible department, base and
duty-pattern.
The strict differentiation between the two aspects can be disputed and is not important for JCMS except for data ownership
reasons. There is a “CrewEmployment” entry that covers what typically is HR information, a “CrewDeployment” section for
the carrier, department and related custom information (like work patterns).
The aspects of home-base and seniority are covered in their own sections since the handling and data ownership varies
more between installations. In addition, there is a section named “rank” (with data type “CrewFunction”) that represents
the assignable positions that a crew member can be deployed in. Crew member has only one rank at a time. If crew member
can fly either as e.g. Captain and as First Officer, this can be expressed with one rank that combines the different
positions. The translation between a certain deployment rank and the corresponding set of assignable positions is part
of the static base data in JCMS. Finally there is a “CrewCommuterAirport” section to represent information about airports
(other than the home base) which a crew member can easily reach. These are typically airports near the place where the crew
member actually lives. All the Employment and Deployment related information can be provided in plain mode
as well as in validity mode.

Note that the titleRank which is part of the employment section is not used in any way in the decision about what positions
or roles a crew member can be assigned to. TitleRank is not connected to the rank/position concept explained above,
and the rank enumerations can contain different values even though there is typically a big overlap - Captain is a
name often used both for a titleRank and a (deployment) rank.

If a contract code is given as a part of the CrewEmployment record, this code must match one of the existing contract
types specified as catalog data in JCMS. However, the interface does not require that the validity period of the
contract type as specified in JCMS actually matches the validity period of the CrewEmployment as specified in the
incoming message.

### 9.6.1. Default employer airline code

Although the employer airline code is a mandatory property in the internal model, it is not a required field in
crew data input messages. Instead of source systems sending an explicit employer airline code with each message, an
implicit employer code must be defined in the customization layer. In cases where lent-in crew members are used in the
planning process their actual employer code must be explicitly given (at least if JCMS requires a distinction between
employers, e.g. due to payroll management).

9.6.1.1. Crew Deployment
For CrewDeployment, if carrier is specified as an empty string, then default employer will be used as carrier.
If carrier is not specified, i.e. None, then if there exist a current valid deployment, the deployment will be ended.

## 9.7. Travel Documents

Passports and Visa are stored in JCMS as part of a more general set of travel documents, since there might be cases where
crew don’t use a passport but other type of identification documents to travel abroad, for example inside the Schengen area,
often an ID-card is good enough. Also instead of visa there can be green-cards or other documents, and they are not
necessarily bound to a single passport. Passport and Visa are identified by constant values in the document type hierarchy
which should be used to transfer the data.
Travel documents are always transferred in the “CrewDataValidity” service.

## 9.8. Crew Qualification Data

In JCMS crew qualification is described by a set of standard entities, depending on how the qualification is established
and maintained. In some cases the system keeps track of the actual documents that define the qualification; these are
called “CrewQualificationDocument”. An example could be the pilot license if the system is keeping track of it.
Other qualifications are just “planned and assumed” to be valid during certain (normally rather long) time periods,
this is typically the case for equipment specific qualifications as well as for restrictions. These are stored as
“CrewQualification” and “CrewRestriction” entries.
Additionally crew must normally successfully participate in certain events, like seminars and medical checks to maintain
their qualifications. The outcome of these (typically recurrent) events is kept track of as “CrewQualificationEvent” entries.
All qualification related information is transferred in the “CrewDataValidity” service.

## 9.9. Examples

The following example provides crew member data in plain mode. The crew member is inserted or updated based on the “crewId”.

## 9.10. Detailed use cases CrewDataPlain service

### 9.10.1. Create/update personal information

The CrewDataPlain service is used for communicating crew information interpreted as “valid now” to JCMS, i.e. all information
in the message is currently valid in the sending system. This service is useful for systems that know the currently
valid information but don’t keep track of historical and future crew information. Internally JCMS stores most crew
information with time validity. Information received over CrewDataPlain service is valid from the creation time given
in the message and until next existing record in JCMS starts. If no such record exists in JCMS, the given value is valid
until further notice. It’s a good practice to set the created time to the current date, ignoring the hour and minute
resolution as changes of crew data typically doesn’t need better granularity than the date it changed.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;updateCrewDataPlainRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;HR-system&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-01T00:00:00.0Z&quot;&gt;
  &lt;addCrew crewId=&quot;123456&quot; givenName=&quot;Bill&quot; surName=&quot;Johnson&quot;&gt;
  &lt;/addCrew&gt;
&lt;/updateCrewDataPlainRequest&gt;

The message above creates a new crew member with key “crewId” 123456 in JCMS or fails if the crew member already exists.
The name and surname properties of the crew member are set to the values provided in the message.

State of crew member in JCMS

The CrewDataPlain service can be used for updating single attributes at a time, which means only properties provided
in the message are updated in JCMS. The crew element for the message above could optionally also contain more crew
information e.g. gender, date of birth, marital status and nationality. Such information could have been included in the
message above but can also be supplied by sending an update message using the same “crewId”. This message might be sent from
another system which only knows these specific details about the crew member. This system however doesn’t master the
creation of crew members, hence the operation should fail if the crew member doesn’t yet exist in JCMS. This is a good practice
for finding synchronization issues.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;updateCrewDataPlainRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;CrewInfo-system&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-01T00:00:00.0Z&quot;&gt;
  &lt;updateCrew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;update gender=&quot;M&quot; birthDate=&quot;1973-06-15&quot; marital=&quot;MARRIED&quot; nationality=&quot;US&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/updateCrew&gt;
&lt;/updateCrewDataPlainRequest&gt;

The message above updates the properties of “crewId” 123456 using the given values in the message. The operation fails
if the crew member doesn’t already exist in JCMS.
Other properties of the crew member, e.g. given name and surname are not updated as they are not provided in the message.

### 9.10.2. Adding, updating and removing crew related objects

Crew related objects, e.g. crew addresses, can be created, updated and removed for a specific
crew member using the CrewDataPlain service. The interface only operates on objects identified by their
business keys as specified in incoming message.

The following crew objects follows the same procedure for create, update and removal:
- address
- contact
- employment
- deployment
- homebase
- rank

As an example we will use the CrewDataPlain service for creating, updating and removing addresses for a crew member.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;setCrewDataPlainRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;HR-system&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-01T00:00:00.0Z&quot;&gt;
  &lt;crew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;address function=&quot;PRIMARY&quot; city=&quot;Denver&quot; postalcode=&quot;12345-4567&quot; country=&quot;US&quot; state=&quot;Colorado&quot; street=&quot;8751 E Hampden Long Street&quot; extraLine=&quot;C2&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;address function=&quot;SECONDARY&quot; city=&quot;Winston Salem&quot; postalcode=&quot;10032-3365&quot; country=&quot;US&quot; state=&quot;North Carolina&quot; street=&quot;2425 Old Long Rd Apt 12c&quot; extraLine=&quot;&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/crew&gt;
&lt;/setCrewDataPlainRequest&gt;

The message above creates or updates two addresses with business keys “PRIMARY” and “SECONDARY” with the values given
in the message. JCMS only accepts objects with a known business key. The values “PRIMARY” and “SECONDARY” must
in this case exist in the database. The values to use as business keys may vary between installations and
must be defined by each customer installation.

The addresses are valid from 2015-02-01 00:00 as this is the created time of the message.

Updating the “PRIMARY” address of the crew member can be done by sending a message that
only contains the primary address.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;setCrewDataPlainRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;HR-system&quot; created=&quot;2015-03-02T00:00:00.0Z&quot;&gt;
  &lt;crew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;address function=&quot;PRIMARY&quot; city=&quot;Denver&quot; postalcode=&quot;11111-2222&quot; state=&quot;Colorado&quot; street=&quot;32 Sand Road&quot; extraLine=&quot;&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/crew&gt;
&lt;/setCrewDataPlainRequest&gt;

The message above updates the values for the “PRIMARY” address with new values and the change is valid from 2015-03-02 00:00.
Please note that country of the address is not updated as it’s not provided, hence the updated address keeps the same country.
Also note that addr_extra is set to null since extraLine is empty string.
The message doesn’t remove or update the “SECONDARY” address as this object is not specified in incoming message.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;setCrewDataPlainRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;HR-system&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-03T00:00:00.0Z&quot;&gt;

    &lt;address function=&quot;PRIMARY&quot; city=&quot;Denver&quot; postalcode=&quot;11111-2222&quot; country=&quot;US&quot; state=&quot;Colorado&quot; street=&quot;32 Sand Road&quot; extraLine=&quot;&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;address function=&quot;SECONDARY&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/crew&gt;
&lt;/setCrewDataPlainRequest&gt;

The message above removes the object “SECONDARY” address from 2015-02-03 00:00, and updates the “PRIMARY” address with the
values provided in the message.

### 9.10.3. Adding, updating and removing emergency contacts

In CrewDataPlain service, the set of emergency contacts for a certain crew member is always sent as a complete state, i.e.
all existing emergency contacts are replaced by those given in the message.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;setCrewDataPlainRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;HR-system&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-06T00:00:00.0Z&quot;&gt;
  &lt;crew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;emergencyContact name=&quot;Jane Doe&quot; relation=&quot;spouse&quot; phone1=&quot;+1 456 132124 45&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;emergencyContact name=&quot;Jim Grant&quot; relation=&quot;father&quot; phone1=&quot;+1 343 253532 22&quot; phone2=&quot;+1 343 111111 11&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/crew&gt;
&lt;/setCrewDataPlainRequest&gt;

The message above replaces all emergency contacts for crew member with “crewId” 123456 with the information provided by
the message. There is no information about the priority for the emergency contacts. By default the contacts
are prioritized as listed in the message (highest priority first).

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;setCrewDataPlainRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;HR-system&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-10T00:00:00.0Z&quot;&gt;
  &lt;crew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;emergencyContact name=&quot;Jim Grant&quot; relation=&quot;father&quot; phone2=&quot;&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/crew&gt;

The message above replaces all emergency contacts for crew member with “crewId” 123456 with the information provided by
the message. The “spouse” contact is completely removed (including all history). The “father” contact is updated and “phone2” information is removed
but other properties, e.g. “phone1” and “priority”, are kept as they are not included in the incoming message. The new values for “father” contact
are valid from 2015-02-10 00:00 (message create date) until further notice.

## 9.11. Detailed use cases CrewDataValidity service

### 9.11.1. Managing passport and visa information

Passports and related travel documents are managed using the CrewDataValidity service. Documents like these have
a natural validity period spanning between issuing date of the document until the expiry date of the document.

The following message can be sent to create a U.S. passport containing a Swedish visa.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;updateCrewDataValidityRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;APIS&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-20T11:10:26&quot;&gt;
  &lt;updateCrew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;setTravelDocument issueCountry=&quot;US&quot; documentNumber=&quot;31195855&quot; birthCountry=&quot;IN&quot; birthDate=&quot;1974-01-22&quot; birthPlace=&quot;Mumbai&quot; expiryDate=&quot;2014-11-17&quot; givenName=&quot;Rahul Sam&quot; issueAuthority=&quot;United States Department of State&quot; issueDate=&quot;2005-11-18&quot; surName=&quot;Gupta&quot; birthName=&quot;&quot;&gt;
      &lt;documentType category=&quot;PASSPORT&quot; type=&quot;PASSPORT&quot; /&gt;
      &lt;associateDocument issueCountry=&quot;SE&quot; issueDate=&quot;2012-02-14&quot; expiryDate=&quot;2012-06-01&quot; documentNumber=&quot;D23106202&quot;&gt;
        &lt;documentType category=&quot;VISA&quot; type=&quot;VISA&quot; /&gt;
      &lt;/associateDocument&gt;
    &lt;/setTravelDocument&gt;
  &lt;/updateCrew&gt;
&lt;/updateCrewDataValidityRequest&gt;

The following message removes the passport. Please note that removing the passport using deleteTravelDocument does not remove its
associated documents in JCMS. If one wish to remove both the passport and its associated documents, one can use clearTravelDocuments
element instead.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;updateCrewDataValidityRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;APIS&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-20T11:10:26&quot;&gt;
  &lt;updateCrew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;deleteTravelDocument issueCountry=&quot;US&quot; documentNumber=&quot;31195855&quot;&gt;
      &lt;documentType category=&quot;PASSPORT&quot; type=&quot;PASSPORT&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;/deleteTravelDocument&gt;
  &lt;/updateCrew&gt;
&lt;/updateCrewDataValidityRequest&gt;

The crew member doesn’t have any passport after processing the message above.

It’s also possible to provide all passports as state by including the clearTravelDocuments element in the request message to JCMS.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;updateCrewDataValidityRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;APIS&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-20T11:10:26&quot;&gt;
  &lt;updateCrew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;clearTravelDocuments&gt; &lt;!-- removes all existing passports of this crewmember before adding new ones --&gt;
      &lt;documentType category=&quot;PASSPORT&quot; type=&quot;PASSPORT&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;/clearTravelDocuments&gt;
    &lt;!-- All passports for this crew member provided as a state --&gt;
    &lt;setTravelDocument issueCountry=&quot;US&quot; documentNumber=&quot;31195855&quot; birthCountry=&quot;IN&quot; birthDate=&quot;1974-01-22&quot; birthPlace=&quot;Mumbai&quot; expiryDate=&quot;2014-11-17&quot; givenName=&quot;Rahul Sam&quot; issueAuthority=&quot;United States Department of State&quot; issueDate=&quot;2005-11-18&quot; surName=&quot;Gupta&quot; birthName=&quot;&quot;&gt;
      &lt;documentType category=&quot;PASSPORT&quot; type=&quot;PASSPORT&quot; /&gt;

      &lt;clearAssociateDocuments /&gt; &lt;!-- removes existing visas from this passport before adding new ones --&gt;

      &lt;!-- All visas for this passport --&gt;
      &lt;associateDocument issueCountry=&quot;JP&quot; issueDate=&quot;2012-01-23&quot; documentNumber=&quot;CC0064037&quot; expiryDate=&quot;2015-01-23&quot;&gt;
        &lt;documentType category=&quot;VISA&quot; type=&quot;VISA&quot; /&gt;
      &lt;/associateDocument&gt;
      &lt;associateDocument issueCountry=&quot;SE&quot; issueDate=&quot;2012-02-14&quot; expiryDate=&quot;2012-06-01&quot; documentNumber=&quot;D23106202&quot;&gt;
        &lt;documentType category=&quot;VISA&quot; type=&quot;VISA&quot; /&gt;
      &lt;/associateDocument&gt;
    &lt;/setTravelDocument&gt;

    &lt;setTravelDocument issueCountry=&quot;DE&quot; documentNumber=&quot;C01X0006H&quot; birthCountry=&quot;IN&quot; birthDate=&quot;1974-01-22&quot; birthPlace=&quot;MUMBAI&quot; expiryDate=&quot;2017-10-31&quot; givenName=&quot;RAHUL&quot; issueAuthority=&quot;STADT KÖLN&quot; issueDate=&quot;2017-01-11&quot; surName=&quot;GUPTA&quot; birthName=&quot;&quot;&gt;
      &lt;documentType category=&quot;PASSPORT&quot; type=&quot;PASSPORT&quot; /&gt;
      &lt;clearAssociateDocuments /&gt; &lt;!-- removes existing visas from this passport before adding new ones --&gt;
    &lt;/setTravelDocument&gt;
  &lt;/updateCrew&gt;
&lt;/updateCrewDataValidityRequest&gt;

### 9.11.2. Adding, updating and removing crew related objects

Crew related objects, e.g. crew qualifications, can be created, updated and removed for a specific
crew member using the CrewDataValidity service. The interface only operates on objects identified by their
business keys for the time period specified in incoming message.

The following crew objects follows the same procedure for create, update and removal:
- address
- contact
- emergencyContact
- employment
- deployment
- homebase
- seniority
- qualification
- restriction
- rank

As an example we will use the CrewDataValidity service for creating, updating and removing qualifications for a crew member.
The service can be used for feeding historical, current as well as future information for a crew related objects. Providing
historical information can be useful when initially feeding JCMS with information.

&lt;updateCrewDataValidityRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;TQ&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-20T11:10:26&quot;&gt;
  &lt;updateCrew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;setQualification validFrom=&quot;2002-01-01T06:00:00+06:00&quot; validTo=&quot;2005-05-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;aircraft:B737&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;setQualification validFrom=&quot;2008-05-01T00:00:00Z&quot; validTo=&quot;2011-02-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;aircraft:B737&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;setQualification validFrom=&quot;2011-07-15T00:00:00&quot; validTo=&quot;2013-11-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;aircraft:B747&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;setQualification validFrom=&quot;2014-02-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;aircraft:B787&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;setQualification validFrom=&quot;2014-01-01T00:00:00&quot; validTo=&quot;2014-07-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;airport:WLG&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/updateCrew&gt;
&lt;/updateCrewDataValidityRequest&gt;

The message above creates historical, present and future qualifications for crew member with “crewId” 123456. The message contains three aircraft
qualifications and one airport qualification. Please note that the object “aircraft:B737” contain two validity records defining
the periods when crew member was qualified for that aircraft type. The validity record for object “aircraft:B787” doesn’t include any validTo
information, hence this object becomes valid until further notice.

aircraft:B737

2013-11-01 00:00

aircraft:B787

2014-02-01 00:00

2014-07-01 00:00

An object is logically removed by using the corresponding terminate element. This operation removes the object at the validTo time specified
in the incoming message by ending its validity.

&lt;updateCrewDataValidityRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;TQ&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-20T11:10:26&quot;&gt;
  &lt;updateCrew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;terminateQualification validTo=&quot;2016-03-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;aircraft:B787&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/updateCrew&gt;
&lt;/updateCrewDataValidityRequest&gt;

The message above ends the validity for object “aircraft:B787” at 2016-03-01 00:00.

&lt;updateCrewDataValidityRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;TQ&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-20T11:10:26&quot;&gt;
  &lt;updateCrew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;setQualification validFrom=&quot;2015-01-01T00:00:00&quot; validTo=&quot;2015-07-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;airport:WLG&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/updateCrew&gt;

In order to communicate the full state of an object’s validity, the set operation(s) must be combined with a terminate element using an early validTo time.

&lt;updateCrewDataValidityRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;TQ&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-20T11:10:26&quot;&gt;
  &lt;updateCrew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;terminateQualification validTo=&quot;1970-01-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;airport:WLG&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;setQualification validFrom=&quot;2015-01-01T00:00:00&quot; validTo=&quot;2015-07-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;airport:WLG&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/updateCrew&gt;
&lt;/updateCrewDataValidityRequest&gt;

The message above contains the same validity period for the object “airport:WLG” but is preceded by a terminate element with validTo set
way back in the past. The terminate element wipes out both existing time slices of airport:WLG. The set operation then recreates the
airport:WLG qualification with the new validity period.

The technique to communicate the full state of an object, described in the previous use case, is usable e.g. in case the source system
wants to set the validTo of a qualification to a specific date without knowing the current validTo in JCMS.

&lt;updateCrewDataValidityRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;TQ&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-20T11:10:26&quot;&gt;

Then, the same terminateQualification element alone wouldn’t have any effect since the qualification already ends before the specified validTo.
Instead, in this case a setQualification operation would be needed in order to extend the validity of the qualification to the original validTo:

&lt;updateCrewDataValidityRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;TQ&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-20T11:10:26&quot;&gt;
  &lt;updateCrew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;setQualification validFrom=&quot;2011-07-15T00:00:00&quot; validTo=&quot;2013-11-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;aircraft:B747&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/updateCrew&gt;
&lt;/updateCrewDataValidityRequest&gt;

The problem illustrated in this example is that the source system would need to apply different operations depending on
the current state of the object in JCMS. To avoid this problem, the source system can communicate the state of the qualification by
combining the terminateQualification and setQualification elements as described in the previous use case. By using the same validTo
in terminateQualifaction as in the setQualification element, existing historical records of the aircraft:B787 qualification can be
retained:

&lt;updateCrewDataValidityRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;TQ&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-20T11:10:26&quot;&gt;
  &lt;updateCrew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;terminateQualification validTo=&quot;2013-11-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;aircraft:B747&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;setQualification validFrom=&quot;2011-07-15T00:00:00&quot; validTo=&quot;2013-11-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;aircraft:B747&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/updateCrew&gt;
&lt;/updateCrewDataValidityRequest&gt;

### 9.11.4. Providing objects as a full state

It’s possible for an external system to communicate the full state of certain objects, for example a set of crew qualification that might be mastered
by an external training management system.
The clear element should be used when communicating a full state. This guarantees that existing entries are removed from JCMS before adding
the objects provided by the message.

The example below provides all aircraft qualifications after year 2010 for crew member 123456. The attribute clearFrom makes sure to not remove any data in JCMS
before this date, since the message only provides qualifications for year 2010.

&lt;updateCrewDataValidityRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;TQ&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-20T11:10:26&quot;&gt;
  &lt;updateCrew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;!-- remove existing qualifications before adding new ones --&gt;
    &lt;clearQualifications qualification=&quot;aircraft:B737&quot; removeFrom=&quot;2010-01-01T00:00:00&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;clearQualifications qualification=&quot;aircraft:B747&quot; removeFrom=&quot;2010-01-01T00:00:00&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;clearQualifications qualification=&quot;aircraft:B787&quot; removeFrom=&quot;2010-01-01T00:00:00&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;!-- provide all qualifications as a state from 2012-01-01 and forward --&gt;
    &lt;setQualification validFrom=&quot;2010-01-01T00:00:00&quot; validTo=&quot;2011-02-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;aircraft:B737&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;setQualification validFrom=&quot;2012-08-15T00:00:00&quot; validTo=&quot;2013-12-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;aircraft:B747&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;setQualification validFrom=&quot;2014-03-01T00:00:00&quot; qualification=&quot;aircraft:B787&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/updateCrew&gt;
&lt;/updateCrewDataValidityRequest&gt;

The result is that qualifications in 2010 match exactly the information provided in the message:

qual

validfrom

validto

Training schedules can be updated by sending additional messages for the same curriculum. The interface updates existing training schedules if the
provided start and end times doesn’t deviate too much from the existing training schedule for that curriculum in JCMS. By default the interface creates a new
schedule if the provided start and end times deviate more than 60 days compared to existing schedule. The interface can be configured to override the
default value of 60 days.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;updateCrewDataValidityRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;APIS&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-20T11:10:26&quot;&gt;
  &lt;updateCrew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;trainingSchedule curriculum=&quot;B737Init&quot; start=&quot;2019-02-01T00:00:00&quot; end=&quot;2019-03-31T00:00:00&quot;&gt; &lt;!-- start / end times are updated --&gt;
      &lt;step number=&quot;1&quot; type=&quot;SIM73&quot; events=&quot;4&quot; requiredEquipment=&quot;B737&quot; /&gt;
      &lt;step number=&quot;2&quot; type=&quot;LIFUS&quot; events=&quot;8&quot; requiredEquipment=&quot;B737&quot; remark=&quot;No Asia&quot; /&gt;
      &lt;step number=&quot;3&quot; type=&quot;ILC&quot; events=&quot;2&quot; requiredEquipment=&quot;B737&quot; remark=&quot;Prefer Europe&quot; /&gt;
      &lt;step number=&quot;3&quot; type=&quot;NEW&quot; blockHours=&quot;PT100H&quot; requiredEquipment=&quot;B737&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;/trainingSchedule&gt;
  &lt;/updateCrew&gt;

It’s also possible to provide all training schedules per crew member as a state. This is done by providing the clearTrainingSchedules element in the message,
removing existing training schedules before adding the ones provided in the message. The clearTrainingSchedules element can further specify what time range and or
curriculum types to clear if the message only provides a subset of all training schedules.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;updateCrewDataValidityRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;APIS&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-20T11:10:26&quot;&gt;
  &lt;updateCrew crewId=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
    &lt;clearTrainingSchedules removeFrom=&quot;2019-01-01T00:00:00&quot; /&gt; &lt;!-- Remove all existing training schedules for this crew member starting after 01Jan2019 before adding new ones. --&gt;

    &lt;!-- All training schedules starting after 01Jan2019 for this crew member --&gt;
    &lt;trainingSchedule curriculum=&quot;B737Init&quot; start=&quot;2019-02-01T00:00:00&quot; end=&quot;2019-03-31T00:00:00&quot;&gt;
      &lt;clearSteps /&gt;
      &lt;step number=&quot;1&quot; type=&quot;SIM73&quot; events=&quot;4&quot; requiredEquipment=&quot;B737&quot; /&gt;
      &lt;step number=&quot;2&quot; type=&quot;LIFUS&quot; events=&quot;8&quot; requiredEquipment=&quot;B737&quot; remark=&quot;No Asia&quot; /&gt;
      &lt;step number=&quot;3&quot; type=&quot;ILC&quot; events=&quot;2&quot; requiredEquipment=&quot;B737&quot; remark=&quot;Prefer Europe&quot; /&gt;
      &lt;step number=&quot;3&quot; type=&quot;NEW&quot; blockHours=&quot;PT100H&quot; requiredEquipment=&quot;B737&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;/trainingSchedule&gt;
    &lt;trainingSchedule curriculum=&quot;B737RE&quot; start=&quot;2019-10-01T00:00:00&quot; end=&quot;2019-10-31T00:00:00&quot;&gt;
      &lt;clearSteps /&gt;

    &lt;/trainingSchedule&gt;

## 9.12. Providing invalid enumeration values in request message

Several values in the incoming request message refer to catalog data defined by various tables in JCMS. Example of such enumeration values
are marital status, rank, address type, contact type, seniority group, home base, country code etc. Valid enumeration values for
these types vary between installations and must be defined by each customer installation. The complete message
is rejected in case of providing enumeration values which don’t match the catalog data in JCMS.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;setCrewDataPlainRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;HR-system&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-01T00:00:00.0Z&quot;&gt;
  &lt;crew crewId=&quot;123456&quot; birthDate=&quot;1973-06-15&quot; marital=&quot;MAR&quot; nationality=&quot;US&quot;&gt;
  &lt;/crew&gt;
&lt;/setCrewDataPlainRequest&gt;

The message above provides invalid enumeration value for marital status. The message is rejected and no changes are saved.
An error message with the following content is created by the interface and put on a static error queue.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;setCrewDataPlainFault xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;CrewDataInput&quot; code=&quot;MessageError&quot; subcode=&quot;ReferenceNotFound&quot; requestId=&quot;1&quot;&gt;
  &lt;reason&gt;marital_status with key &#39;id=MAR&#39; not found in CrewBasicPlainUpdate.marital&lt;/reason&gt;
  &lt;sourceMessage&gt;&lt;![CDATA[&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;setCrewDataPlainRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewDataInput/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;HR-system&quot; created=&quot;2015-02-01T00:00:00.0Z&quot;&gt;
  &lt;crew crewId=&quot;123456&quot; birthDate=&quot;1973-06-15&quot; marital=&quot;MAR&quot; nationality=&quot;US&quot;&gt;
  &lt;/crew&gt;
&lt;/setCrewDataPlainRequest&gt;
]]&gt;&lt;/sourceMessage&gt;
&lt;/setCrewDataPlainFault&gt;

The error message states the reason for rejecting the message. In this case the provided value “MAR” for marital status
is not found in the catalog data table marital_status.

## 9.13. IOService builder configuration

Service CrewDataInput version 4 (see Note for IOService builder)

&lt;smog-service name=&quot;CrewDataInput&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; protocol=&quot;plainxml&quot;&gt;
  &lt;service-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_input_4/services.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;protocol-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_input_4/protocol.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;service-mapping location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_input_4/mapping.xml&quot;/&gt;
&lt;/smog-service&gt;

Service CrewDataInputJOC version 4 (see Note for IOService builder)

&lt;smog-service name=&quot;CrewDataInputJOC&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; protocol=&quot;plainxml&quot;&gt;
  &lt;service-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_input_4/services.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;protocol-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_input_4/protocol.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;service-mapping location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_input_4/mapping.xml&quot;/&gt;
&lt;/smog-service&gt;

Note that with this version of the above services also protocols soap and plainjson are supported.

# 10. Crew Data Output

This chapter describes the interface that can be used to extract crew data from JCMS.
Crew data is normally sent when explicitly requested by an external user or system (request/response pattern).
The interface can also be configured to send crew data spontaneously, either by triggering on changes or on a
scheduled basis (publish/subscribe pattern). The latter requires however a trigger service to be configured inside
JCMS. Such a trigger is not provided out of the box by the standard interface (or by the OTS system) but
must be added as part of an implementation project. In addition, it is also possible as a part of customization,
to add mechanisms to enable a user to manually request crew data to be sent out to predefined destinations.

Normally in a Crew Tracking system, only a small portion of the crew data used by the system is owned and mastered
by the Tracking system itself. Most of the data is normally mastered by other systems such as a HR system.
Nevertheless, the interface and the crew data that it exposes may of course be used as a practical
way to feed any downstream system for whatever purpose.

Latest version of this interface is 5.
Link to CrewDataOutput_5.xsd
Link to CrewDataOutput_5.wsdl
Link to CrewDataOutput_5_schema.json
Link to CrewDataOutput_5_openapi.json

The current version of this interface is 3.
Link to CrewData_3.xsd
Link to CrewDataSoap_3.wsdl

## 10.1. Interface capabilities

The interface supports the following request types:

The operation “getAllCrewData” requests the complete superset of crew data for all crew members, optionally
filtered by period, crew category, homebase and/or employer. If neither of those filtering criteria are specified, then all
crew members are returned. Else, the interface returns all crew belonging to the
specified category, homebase and/or employer at the start of the period (or the time of the request in case a period is not specified).
Note that if an employer is not specified in
the request, the system does not check for a valid employment even if a default employer is configured
(see Default employer airline code). If a period is specified in the request, it also limits the output
crew data to records valid anywhere inside the given period. If not specified, all historical, current and future
data is provided.

By means of operation “getAllCrewDataByCrewId” it is possible to request crew data for a list of crew members,
identified by their crew id (alias). At least one crew id must be specified in the request. A period filter can
optionally be specified just like in the “getAllCrewData” request.

The operation “getCrewList” requests a list of crew members, optionally filtered by crew category, homebase and/or
employer in the same manner as described for “getAllCrewData”. In contrast to “getAllCrewData” however, it requires
that a default employer is configured, unless employer is explicitly given in the request. The response consists of
a list of crew members with their crew id, category, homebase and employer. If crew has employments with more than
one employer, the one given in the request is chosen otherwise the default employer.

## 10.2. Scope of crew data

In this context, crew data is understood as properties describing the crew member and in some sense “belongs” to her/him.
Other information that is more loosely or temporarily associated with the crew member is not included. As an example,
surname, passport and address is regarded as crew data whereas annotations, check-in event recordings and activity
assignments are not.

The various types of crew data describe different aspects of the crew member. Some of these types belong to completely
separate business domains of the airline and are mainly unrelated. Therefore a subscribing or requesting system is
normally only interested in a certain subset of the crew data. In the standard crewdata output interface however no
attempt is made to partition the crew data into such predefined subsets. Beside the ‘getAllCrewData’ operation described
above, the standard interface provides definitions and mapping logic for each of the crew data types separately. These
can be easily referenced in the customization layer to define operations tailored for specific destination systems.
Such a custom operation aggregates these predefined standard definitions and mappings into a subset of crew data that
fulfills the needs of one (or more) specific consumer.

Note that the interface, as provided in its standard version, returns data for all crew members available in the
database, that may include crew members who have retired, terminated their employment, or are not available for planning
for some other reason. Such crew members are normally kept in the system for some time in order to retain a consistent
set of historical data. JCMS does not have a standard definition of whether a crew member is considered valid
or not since the criteria vary between airlines. In some cases it may even be the desired behavior to also include obsolete
crew members or crew members that are currently not available for planning. Therefore, the interface provides a predefined
filter function that can be overridden in the customization layer to implement specific filtering criteria for crew members.
This filter function is applied in both operations “getAllCrewData” and “getCrewList”.

## 10.3. Validity of crew data

In JCMS the majority of crew data is valid during certain time periods. For parts of the information the validity is
actually an important part of the business data, for example it is important for planning to know if and when
qualifications will expire even if they are still valid today. Also actual documents, as passports and licenses,
have a natural validity period from when they are issued until they expire. For other information, like contacts,
the system may need to keep information about future changes, i.e. to register an upcoming change of a phone number
before it is actually in effect. For these reasons, and for the purpose of keeping track of historical changes in
general, most of the crew data is stored in JCMS with a time dimension. For more information see Dates and Times.
It is possible per request to control whether the interface should return historical and/or future data. If a
requesting or subscribing system is only interested in current crew data (i.e. data that is valid at the time of the
request), then it should specify current time (in UTC) as both periodStart and periodEnd in the requests.

## 10.4. Organization of output data

An output message consists of a list of zero or more crew members, sorted by their crew id. For each crew member, some
basic attributes are provided along with a list of time valid data types. Each data type with time validity information is
output as a list of time slices, where each time slice represents a business object, e.g. a qualification, for a period
during which its attribute values are constant. If an attribute has changed at a certain point in time, that point in time
marks the start of a new time slice. Time slices are sorted by business object and secondly by validity start time. If no
records are available in JCMS for a certain data type, then an empty list of time slices is provided for that data type.
With each data type, the aggregated data period for all business objects is provided. If no records are available, the
aggregated period defaults to the requested period, if specified.

## 10.5. Default employer airline code

The JCMS crew data model supports storing crew members from different employers. An individual crew member may even have
contracts with more than one employer airline. Therefore, rank, contracts and seniority can be stored individually per
employer. This modeling option may be useful for airlines working with lent-in crew and where different employments must
be distinguished e.g. due to payroll management. If only the airline’s own crew members are stored in JCMS, the employer
is always the same and thus this modeling option is not used. For convenience, a default employer can be configured in
the customization layer in those cases, for the interface to use when an employer is not explicitly stated. Note that
even when a default employer is defined, another employer code may still be stated in a request message, in which case
it overrides the default employer for that request.

Default employer is configured by implementing the following Rave variable :

interfaces_core.%default_employer_p%

## 10.6. Error handling

The interface conforms to the same error handling strategy as most of the standard interfaces, i.e. to reject
the incoming message if it cannot be entirely and completely processed. as an example, a getAllCrewDataByCrewId request
is rejected if any of the given crew ids is not found in JCMS. In such cases an error message is also issued in
the log file, containing detailed information about the error.

# 11. Crew Messages service

This chapter describes the Crew Messages standard interface. It is used internally in JCMS
when sending messages to crew members over various communication channels such as email or SMS. The service
itself doesn’t implement the actual communication protocol sending the messages to crew. Instead it relies on some communication gateway as
part of a specific customer solution. Such a gateway may be an external system or a Camel route
in the Integrator, depending on customer solution.
External systems can also use this service for providing information about crew messages that has been sent, for example indicating
that a specific message has been read by a crew member.

In JCMS, two typical use cases exist for the Crew Message service:

As soon as there is a new crew roster change notification, the system sends a message to the crew member
if he/she has agreed to subscribe to such notifications. The message informs crew to log in to Crew Access
to view the actual changes to the roster. This feature requires a trigger service to be
configured inside JCMS. The trigger needs to react on new publication notification items in the data model
and send corresponding request messages to the Crew Messages service. Such triggers are not provided out
of the box by the standard interface but must be added as part of the customer project implementation.

- Tracker free text messages to crew members.

The receiving gateway may distinguish different use cases by looking at a special source attribute
in the output message. The content of the source attribute is copied from that of the request message.
Therefore, all output messages are typically sent to the same queue although other routing solutions can
be configured for specific customer implementations.

The current version of this interface is 3.
Link to CrewMessages_3.xsd
Link to CrewMessages_3_schema.json

Previous versions of this interface
Link to CrewMessages_2_0.xsd

## 11.1. Interface capabilities

Available operations are:

generateCrewMessagesUsed internally by JCMS for sending messages for one or more crew members. For each message, zero or
more channelTypes may be specified. The channelTypes are identical to the crew contact types defined
as base data in the data model, ‘email’ and ‘phone’ are typical examples of contact types.
For each channelType the service looks up the actual crew contact address for the corresponding
contact type and inserts it into the output message. If the crew member has more than one contact
of the specified type, then the one with highest priority (lowest priority number) is selected.

updateCrewMessagesUsed by external systems to provide information about crew messages that has been sent, for example indicating
that a specific message has been read by a crew member.

### 11.1.1. Content of the output message

One output message is produced per request to generateCrewMessages operation. The structure of the produced output message is the same as the request,
i.e. it may contain several crew members and more than one CrewMessage structure per crew member. In analogy
with the request, each CrewMessage can also specify more than one destination channel.
The following fields are included in the CrewMessage structure:

subject (optional). Copied from request. Not applicable for some channel types like land line or mobile
phones.

- body If body is missing in the request, &lt;UNDEFINED MESSAGE&gt; is used as output.
- messageId (optional). Copied from request. Should be used
channel (optional). If no ‘channelType’ is specified in the request then the receiving gateway is
assumed to know where to send the crew message. The channel consists of the following sub-elements:

- type. Copied from channelType in the request.
- contact. The actual contact as looked up by the service, e.g. email address or phone number.

As already mentioned above the source attribute on the root element of the output message is copied
from the request message in order to identify the origin of the message. There exists two pre-defined
sources in JCMS corresponding to the two typical use cases described above: Access for the roster
change notifications and JCMS for tracker free text messages.

### 11.1.2. Error handling

The interface conforms to the same error handling strategy as most interfaces, i.e. to reject a request message
if it cannot be entirely and completely processed. Concretely for the Crew Messages service it means that if
it fails processing any part of a request, an error message is generated and the entire request is discarded.
The following errors can occur when processing a request:

- Crew member not found. A crew member with the specified alias doesn’t exist.
- Specified ‘channelType’ does not exist as contact type in JCMS base data.
- Unknown contact address. Crew member doesn’t have any contact of the specified type.

Note that the ‘source’ attribute of the error message is always set to the service name, ‘CrewMessages’.
However, the origin can be identified through the request message which is also enclosed in the error
message.

## 11.2. Use cases

In this example a message is sent to two crew members with individual sets of channels.
The generateCrewMessagesRequest below is used internally in JCMS when sending messages to crew.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;generateCrewMessagesRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewMessages/v3&quot; version=&quot;3&quot; source=&quot;JCMS&quot; created=&quot;2021-05-03T15:43:32Z&quot;&gt;
  &lt;messageParameters crewId=&quot;222222&quot; messageId=&quot;80048064-fbcf-4e25-be5b-a48ac8eee1cb&quot;&gt;
    &lt;subject&gt;Test 1&lt;/subject&gt;
    &lt;body&gt;Hello, this is a test.&lt;/body&gt;
    &lt;channelType&gt;email&lt;/channelType&gt;
    &lt;channelType&gt;phone&lt;/channelType&gt;
  &lt;/messageParameters&gt;
  &lt;messageParameters crewId=&quot;333333&quot; messageId=&quot;80048064-fbcf-4e25-be5b-a48ac8eee1cb&quot;&gt;
    &lt;subject&gt;Test 1&lt;/subject&gt;
    &lt;body&gt;Hello, this is a test.&lt;/body&gt;
    &lt;channelType&gt;email&lt;/channelType&gt;
    &lt;channelType&gt;mobile&lt;/channelType&gt;
  &lt;/messageParameters&gt;
&lt;/generateCrewMessagesRequest&gt;

this leads to the following sendCrewMessages output message.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;sendCrewMessages xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewMessages/v3&quot; version=&quot;3&quot; source=&quot;JCMS&quot;&gt;
  &lt;message crewId=&quot;222222&quot; messageId=&quot;80048064-fbcf-4e25-be5b-a48ac8eee1cb&quot;&gt;
    &lt;subject&gt;Test 1&lt;/subject&gt;
    &lt;body&gt;Hello, this is a test.&lt;/body&gt;
    &lt;channel type=&quot;email&quot; contact=&quot;some.address@example.com&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/message&gt;
  &lt;message crewId=&quot;333333&quot; messageId=&quot;80048064-fbcf-4e25-be5b-a48ac8eee1cb&quot;&gt;
    &lt;subject&gt;Test 1&lt;/subject&gt;
    &lt;body&gt;Hello, this is a test.&lt;/body&gt;
    &lt;channel type=&quot;email&quot; contact=&quot;another.address@somehere.com&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;channel type=&quot;mobile&quot; contact=&quot;3456789&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/message&gt;
&lt;/sendCrewMessages&gt;

The output message above is forwarded to some communication gateway that is responsible for sending actual messages to crew using
appropriate communication channels.
The communication gateway and other external systems can also provide feedback to JCMS on messages that has been sent, by using the updateCrewMessages request.
The example message below can be sent to indicate what crew members that actually received and read the sent messages.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;updateCrewMessagesRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewMessages/v3&quot; version=&quot;3&quot; source=&quot;External system&quot; created=&quot;2021-05-03T14:26:23Z&quot;&gt;
    &lt;messageStatus crewId=&quot;222222&quot; messageId=&quot;80048064-fbcf-4e25-be5b-a48ac8eee1cb&quot; isRead=&quot;true&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;messageStatus crewId=&quot;333333&quot; messageId=&quot;80048064-fbcf-4e25-be5b-a48ac8eee1cb&quot; isRead=&quot;false&quot;/&gt;
&lt;/updateCrewMessagesRequest&gt;

## 11.3. IOService builder configuration

Service CrewMessages version 3

  &lt;service-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_messages_3/services.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;protocol-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_messages_3/protocol.xml&quot;/&gt;

# 12. Crew On Flight

This chapter describes the interface that can be used to get flight and related crew information from JCMS.
The flight and crew information is normally sent when explicitly requested by an external user or system
(request/response pattern). The information can also be published to external systems by JCMS, either triggered by database changes or
on a scheduled basis (publish/subscribe pattern). The latter requires however a service trigger to be
configured inside JCMS. Such triggers are not provided out of the box by the standard interface but must
be added as part of an implementation project. In addition, it is also possible, as a part of
implementation project customization, to add mechanisms to enable e.g. a Tracking user to manually request
crew list information to be sent out to predefined destinations.

The current version of this interface is 4
Link to CrewOnFlight_4.xsd
Link to CrewOnFlight_4.wsdl
Link to CrewOnFlight_4_schema.json
Link to CrewOnFlight_4_openapi.json

Previous versions of this interface
Link to CrewOnFlight_3_1.xsd (version 3.1)
Link to CrewOnFlightSoap_3_1.wsdl (version 3.1)

## 12.1. Interface capabilities

The interface supports three operations:

- The operation “ping” pings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).
The operation “crewOnFlight” delivers the list of crew members that are assigned to the flights
matching the given criteria of the request.

The operation “getFlightSummary” delivers the information about the flights matching the request along with a
summary, e.g. number of crew on the flight along with other information. The response doesn’t provide information about specific crew members.

### 12.1.1. Scope and content of returned crew list

A request must contain a date range (startDate and endDate), specifying the dateOfOrigin (udor) of the requested flights.
Other fields in the request (flightNumber, startStation, etc.) are optional, but can be used for specifying more details about the flights that should be returned.
The response contains all (non-deleted) flight leg instances with a dateOfOrigin in the date range that matches the values of the request, including return-to-ramp and wait-at-gate events.
The request should use same date as startDate and endDate when requesting information for flights on a specific dateOfOrigin.

### 12.1.2. Rave Definitions

The following Rave variables are defined in the CARMSYS and used by the Crew On Flight interface:

- interfaces_core.%cof_min_connection_time%: Minimum connection time needed by crew member for next flight.
- interfaces_core.%cof_leg_crew_competences%: Comma separated string containing all relevant competences for a crew member on this flight. Empty string if crew member has no relevant competences or void if competences should not be communicated for a crew member.

The business logic behind these Rave variables need to be implemented in a CARMUSR to comply with the expected behavior of each individual airline.

### 12.1.3. Error handling

The interface conforms to the same error handling strategy as most interfaces, i.e. to reject the message
if it cannot be entirely and completely processed. Concretely for the CrewOnFlight interface it
means e.g. that if it fails to find or process any of the flights or crew matching a “crewOnFlight” request, it
will respond with an error message.

## 12.2. Use cases

The examples below all use the plain XML service, the same use cases can be executed in the SOAP service
but then a SOAP envelope and the SoapAction header are required.

Request a single flight, identified by (startDate, carrier, flightNumber, startStation and endStation).

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;crewOnFlightRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewOnFlight/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; created=&quot;2014-08-30T12:00:00&quot; source=&quot;TEST&quot; startDate=&quot;2014-03-24&quot; endDate=&quot;2014-03-24&quot; flightNumber=&quot;101&quot; carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; startStation=&quot;MUC&quot; endStation=&quot;CPH&quot;/&gt;

this will lead to an output like the following

&lt;crewOnFlightResponse xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewOnFlight/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;CrewOnFlight&quot;&gt;

    &lt;assignedCrew&gt;
      &lt;crew crewId=&quot;123&quot; position=&quot;AH&quot; deadheadInd=&quot;false&quot; surName=&quot;Montez&quot; givenName=&quot;Lola&quot;&gt;
        &lt;trip name=&quot;humbug&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2014-03-24&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;minorAddition&gt;
          &lt;nextActivity minConnectionTime=&quot;PT30M&quot;&gt;
            &lt;leg dateOfOrigin=&quot;2014-03-24&quot; carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; flightNumber=&quot;101&quot; startStation=&quot;CPH&quot; endStation=&quot;GOT&quot; scheduledStartTime=&quot;2014-03-24T09:30:00Z&quot; scheduledEndTime=&quot;2014-03-24T11:05:00Z&quot;/&gt;
          &lt;/nextActivity&gt;
        &lt;/minorAddition&gt;
      &lt;/crew&gt;
      &lt;crew crewId=&quot;124&quot; position=&quot;FC&quot; deadheadInd=&quot;false&quot; surName=&quot;Jeppesen&quot; givenName=&quot;Elroy&quot;&gt;
        &lt;trip name=&quot;humbug&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2014-03-24&quot;/&gt;
