# 13. Crew On Flight import to JOC

This chapter describes the interface that can be used for importing crew flight connections into an Ops Control (JOC) system.

The current version of this interface is 4
Link to CrewOnFlightJOC_4.xsd
Link to CrewOnFlightJOC_4.wsdl
Link to CrewOnFlightJOC_4_schema.json
Link to CrewOnFlightJOC_4_openapi.json

## 13.1. Interface capabilities

Available operations are:

pingPings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).

updateCrewOnFlightThe operation “updateCrewOnFlight” creates and updates crew assignment and connection information for JOC.

The purpose of the CrewOnFlightJOC service is for a JOC system to import flight crew assignments and connections from JCT or
a third party Crew Tracking system. It takes as input the same message structure as produced by the ordinary CrewOnFlight service
(struct CrewOnFlightResponse), although only a subset is actually imported and used by JOC.

The following records or sub-structures are not used by JOC:

- annotation - annotations to crew for a flight leg
- passengers - number of passengers booked on the flight leg
- aircraft - the aircraft assigned to the flight leg
- trainingTag - set of tags to indicate training characteristics of the flight leg if used for training
- trip - the trip to which crew is assigned
- nextActivity - only next connecting flight leg is used by JOC, next activities of type groundTransport or groundTasks are ignored.

The crew assignments and relevant qualifications (a.k.a. crew competences) for a flight is imported as a state,
i.e. the interface expects all assigned crew members to be included, and for each crew member all qualifications for that flight leg to be listed.

For nextActivity, the flight number of the leg must be specified as a minimum. A fuzzy search is conducted trying
to identify the best-match flight leg. With more information provided, the match accuracy increases.

It’s strongly recommended to provide scheduledStartTime for the next flight leg, especially when the depature time of the current flight leg
is approaching. In this case, the search allows connection to go backwards within allowed deviation from the provided start time. This is also the case if scheduledEndTime is provided.
Otherwise, it assumes that the best known departure time of next flight leg must be after the best known arrival time of the current flight leg.

If only flightNumber is provided for the next flight leg, and the next flight leg belongs to a multi-leg flight,
the matching logic assumes that the start station of the next flight leg must match the end station of the current flight leg.
Therefore, it’s recommended to provide startStation of the next flight leg for co-terminal scenarios.

The allowed deviation is configurable by setting value for scheduledTimesMatchSlack of RequestHolder class.
The default value is 60 mins.

Example: to change allowed deviation to 90 mins

&lt;!-- use custom service-mapping for CrewOnFlightJOC in ioservice_builder.xml --&gt;
&lt;ioservice pattern=&quot;subscriber&quot;&gt;
  &lt;description&gt;Create/Update crew connections and qualifications.&lt;/description&gt;
  &lt;smog-service name=&quot;CrewOnFlightJOC&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; protocol=&quot;plainxml&quot;&gt;
    &lt;service-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/services.xml&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;protocol-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/protocol.xml&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;service-mapping location=&quot;$CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.ext/mapping_joc.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/smog-service&gt;
&lt;/ioservice&gt;

&lt;!-- use a different &quot;common&quot; module in .../std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.ext/mapping_joc.xml --&gt;
&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;service-mapping xmlns=&quot;http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2&quot; language=&quot;Python&quot; target=&quot;air2_mave2&quot;&gt;
  &lt;include href=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/mapping_joc.xml&quot;/&gt;

  &lt;input-mapping struct=&quot;flight_output.CrewOnFlightResponse&quot;&gt;
    &lt;import alias=&quot;common&quot; name=&quot;datafeeds.crew_on_flight_4.crew_on_flight_helper&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/input-mapping&gt;
&lt;/service-mapping&gt;

# set value for RequestHolder.scheduledTimesMatchSlack in crew_on_flight_helper.py
from std_interfaces.common import RequestHolder as core_request_holder

class RequestHolder(core_request_holder):

    scheduledTimesMatchSlack = 90

### 13.1.1. Identification of flight legs

When looking up a leg for processing the interface uses all the provided flight and leg key elements. If dateOfOrigin is not provided,
a best match is performed based on the scheduled start and end stations and times. The scheduled times are allowed to deviate from those
stored in JCMS in accordance with the scheduledTimesMatchSlack parameter as explained earlier. If no matching leg is found an error
message is logged but processing of other flights in the message continues.

### 13.1.2. Error handling

If the interface encounters a flight leg that it cannot identify in the JOC data model it skips that flight record with a log error
message and continues processing the next flight record in the message. If a connecting flight (next leg) cannot be identified based
on the specified properties, then that crew connection is skipped with a warning message. If some other part of the connection information,
e.g. the specified crew position or a crew competence type, then the crew connection is still stored but without that piece of information.
A warning log message is also issued. If a crew member cannot be identified by it’s crewId, the interface creates the crew member ad hoc
in the JOC data model using the specified surname and given name, if available.

## 13.2. Use cases

The examples below all use the plain XML service, the same use cases can be executed in the SOAP service
but then a SOAP envelope and the SoapAction header are required.

The example below illustrates the usage of the client implementation for importing flight crew connection information into JOC.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;crewOnFlightResponse xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewOnFlightJOC/v4&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; source=&quot;AIMS&quot; created=&quot;2014-03-25T07:10:45Z&quot;&gt;
  &lt;flight carrier=&quot;JP&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2014-03-25&quot; flightNumber=&quot;942&quot; startStation=&quot;CCU&quot; endStation=&quot;BLR&quot; scheduledStartTime=&quot;2014-03-25T06:15:00Z&quot; scheduledEndTime=&quot;2014-03-25T08:15:00Z&quot;&gt;
    &lt;assignedCrew&gt;
      &lt;crew crewId=&quot;12345&quot; position=&quot;FC&quot;&gt;
        &lt;minorAddition&gt;
          &lt;!-- provide all qualifications relevant in JOC for this crew member --&gt;
          &lt;qualifications&gt;
            &lt;qualName&gt;LVTO&lt;/qualName&gt;
            &lt;qualName&gt;ILS-CAT3&lt;/qualName&gt;
          &lt;/qualifications&gt;
          &lt;!-- only provide next connecting flight leg of crew member if it&#39;s within same duty --&gt;
          &lt;nextActivity minConnectionTime=&quot;PT45M&quot;&gt;
            &lt;leg flightNumber=&quot;435&quot; /&gt;
          &lt;/nextActivity&gt;
        &lt;/minorAddition&gt;
      &lt;/crew&gt;
      &lt;crew crewId=&quot;54321&quot; position=&quot;AH&quot;&gt;
        &lt;minorAddition&gt;
          &lt;!-- provide empty &lt;qualifications&gt; element if there are no relevant qualifications for this crew member --&gt;
          &lt;qualifications /&gt;
          &lt;!-- only provide next connecting flight leg of crew member if it&#39;s within same duty --&gt;
          &lt;nextActivity minConnectionTime=&quot;PT45M&quot;&gt;
            &lt;leg flightNumber=&quot;123&quot; scheduledStartTime=&quot;2014-03-26T10:00:00Z&quot;/&gt;
          &lt;/nextActivity&gt;
        &lt;/minorAddition&gt;
      &lt;/crew&gt;
    &lt;/assignedCrew&gt;
  &lt;/flight&gt;
&lt;/crewOnFlightResponse&gt;

# 14. Crew On Flight Events

This chapter describes the standard interface for publishing crew on flight information
to external systems when changes to these assignments occur in JCMS.
Crew On Flight messages are published by the interface
when crew flight assignment information is updated in the database.
For details about the native format, please refer to the Crew On Flight interface
(see Crew On Flight).

This interface utilizes the message receivers pattern (see Message Receivers)
to enable configuration of different logical receivers with different format expectations,
and the Subscription Management pattern (see Subscription Management) to
enable runtime configuration of the subscription filter.
The default receiver uses the CrewOnFlightFormatter which supports splitting the
message per flight. In addition, there are a number of standard formatters available for
various purposes. All formatters are described below in Formatters.

The default subscription configuration
is a gliding subscription with a PeriodFilter covering 30 days back and 60 days forward,
see std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.trigger.
The standard mapping for this interface is based on the mappings for the request/response service,
but adds the formatting and subscription features.

&lt;service-mapping xmlns=&quot;http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2&quot; target=&quot;crew_on_flight_delta&quot; language=&quot;Python&quot;&gt;
  &lt;include href=&quot;./mapping.xml&quot;/&gt;

  &lt;!-- add postprocess to the default server mapping --&gt;
  &lt;server-impl service_name=&quot;CrewOnFlight&quot; service_version=&quot;4&quot;&gt;
    &lt;post-process name=&quot;format&quot; module=&quot;std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.generators&quot; function=&quot;CrewOnFlightMessageGenerator.format&quot; operation=&quot;getCrewOnFlight&quot; process_struct=&quot;true&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/server-impl&gt;

  &lt;input-mapping struct=&quot;flight_output.CrewOnFlightRequest&quot;&gt;
    &lt;import alias=&quot;generators&quot; name=&quot;std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.generators&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;import alias=&quot;formatters&quot; name=&quot;std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.formatters&quot;/&gt;

    &lt;assign name=&quot;dataset&quot; expr=&quot;&#39;LIVE&#39;&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;assign name=&quot;plan&quot; expr=&quot;request_holder.plan&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;assign name=&quot;changeset&quot; expr=&quot;planholder.getChangeSet()&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;assign name=&quot;service_logger&quot; expr=&quot;service_context.service_logger&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;assign name=&quot;now_time&quot; expr=&quot;planholder.getNowTime()&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;assign name=&quot;subscription_filter&quot; expr=&quot;service_context.subscription_manager.filter&quot;&gt;
      &lt;condition expr=&quot;service_context.subscription_manager is not None&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;/assign&gt;

    &lt;!-- avoid r/r default flight selection --&gt;
    &lt;assign name=&quot;flights&quot; expr=&quot;[]&quot;/&gt;

    &lt;!-- initialize the generator and formatter --&gt;
    &lt;assign name=&quot;generator&quot; expr=&quot;generators.CrewOnFlightMessageGenerator(@{service}, plan, service_logger, now_time, subscription_filter)&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;assign name=&quot;formatter&quot; expr=&quot;formatters.CrewOnFlightFormatter(service_logger, split_msg=True)&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;call name=&quot;add_formatter&quot; expr=&quot;generator.add_receiver(&#39;from.ioservice.CrewOnFlight_4_event&#39;, formatter)&quot;/&gt;

    &lt;!-- find affected flights--&gt;
    &lt;call-last name=&quot;find_flights&quot; expr=&quot;flights.extend(generator.find_affected_flights(changeset))&quot;/&gt;

  &lt;/input-mapping&gt;
&lt;/service-mapping&gt;

Crew information is by default communicated using the LIVE dataset, but
the service can be configured to use PUBLISHED or ACKNOWLEDGED dataset instead.
This is achieved by using a custom SMOG mapping, overriding the dataset variable.

&lt;input-mapping struct=&quot;flight_output.CrewOnFlightRequest&quot;&gt;
  &lt;assign name=&quot;dataset&quot; expr=&quot;&#39;PUBLISHED&#39;&quot;/&gt;
&lt;/input-mapping&gt;

Note that one SMOG mapping file is needed for each dataset name, and each smog mapping
file must have a unique target attribute in the &lt;service-mapping&gt; element.

With the example configuration below, every day at 0:30, the load service goes through all flight legs
with a departure time (actual, estimated, or scheduled) within the subscription period, 0:00 - 48:00 hours from now time.

  &lt;/delta-service&gt;
  &lt;load-service name=&quot;CrewOnFlight&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; protocol=&quot;plainxml&quot; &gt;
    &lt;service-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/services.xml&quot; /&gt;

# 15. Crew Roster Input

This chapter describes the interfaces that can be used to provide roster data to JCMS. Roster data usually has a shared ownership model,
where the data for different time periods is owned by different systems at different times in the planning process.

The current version of this interface is 3.
Link to RosterState_3.xsd
Link to RosterState_3.wsdl
Link to RosterState_3_schema.json
Link to RosterState_3_openapi.json

Previous versions of this interface is 2.1.
Link to RosterState_2_1.xsd

## 15.1. Interface capabilities

The source system may send updates for several updates in one message. The interface then treats the complete
message as one transaction. Should an error occur for one of the roster updates, the others will be discarded too.
The general error handling strategy is to store any incoming data if possible, even if it is considered illegal.
Data that cannot be stored, e.g. assignments referring to a non-existing station, will always yield an exception
and the message will be rejected. This is true regardless if the faulty data is required or not.

Available operations are:

pingPings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).

setRostersUpdates rosters in JCMS with information from the provided message (one-way request without any response message).

setRostersWithAckSame as setRosters but with an acknowledge response on successful operation (request/response).

The interface handles crew assignments to trips and tasks.

trip:

- Assigned trips are expected to be already existing in the system before being assigned to crew members by this interface.
- This interface doesn’t support assignment information of activities within a trip, e.g. assigned training tag/roster tag on a flight leg within a trip is not supported.

task:

- Tasks are created by the interface together with the assignment to that activity.
Internally in JCMS a task may be classified as either a “ground task”, e.g. a training task, or a “personal activity” (pact), e.g. a vacation.

A ground task is “wrapped” inside a trip internally in JCMS, and the crew member is assigned to the wrapper trip instead of to the activity
directly. The interface creates the wrapper trip automatically for ground task.

- A personal activity is directly assigned to the crew member without being “wrapped” inside a trip.

JCMS will use the current state (at time of the message evaluation) of the trip or task to fill the assignment attributes (stations and times).

Additional crew assignment information can be provided in the form of assignment training tags and roster tags.
The information is updated as a state, i.e. the assigned training tags/roster tags in JCMS are updated to match the information in the inbound message.
Tags are removed from the roster in JCMS if the inbound message doesn’t have any tag for the assignment respectively, even if the existing tags
were added by some other user or process.

Changes are saved in the live dataset and normally published automatically. It is possible to configure
the interface so that changes are also acknowledged automatically.

The picture below illustrates the logical flow when the interface handles a roster update request. The remainder
of this chapter provides more details on various aspects of the functionality.

Activity diagram for roster updates¶

### 15.1.1. Matching of trips and tasks

For the matching of trips and tasks in the roster interface first of all the general rules described in the
introduction apply, see Matching of Planning Objects. The purpose of the matching is to find existing trips
or activities on the roster on which the roster update operations should be applied.

For trips, if no matching trip is found or if the match is ambiguous, then the operation fails and an error response message is returned.
By default, only “name” and “dateOfOrigin” in TripMatch elements are used for trip matching, other attributes (“category”, “homeBase”
“startStation”, “endStation”, “startTime”, “endTime”) are not used for matching and will be removed in future version of this interface.

Tasks are only looked up within the given crew member’s roster. The matching requires the activityType as well as the stations to
be identical and for the start/end the same fuzzy matching as for flights is used. The interface creates
new tasks on the roster if necessary.
If no stations are provided for a task, the most recent valid homebase of the crew member, relative to the activity’s start time,
are used as default stations.

Generally, if an existing assignment is found it is updated with the role attribute and additional information that is available on the
assignment in the message.

Note that if an existing trip assignment is not found, then a role must be specified in order for a new assignment
to be created, otherwise the operation will fail. For ground tasks and (non-personal) ground transports on the other hand,
role is not required. If a role is specified, it is used when assigning the wrapper trip that contains the task. If a role
is not specified, then a default role is derived from the crew member’s function. For personal activities, a role is not
required, therefore no default role is used if not specified.

If no role is specified when updating an existing ground task or (non-personal) ground transport assignment, then
the role will fall back to the default role. If no role is specified when updating an existing personal activity
assignment, then the role will be removed if a role existed in the data model before the update.

The picture below illustrates the process of matching trips and tasks from a logical point of view.

Activity diagram for matching existing trips and tasks¶

If the best match is ambiguous then the operation will fail. If no matching task is found the interface will create one.
Tasks that are no longer assigned will be completely deleted (not only de-assigned). For a found match, the
activity times will be updated if they differ from those specified in the message.

As mentioned earlier, wrapper trips are created when adding a new ground task or a (non-personal) ground transport activity.
The homebase of the wrapper trip is derived in the following way (in priority order):

- The base associated with the activity’s start station, if any
- The base associated with the activity’s end station, if any
- The base whose id is identical to the id of the activity’s start station, if exists
- The base whose id is identical to the id of the activity’s end station, if exists
- The most recent valid homebase of the crew member, relative to the activity’s start time

The interface does not enforce that this homebase corresponds
to the start station of the activity. A deviation will result in an illegal trip that will have to be manually
repaired, e.g. by adding deadhead transports to and from the activity station. Furthermore, the crew composition of the
wrapper trip is set to reflect the role that is used for the assignment, whether it is provided in the message or a derived
default role.

Time offset, i.e. time zone difference to UTC, checking is performed on all specified times, if the offsets are provided. The picture below illustrates
the process of checking time offsets. Note that in the baseline version of roster input interfaces, offsets can
only be provided for tasks. In the figure below, it means only the lower left corner is in effect.

Activity diagram for checking start and end time offsets¶

### 15.1.2. Roster State Input

Roster state input (setRosters operation in RosterState service) is suitable for loading initial rosters or big updates.
It provides complete state of some crew members roster for a given time period.
The given period for updates must be guaranteed to cover all potential changes, so if the source system doesn’t have
fine grained change detection it should send with fixed coarse granularity.
All assignments that might exist in this time period before the message is applied will be removed if no
longer present in the provided data. Assignments that are present both in the message and in the existing roster
will be updated to match the data in the message.

Note that also locked assignments may be updated by the interface, but they are not removed even if the message
doesn’t contain them.

This kind of message is generally sent in batch mode and no two messages about the same crew are expected within the
same time interval (of a few minutes). If it is decided to use this kind of messages in online mode or in combination
with other flows that could touch the same crew in parallel, then conflict detection must be secured. Either all
involved flows use a consistent state reference mechanism (e.g. the cid) or a conflict trigger must be implemented
that fits the message granularity. Note that this method is not well suited for frequent incremental roster updates
since it requires a coarse granularity of conflict detection and is thus prone to temporary “data-to-old” errors.
It might still be the only valid method depending on the capabilities of the source system(s), but note that frequent
messages about the same crew member will lead to many transient errors and thus bad overall performance.

Annotations that are intended to be shared with crew members can be  provided over the interface, such annotations
are internally stored with code PUBLIC.

15.1.2.1. Roster layer concept
Some sending system might not be aware of the full state of a roster, but only of a selected set of assignments.
We call that selection the  “roster layer” which the source system is responsible for.
The setRosters operation can also be used in this case as long as the assignments in each roster layer can be clearly
identified inside JCMS. The layer is identified by the source name in the message. The message is then interpreted as
replacement for the set of all assignments in the affected roster layer inside the time period.

A typical case is a vacation system which only knows about absences for crew.
The standard interface implementation supports this kind of layer by associating a selection of activity types with
a given source. If a source has a list of activity codes associated with it, then its layer consists of all assigned
activities with any of the codes.
A source that has no definition attached is expected to be the “remaining” and its layer consists of all
assignments that do not have any of the activity codes associated with any other source. By definition this
layer contains all assigned trips because a trip doesn’t have an activity code. This does of course not apply to
the wrapper trips mentioned above.

Since the core implementation doesn’t contain any predefined sets of activity codes, by default all sources will
affect the full roster.

Customization can define sets of activity codes for different sources by adding them to the (default empty)
dictionary defined in the python module that provides the business functions for this interface.
Where more complex logic is needed (e.g. to define a layer that contains a subset of trip assignments) the layer
identification function must be overwritten.

15.1.2.2. Matching of trips and tasks within the roster period
A roster state header shall always give the actually delivered period per roster, but not covering the full carry-out.
If any requested assignment doesn’t start in the specified period the operation will fail, but ending outside the period is ok.
Report time is taken as start time for an assignment, if report time is within the specified period then the operation will succeed.
Note that existing assignments that are found based on the provided information are not dropped even if they
violate these consistency requirements, e.g a trip will stay assigned even if it isn’t fully within the period.

For each provided assignment, the trip or task is looked up according to the principles described above,
see Matching of trips and tasks.

An activity that does not start in the period can only be assigned by providing Task times in the message that are within the
period. Since the activity times are required there is always a check that the actual activity times don’t deviate
too much from the Task times specified in the message. These times are supposed to reflect the source systems view
of the activity state. The actual activity (and wrapper trip if applicable) is updated to reflect this state.

The roster update is supposed to contain the complete state of the crew members roster for the specified layer
and within the specified time period. Any existing assignments that are not included in the message, are removed
unless they are locked.
For ground tasks, the interface not only removes the assignment but also the associated wrapper trip.
Likewise for personal activities the interface removes the assignment. However for technical reasons the activity object itself
is not dropped from the data model, although no crew is assigned to it.

The picture below illustrates the process of removing existing assignments and activities that don’t belong to the
updated roster state.

Activity diagram for removing non-matched assignments¶

## 15.2. Use cases

### 15.2.1. Example scenario

For the examples we assume an installation of JCMS and the crew rosters are fed in from other systems.
The Rostering system for cockpit crew has been updated recently to deal with the full state, including planned absences,
while for cabin crew the vacation and long term absences are handled in a  separate system still.

For process reasons Holiday seasons are planned separately,
we assume the next planning period to load is from 28th of November to 20th of December 2009.
The rosters are already available for November, and now we are about to load the next month.

The base for the following examples is the state of the roster for a Flight Officer and a Purser, to demonstrate the difference in layer handling.
For cockpit crew the Rostering system is the only source and all assignments are owned by it until the Tracking period starts.
For cabin crew all activities in the activity groups “VAC” (vacation) and “LOA” (leave of absence) are provided and maintained in the vacation system
while all other activities are owned by the Rostering system until the Tracking period starts.

From a technical perspective we have a layer setup like this:

- Cockpit has just one layer for all assignments. (Default layer)
- Cabin has two layers. One for vacations and one for the rest.

### 15.2.2. UC: Basic update of trip assignments

Actor: An external system that sends messages containing only crew trip assignments.

Actor: A person with role tracker, that changes a trip and locks it.

As there is no coupling between different crew member’s rosters, even though the data can come in the same in message,
this UC only needs to consider one crew member’s roster.
Precondition: we need to have to trips that we can assign.

First the rostering system sends us a msg that contains two assignments of trips, asmt1 &amp; asmt2.
We process the msg and assign them to the crew member with the specific role for each asmt.
Then the tracker actor updates the asmt1, changing the role, and then locks it, preventing it from being deleted by incoming msgs.
The external system sends an update that deletes asmt1 &amp; updates asmt2 with a different role.
This results in no changes for asmt 1, since it is locked, and updates of the asmt 2.
Note that the asmt 2 object should be updated not recreated, so it should still contain the same untouched data as before.
Assignment 2 has new role as FC.

In messages:

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; ?&gt;
&lt;ns1:setRostersRequest created=&quot;2009-12-01T00:00:00&quot;
	source=&quot;ROSTER&quot; version=&quot;2.1&quot;
	xmlns:ns1=&quot;http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com&quot;&gt;
	&lt;ns1:roster crewId=&quot;04873&quot; end=&quot;2009-12-05T00:00:00&quot; start=&quot;2009-11-05T00:00:00&quot;&gt;
		&lt;ns1:assignment role=&quot;FP&quot;&gt;
			&lt;ns1:trip name=&quot;51470&quot; /&gt;
		&lt;/ns1:assignment&gt;
		&lt;ns1:assignment role=&quot;FP&quot;&gt;
			&lt;ns1:trip name=&quot;7771&quot; /&gt;
		&lt;/ns1:assignment&gt;
	&lt;/ns1:roster&gt;
&lt;/ns1:setRostersRequest&gt;

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; ?&gt;
&lt;ns1:setRostersRequest created=&quot;2009-12-01T00:00:00&quot;
	source=&quot;ROSTER&quot; version=&quot;2.1&quot;
	xmlns:ns1=&quot;http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com&quot;&gt;
	&lt;ns1:roster crewId=&quot;04873&quot; end=&quot;2009-12-01T00:00:00&quot; start=&quot;2009-11-10T00:00:00&quot;&gt;
		&lt;ns1:assignment role=&quot;FC&quot; &gt;
			&lt;ns1:trip name=&quot;7771&quot; /&gt;
		&lt;/ns1:assignment&gt;
	&lt;/ns1:roster&gt;
&lt;/ns1:setRostersRequest&gt;

Gantt view result:

in msg   |--------|===asmt1====|----------|===asmt2===|---------|
lock              |===asmt1====|
in msg          |-------------------------|===asmt2===|---------|
db after  --------|===asmt1====|----------|===asmt2===|------------

### 15.2.3. UC: Carry in/out assignments in message

Actor: An external system that sends messages containing only crew trip assignments.

Any assignment in message that start outside the update window are considered faulty and will give an error.

In the example below, both the messages contains assignments that are partly outside the update window.
The first one starts outside the update window, this is an error so nothing will be committed to db.
The second one starts in, and ends outside the update window, this is ok so it will be committed to db.

In messages:

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; ?&gt;
&lt;ns1:setRostersRequest created=&quot;2009-12-01T00:00:00&quot;
	source=&quot;ROSTER&quot; version=&quot;2.1&quot;
	xmlns:ns1=&quot;http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com&quot;&gt;
	&lt;ns1:roster crewId=&quot;04873&quot; end=&quot;2009-11-29T11:00:00&quot; start=&quot;2009-11-27T00:00:00&quot;&gt;
		&lt;ns1:assignment role=&quot;FP&quot;&gt;
			&lt;ns1:trip name=&quot;51470&quot; /&gt;
		&lt;/ns1:assignment&gt;
	&lt;/ns1:roster&gt;
&lt;/ns1:setRostersRequest&gt;

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; ?&gt;
&lt;ns1:setRostersRequest created=&quot;2009-12-01T00:00:00&quot;
	source=&quot;ROSTER&quot; version=&quot;2.1&quot;
	xmlns:ns1=&quot;http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com&quot;&gt;
	&lt;ns1:roster crewId=&quot;04873&quot; end=&quot;2009-11-29T11:00:00&quot; start=&quot;2009-11-27T00:00:00&quot;&gt;
		&lt;ns1:assignment role=&quot;FP&quot;&gt;
			&lt;ns1:trip name=&quot;7771&quot; /&gt;
		&lt;/ns1:assignment&gt;
	&lt;/ns1:roster&gt;
&lt;/ns1:setRostersRequest&gt;

Gantt view result:

upd window          |--------------------------------|
in msg     |=======asmt1=======|
in msg                                    |=======asmt2=======|
db after            |---------------------|=======asmt2=======|

### 15.2.4. UC: Update of existing assignments carry in/out

Actor: An external system that sends messages containing only crew trip assignments.

Any existing assignments in the db that themselves stick out of, i.e. start in, the update period are consider to be targets for update.

In the example below we have two assignments, in the db, that are partly inside the update period,
but only the one starting inside will be considered for update.
As a result the asmt starting in the update period will be deleted.

In messages:

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; ?&gt;
&lt;ns1:setRostersRequest created=&quot;2009-12-01T00:00:00&quot;
	source=&quot;ROSTER&quot; version=&quot;2.1&quot;
	xmlns:ns1=&quot;http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com&quot;&gt;
	&lt;ns1:roster crewId=&quot;04873&quot; end=&quot;2009-12-01T00:00:00&quot; start=&quot;2009-11-01T00:00:00&quot;&gt;
		&lt;ns1:assignment role=&quot;FP&quot; &gt;
			&lt;ns1:trip name=&quot;39410&quot; /&gt;
		&lt;/ns1:assignment&gt;
		&lt;ns1:assignment role=&quot;FP&quot; &gt;
			&lt;ns1:trip name=&quot;35481&quot; /&gt;
		&lt;/ns1:assignment&gt;
	&lt;/ns1:roster&gt;
&lt;/ns1:setRostersRequest&gt;

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; ?&gt;
&lt;ns1:setRostersRequest created=&quot;2009-12-01T00:00:00&quot;
	source=&quot;ROSTER&quot; version=&quot;2.1&quot;
	xmlns:ns1=&quot;http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com&quot;&gt;
	&lt;ns1:roster crewId=&quot;04873&quot; end=&quot;2009-11-21T00:00:00&quot; start=&quot;2009-11-15T00:00:00&quot;&gt;
		&lt;ns1:assignment role=&quot;FP&quot;&gt;
			&lt;ns1:trip name=&quot;16117&quot; /&gt;
		&lt;/ns1:assignment&gt;
	&lt;/ns1:roster&gt;
&lt;/ns1:setRostersRequest&gt;

prereq  ---|====trip1====|--------------|===trip2===|----
prereq  ---|====asmt1====|--------------|===asmt2===|----

### 15.2.5. UC: Update separation in 2 layers for separate activities.

Actor: An external system that sends messages containing only crew trip or personal activity assignments.This is considered to be in the layer 1.

Actor: A second external system that sends messages containing only crew ground task assignments.This is considered to be in the layer 2.

The first message sends assignments that will be committed to db.
The second message has an update period that covers the previous assignment,
but they are in layer 1 so they are ignored, since the message is layer 2.
So, the result is that asmt1 and asmt2 are left in the db and the asmt3 is added.

In messages:

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; ?&gt;
&lt;ns1:setRostersRequest created=&quot;2009-12-01T00:00:00&quot;
	source=&quot;ROSTER&quot; version=&quot;2.1&quot;
	xmlns:ns1=&quot;http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com&quot;&gt;
	&lt;ns1:roster crewId=&quot;04873&quot; end=&quot;2009-12-28T00:00:00&quot; start=&quot;2009-10-28T00:00:00&quot;&gt;
		&lt;ns1:assignment role=&quot;FP&quot; &gt;
			&lt;ns1:trip name=&quot;7771&quot; /&gt;
		&lt;/ns1:assignment&gt;
		&lt;ns1:assignment&gt;
			&lt;ns1:task activityType=&quot;VY12&quot; endStation=&quot;CPH&quot;
				endTime=&quot;2009-12-05T00:00:00&quot; startStation=&quot;CPH&quot; startTime=&quot;2009-12-04T00:00:00&quot; /&gt;
		&lt;/ns1:assignment&gt;
	&lt;/ns1:roster&gt;
&lt;/ns1:setRostersRequest&gt;

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; ?&gt;
&lt;ns1:setRostersRequest created=&quot;2009-12-01T00:00:00&quot;
	source=&quot;TRAINING&quot; version=&quot;2.1&quot;
	xmlns:ns1=&quot;http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com&quot;&gt;
	&lt;ns1:roster crewId=&quot;04873&quot; end=&quot;2009-12-10T00:00:00&quot; start=&quot;2009-11-20T00:00:00&quot;&gt;
		&lt;ns1:assignment role=&quot;FP&quot;&gt;
			&lt;ns1:task activityType=&quot;E&quot; endStation=&quot;CPH&quot; endTime=&quot;2009-12-02T09:00:00&quot;

### 15.2.6. UC: Updates in each of 2 layers while keeping separation.

Actor: An external system that sends messages containing only crew trip or personal activity assignments.This is considered to be in the layer 1.

Actor: A second external system that sends messages containing only crew ground task assignments.This is considered to be in the layer 2.

The first message send layer 1 assignments that will be committed to db.
The second message has an update period that covers the previous assignment,
and add two ground assignments.
This results is all assignments committed to the db since they are separate layers.

Now two new messages are sent in, one for each layer, with updates to the assignments.
The result is that the updates delete assignments for their layer only,
leaving two modified assignments in the db.

In messages:

		&lt;ns1:assignment role=&quot;FP&quot; &gt;
			&lt;ns1:trip name=&quot;7771&quot; /&gt;
		&lt;/ns1:assignment&gt;
		&lt;ns1:assignment&gt;
			&lt;ns1:task activityType=&quot;VY12&quot; endStation=&quot;CPH&quot;
				endTime=&quot;2009-12-05T00:00:00&quot; startStation=&quot;CPH&quot; startTime=&quot;2009-12-04T00:00:00&quot; /&gt;
		&lt;/ns1:assignment&gt;
	&lt;/ns1:roster&gt;
&lt;/ns1:setRostersRequest&gt;

in layer 1 |------------------------------------|===pact=asmt2===|--------|
in layer 2    |-------------|=grnd=asmt3=|--------------------------------|
db after  ------------------|=grnd=asmt3=|------|===pact=asmt2===|-------

# 16. Crew Roster Output

This chapter describes the interfaces that can be used to get roster information from JCMS.
Roster information is normally sent when explicitly requested by an external user or system
(request/response pattern). The information can also be sent spontaneously by JCMS, either on changes or
on a scheduled basis (publish/subscribe pattern). The latter requires however a service trigger to be
configured inside JCMS. Such triggers are not provided out of the box by the standard interface but must
be added as part of an implementation project. In addition, it is also possible, as a part of
implementation project customization, to add mechanisms to enable e.g. a Tracking user to manually request
roster information to be sent out to predefined destinations.

The current version of this interface is 5.
Link to RosterStateOutput_5.xsd
Link to RosterStateOutput_5.wsdl
Link to RosterStateOutput_5_schema.json
Link to RosterStateOutput_5_openapi.json

Previous versions of this interface
Link to RosterState_4.xsd (version 4)
Link to RosterStateSoap_4.wsdl (version 4)
Link to RosterState_2_0.xsd (version 2.0)
Link to RosterStateSoap_2_0.wsdl (version 2.0)

## 16.1. Interface capabilities

The interface supports the following operations:

pingPings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).

getRostersIt allows to request all rosters for a group of crew selected by crew category or base.
If neither category nor base is specified, then rosters of all crew are returned.
It is also possible to specify both category and base in which case the interface returns rosters of
all crew matching both the specified category and base.

getRostersByCrewidIt allows to request rosters for a list of crew members, identified by
their crew id (alias). At least one crew id must be specified in the request.

### 16.1.1. Scope of returned roster state

In both request types it is required to specify a request period. The interface responds with the state of
all matching rosters for the requested time period. Note that roster elements, with some basic crew
attributes, are included for all matching crew members, even if they don’t have any assignments within the
requested period.

All activities (trips or personal tasks) overlapping the
requested time period are included in the response, i.e. the trip or task must start before the end of the requested period
and end after the start of the requested period. The task and trip start/end times must be defined by specific
Rave variables, see Rave definitions.

Assigned trips are always included in their entirety such that also duties and/or activities outside the
requested period are included as long as some piece of the trip is inside the period. In order to
guarantee that trips are always complete, while still maintaining good operating performance, the system
has a built-in assumption about maximum trip length. This is by default set to 10 days, but can be
customized if needed.

### 16.1.2. Content of the roster state

The following types of activities, and any combination of them, are included:

Trip, including the following activities:

- Flight Leg (including return-to-ramp and wait-at-gate events)
- Air Transport
- Ground Task
- Ground Transport

- Ground Task
- Ground Transport
- Crew Activity (e.g. vacation, sickness…)

In accordance with the interface schema, the crew complement of each trip included in the roster state
must contain at least one role. If however crew for some reason would be assigned to a trip with
undefined or empty crew complement, then the interface will output a crew complement item with the
role to which crew is currently assigned, and with the crew count set to 1.

In roster response, the start time is aligned with the start time of the first activity if
it is lower than the period start time in the request.
The end time is however not aligned with the end time of the last activity if it is greater than
the period end time in the request, as it is valid to have carry out activities.

Note that for Air Transports normally very limited information is available. Although represented
by the same data type as normal Flight Legs in the interface schema, some of the fields like e.g.
effectiveEndStation, estimatedStartTime and actualStartTime are never included for Air Transports.

Export of annotations is limited to annotations that are intended to be shared with crew members, such annotations
have an annotation code that is internally tagged with the attribute ‘is_public’ set to True.

All Ground Tasks outside trips are technically “wrapped” inside a trip internally in JCMS. However, in the
roster state messages produced by this interface they are represented as plain tasks without the wrapper
trip. Conversely, a Ground Task that has explicitly been wrapped in a real trip is represented as a trip
on the roster and it contains the Ground Task as a task element. The system distinguishes wrapper trips from
real trips by using a special trip category reserved exclusively for internal usage.

### 16.1.3. Supported protocols

The interface supports requests using both plain XML and SOAP. The SOAP service is primarily intended for
supporting external WEB services. For use with internal triggers the plain XML form of the service is
normally used.

### 16.1.4. Rave definitions

The following Rave variables are defined in the CARMSYS and used by the Crew Roster Output standard interface:

interfaces_core.%roster_out_trip_start_utc%: Defines the start time of a trip or task, used for output of
trip report time and for identifying whether the trip or task is in the requested period or not.

interfaces_core.%roster_out_trip_end_utc%: Defines the end time of a trip or task, used for output of
trip release time and for identifying whether the trip or task is in the requested period or not.

interfaces_core.%crew_trip_training_tags%: Defines the trip-level crew_asmt_trng_tag.
It is used to populate &lt;assignedTrainingTag&gt; of the trip. Multiple tags should be concatenated into a single string
separated by “,”. Empty string should be returned if no tag is found. If the Rave variable is not configured in CARMUSR,
the interface will fall back to use ARA API which only works for LIVE dataset.

interfaces_core.%crew_trip_roster_tags%: Defines the trip-level roster_tag.
It is used to populate &lt;rosterTag&gt; of the trip. Multiple tags should be concatenated into a single string
separated by “,”. Empty string should be returned if no tag is found. If the Rave variable is not configured in CARMUSR,
the interface will fall back to use ARA API which only works for LIVE dataset.

- interfaces_core.%roster_out_leg_pred_alertness%: Defines the predicted crew alertness for flight leg.

The business logic behind these Rave variables need to be implemented in a CARMUSR to comply with the
expected behavior of each individual airline.

### 16.1.5. Error handling

The interface conforms to the same error handling strategy as most interfaces, i.e. to reject the message
if it cannot be entirely and completely processed. Concretely for the Roster State Outbound interface it
means that if it fails to generate roster for any of the crew members matching the request, it will respond
with an error message.

# 17. Flight Events

This chapter describes the standard interface for publishing flight information to external systems when flight related events occur in JCMS.
The interface publish event messages for updates of scheduled flights, before day of operation, as well as aircraft movements,
diversions, return-to-ramp events etc. during day of operation.
Event messages are published by the interface when flight information is updated in the database.

One aspect of external systems, receiving the published event messages, is that they usually expect different type of event messages for the same event occurring in JCMS.
For example, some systems might expect IATA messages while others expects messages on xml or other format.
Another aspect of the receiving systems is that they are interested in different subsets of flight events occurring in JCMS. For example, some systems might
only expect messages for changes of scheduled flights when others expects messages for only operational flights.

The interface handles these two aspects, message format and events of interest, by supporting a concept of receivers,
see Message Receivers.
Multiple receivers can be configured in the Flight Events interface where each receiver is associated with a specific message format, events of interest and other options.

The interface generates event messages for each receiver when flight events occur in JCMS.
A receiver should rather be seen as a “logical receiver”, and is not necessarily the same as an external system receiving the event messages since
there might be several external systems receiving same event messages for one and the same receiver.

Default receivers:

- Native (FlightInput version 5)
- IATA (SSM, ASM, MVT, DIV)

The following table provides an overview of message types published by this interface for different types of events.

** For onward flight changes, ASM ADM is only sent for flights as long as they don’t have an aircraft assigned.

** ASM NEW/EQT/CON/RPL will also be sent when neither PRBD nor ACV exists, even though the SSIM requires that (from March 2012) at least one ofthem need to be included. This applies to SSM EQT/CON as well.

** MVT AA and MVT EA are also generated when estimated/actual arrival times are updated for return-to-ramp or return-to-land events.Such MVT messages contains the departure airport as Airport of Movement and are only generated when when times of the most recent
return event are updated, in case multiple returns has occurred for same flight leg.

** If a Next Information time is set or updated, a separate MVT ED message is published only containing the changed Next Information time.

On certain combinations of events, only one of the message types are generated. The following applies:

If any of the events triggering an ASM RPL message occurs, and at the same time the flight is rescheduled, rerouted, has a change
in tail assignment or onward flight information, then the TIM, RRT, EQT and ADM messages are suppressed and only the RPL message is generated.

If the scheduled arrival station is updated and at the same time the flight is rescheduled, has a change in tail assignment or onward
flight information, then the TIM, EQT and ADM messages are suppressed and only the RRT message is generated.

## 17.1. Configuring message receivers

It’s possible to configure the receivers this interface should use when sending event messages by updating the default SMOG service-mapping
and call the generator.add_receiver method.

&lt;service-mapping xmlns=&quot;http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2&quot; target=&quot;air2_mave2&quot; language=&quot;Python&quot;&gt;
  &lt;include href=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/mapping_client.xml&quot;/&gt;

  &lt;output-mapping struct=&quot;flight_input.FlightsUpdateMsg&quot;&gt;
    &lt;call name=&quot;add_receiver_iata_asm_local&quot; expr=&quot;generator.add_receiver(&#39;from.ioservice.FlightInput_5_event.iata_local&#39;, iata.IATAFormatterASM(service_logger, local_time=True))&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;call name=&quot;add_receiver_iata_ssm&quot; expr=&quot;generator.add_receiver(&#39;from.ioservice.FlightInput_5_event.iata&#39;, iata.IATAFormatterSSM(service_logger))&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;call name=&quot;add_receiver_iata_asm&quot; expr=&quot;generator.add_receiver(&#39;from.ioservice.FlightInput_5_event.iata&#39;, iata.IATAFormatterASM(service_logger, only_send_asm_if_adhoc=True))&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;call name=&quot;add_receiver_iata_mvt&quot; expr=&quot;generator.add_receiver(&#39;from.ioservice.FlightInput_5_event.iata&#39;, iata.IATAFormatterMVT(service_logger))&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/output-mapping&gt;
&lt;/service-mapping&gt;

The generator.add_receiver method registers a new a receiver for messages on a specific format.
Each receiver is associated with a specific message queue and a formatter that determines the format
and formatting options of the generated messages for that receiver.

The example above shows how the formatter IATAFormatterASM is added twice, for different message queues with different formatting options.
The second one of them is configured to only send ASM messages for flights that are in Ad-hoc state. As a complement, there is also
a receiver with IATAFormatterSSM that will send SSM messages for non Ad-hoc flights. Finally there is a receiver set up with the
IATAFormatterMVT formatter.
The example also shows that all these three mentioned receivers are added with the same message queue, specifying that both SSM, ASM and MVT messages
will be sent to same message queue.

### 17.1.1. Native formatter

This formatter generates messages on the native SMOG protocol format of the FlightInput service (i.e. plainxml, soap, plainjson etc.).

Class

std_interfaces.common.NativeProtocolFormatter

Options

Parameter

Type

Description

17.1.1.1. Event annotations
The Native formatter produces annotations to indicate source of latest recorded estimated times for a flight leg, and whether the value
was actually changed or not in the latest change set.

The annotation text is composed of four parts: estimatedTimes:&lt;estimated time&gt;:&lt;source&gt;:&lt;change indicator&gt;

- &lt;estimated time&gt; indicates the estimated time (offBlock, takeoffTime, landingTime or inBlock).
&lt;source&gt; is the name of the writer of the latest value. The source must be pre-configured in entity data_source in the database.
If the writing application has not registered the data source or if the data source is missing in entity data_source, then “unknown” is output.

- change indicator indicates “change” if the value was changed with the latest change set or “nochange” if the value existed already.

Below are examples of annotations in xml format:

&lt;annotation code=&quot;X_SOC&quot;&gt;
  &lt;text&gt;estimatedTimes:offBlock:unknown:nochange&lt;/text&gt;
&lt;/annotation&gt;
&lt;annotation code=&quot;X_SOC&quot;&gt;
  &lt;text&gt;estimatedTimes:takeoffTime:unknown:nochange&lt;/text&gt;
&lt;/annotation&gt;
&lt;annotation code=&quot;X_SOC&quot;&gt;
  &lt;text&gt;estimatedTimes:landingTime:MVT:change&lt;/text&gt;
&lt;/annotation&gt;
&lt;annotation code=&quot;X_SOC&quot;&gt;
  &lt;text&gt;estimatedTimes:inBlock:MVT:nochange&lt;/text&gt;
&lt;/annotation&gt;

Note that the Flight Events interface does not support ordinary flight annotations.

### 17.1.2. IATA ASM formatter

This formatter produces IATA Ad Hoc Schedules Messages (ASM) for relevant flight updates.

Formatted ASM messages does not contain the following information:

- DEI 1 - Joint Operation Airline Designators
- DEI 2 - Operating Airline Disclosure - Code Share
- DEI 9 - Operating Airline Disclosure - Shared Airline or Wet Lease Designation
- Creator Reference
- Secondary Action
- Change Reason, except for ASM CNL where cancellation codes are provided as Change Reason.
- Meal Service Note

Class std_interfaces.iata.formatters.IATAFormatterASM

Options

Parameter

Type

Description

windows_line_endings

bool

If True, ASM messages are produced with ‘\r\n’ line endings
instead of ‘\n’. Default False.

local_time

bool

If True, all times in produced ASM messages are in local time.
Default False (= all times in UTC).

new_instead_of_rin

bool

If True, ASM/NEW messages are produced in place of ASM/RIN when a leg
is reinstated. Default False.

new_cnl_instead_of_flt

bool

If True, an ASM/NEW followed by an ASM/CNL message is produced in
place of ASM/FLT when a flight or sub-segment of a flight is renamed.
If legs already exist with the new flight identifier, then ASM/RPL is
produced instead of ASM/NEW. Default False.

rpl_instead_of_rrt

bool

If True, ASM/RPL messages are produced in place of ASM/RRT when the
scheduled arrival station is updated. Default False.

rpl_instead_of_adm

bool

If True, ASM/RPL messages are produced in place of ASM/ADM when code
share or terminal information is updated. Default False.

suppress_eqt_if_cancelled

bool

If True, ASM/EQT messages are not produced for flight being cancelled.
Default True.

suppress_con_if_cancelled

bool

If True, ASM/CON messages are not produced for flight being cancelled.
Default True.

only_send_asm_if_adhoc

bool

If True, ASM messages are only generated for flights that are in Adhoc
state, i.e. whose flight identifier is recorded in table adhoc_flight.
Default False.

### 17.1.3. IATA SSM formatter

This formatter produces IATA Standard Schedules Messages (SSM) for selected flight updates.

The SSM formatter currently only supports EQT and CON message sub-types. Messages are always generated per
flight instance. E.g. if the planned aircraft type is changed for all daily flights with a certain flight number
during one week, then one message will be generated for each weekday. Likewise if e.g. if the same change applies
to several flight numbers on a particular day, one message per flight number will be generated. By default,
SSM messages are only generated for flights that are not in Ad-hoc state.

Formatted SSM messages does not contain the following information:

- DEI 1 - Joint Operation Airline Designators
- DEI 2 - Operating Airline Disclosure - Code Share
- DEI 9 - Operating Airline Disclosure - Shared Airline or Wet Lease Designation
- Creator Reference
- Secondary Action
- Change Reason, except for ASM CNL where cancellation codes are provided as Change Reason.
- DEI 7 - Meal Service Note

Class std_interfaces.iata.formatters.IATAFormatterASM

Options

Parameter

Type

Description

windows_line_endings

bool

If True, ASM messages are produced with ‘\r\n’ line endings
instead of ‘\n’. Default False.

local_time

bool

If True, all times in produced ASM messages are in local time.
Default False (= all times in UTC).

suppress_eqt_if_cancelled

bool

If True, ASM/EQT messages are not produced for flight being cancelled.
Default True.

suppress_con_if_cancelled

bool

If True, ASM/CON messages are not produced for flight being cancelled.
Default True.

send_ssm_if_adhoc

bool

If True, SSM messages are generated even if the flight is in Adhoc
state, i.e. if the flight identifier is recorded in table adhoc_flight.
Default False.

### 17.1.4. IATA MVT/DIV formatter

This formatter produces IATA Aircraft Movement (MVT) and Aircraft Diversion (DIV) messages for relevant flight updates.

Formatted MVT messages does not contain the following information:

- DEI 8.1, Reclearance Information
- DEI 8.5, Crew Report Time
- DEI 8.6, Movement After Pushback
- DEI 8.8, Take Off Fuel
- DEI 8.9, Take Off Weight
- DEI 8.10, Zero Fuel Weight
- DEI 8.11, Category of Operation
- DEI 11, Next information

MVT messages of any subtype are generated even if the aircraft registration of the flight leg is not known by JCMS,
something which is a deviation from IATA rules in Airport Manual AHM780. In these cases, ‘XXXXX’ is output in place
of the aircraft registration.

Formatted DIV messages does not contain the following information:
* DEI 6, Reason for Diversion

Class std_interfaces.iata.formatters.IATAFormatterMVT

Options

Parameter

Type

Description

windows_line_endings

bool

If True, MVT and DIV messages are produced with ‘\r\n’ line endings
instead of ‘\n’. Default False.

local_time

bool

If True, all times in produced MVT and DIV messages are in local
time. Also the Flight Leg Date (FLD) is based on local time.
In messages generated based on local time, the SI field contains
“Time mode: LT”.
Default False (= all times in UTC).

### 17.1.5. Custom formatter

It’s possible to configure new message formatters by adding a subclass of the MessageFormatter to the configuration layer and implementing
the format method.

from std_interfaces.common import MessageFormatter

class MyMessageFormatter(MessageFormatter):
    &quot;&quot;&quot;
    Formatter generating messages containing the flight number of updated flights.
    &quot;&quot;&quot;

    def format(self, payload, headers):
        &quot;&quot;&quot;
        @param payload: Object containing updated flight data.
        @type payload:  ioservice_impl.air2_mave2.FlightInput_5_client.FlightsUpdateMsg
        @param headers: Dictionary of headers passed with the incoming request message
        @type headers:  dict
        @return:        Tuple of two lists of equal length, one with output messages content and one with message header attributes
        @rtype:         (list of string, list of dict)
        &quot;&quot;&quot;
        contents = list()
        headers = list()
        for action in payload.action:
              contents.append(str(action.setFlight.flightNumber))
              headers.append(dict())
        return contents, headers

Receivers can be configured for messages generated by the custom formatter by passing instances of it to the generator.add_receiver method as described in Configuring message receivers.

## 17.3. IOService builder configuration

Service FlightInput_5_event

&lt;ioservice name=&quot;FlightInput_5_event&quot; pattern=&quot;trigger&quot; handler_module=&quot;std_interfaces.triggers.flight_events&quot;&gt;
  &lt;description&gt;Trigger for flight changes.&lt;/description&gt;
  &lt;subscription&gt;
    &lt;filter name=&quot;all&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;/subscription&gt;
  &lt;delta-service name=&quot;FlightInput&quot; version=&quot;5&quot; protocol=&quot;plainxml&quot;&gt;

# 18. Flight Input

This chapter describes the standard Flight Input interface that can be used for updating the information about flights stored in JCMS. It supports
updating and maintaining the flight schedule before day of operation as well as capturing aircraft movements, diversions, return-to-ramp
events etc. during day of operation. Before this interface was introduced, schedule changes were handled by the Flight Based Schedule Input interface
and day-of-operation changes were handled by the Operational Flight Input interfaces. The new Flight Input interface replaces both these interfaces.
Note that this interface does not replace the Flight Schedule State interface, which is used for initial creation of flights from time tables.

When it comes to changes short before and during operation there will usually be frequent updates to the flight information, capturing the
estimated or actual movements of the aircraft or any disturbances to the planned flow. The picture of clearly identified planned legs is no longer
valid since all atomic events that affect the aircraft, crew and passengers must be taken care of. JCMS has a quite pragmatic view on the
leg entities that focuses on the actual events and not on the question which movements or events belong to “the same official leg”. Groupings of
events into legs or flights are only relevant to determine the initial assignment of potential new items to resources - e.g. a return to ramp event
is assigned to the same aircraft and crew as the leg that was attempted. To change crew or equipment before the actual take off of the “main leg” is
then an explicit operational decision. The interface reflects the pragmatic view of leg identity by using the scheduled departure as optional part
of the key (to avoid issues with uniqueness in case of re-routing back to departure airport) and formulating some operations in term of “atoms” rather
than legs.

In general the systems providing flight information are regarded master relative to JCMS and the interface is implemented as publish/subscribe.

The current version of this interface is 5.
Link to FlightInput_5.xsd
Link to FlightInput_5.wsdl
Link to FlightInput_5_schema.json
Link to FlightInput_5_openapi.json

Previous versions of this interface
Link to FlightInput_1_0.xsd

## 18.1. Interface capabilities

Available operations are:

pingPings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).

updateFlightsCreate or update the information for the provided flights. May be used for updating schedule as well as operational flight information (one-way request without any response message).

updateFlightsWithAckCreate or update the information for the provided flights. May be used for updating schedule as well as operational flight information (with acknowledge response on successful update).

getFlights (deprecated - please use service FlightState instead Flight State)Get complete flight information as a state for all flights within a given period.

These operations can be used in batch (or periodic) mode to provide sets of updates at once or in online mode
to immediately publish schedule changes when they occur (similar to SSM messages).
In online mode it must be considered that the scope of messages that occur close to each other might overlap;
so normally it is assumed that ordering per flight is relevant when using this interface in online mode (but not in batch mode).
An ‘updateFlights’ request message may contain multiple actions on the same flight as well as on several different flights. All actions
within a message are applied in the order they appear in the xml and they are all committed to the data model together in one single
transaction.

The interface does not normally check that information arrives in the order that would be expected during normal operation.
It is for example OK to send an actual landing time even though no take off time is present (yet) and the actual departure is accepted
even though a landing is already present. This allows the source system to also send corrected or lacking information later,
e.g. based on manual flight log handling. Any constraints that are implemented are described together with the affected use cases, e.g. for
return to ramp and rescheduling.

Normally, only flights (and legs) that match the keys listed in a message are manipulated by this interface. However, in accordance with the
general semantics of the Standard Interfaces described in Naming Conventions, it is possible to provide flight information
as a complete “state” for creating new flights or replacing existing ones. When replacing an existing flight (i.e. using ‘replaceFlight’ or
‘putFlight’ actions), any leg that exists previously in the data model, but don’t exist in the new provided flight “state”, is marked as
deleted (a state represented internally as implicitly cancelled). The interface can of course also be used for explicitly canceling specific flights or individual legs by means of the
‘cancelFlight’ and ‘cancelLeg’ elements respectively.

The interface takes care of already existing assignments of flight legs when changes to the flights are coming in.
Existing assignments are kept even when flights are renamed, and new legs (and operational events) in existing flights are assigned
to the same crew and trips as the original legs.
If a multi-leg flight contained a change of crew, then the system will assume that the change shall happen at the same station as planned
if that station is still touched.

## 18.2. Supported time modes

The interface supports both UTC and Local Time modes. Each incoming message has a flag ‘timeModeIsUTC’ indicating whether or not
times are specified in the UTC time zone. Internally in JCMS  all times are stored in the UTC time zone, so any Local times are
converted to UTC by the interface before storing them in JCMS.
There are two aspects of this time conversion that need further clarification:
One is the handling of “day of origin” as part of the flight key.
IATA standard prescribes it to be the UTC day of departure of the first leg; that is not strictly required by JCMS.
The value is never interpreted as time-zoned, it is used purely for identification purpose.
As long as all connected systems use the same date to identify the flight it will work, no time-zone conversion for 0:00 UTC is needed.
The other aspect is with the scheduled departure time if a sending system is working completely local time based.
Since JCMS has its own storage of the time-zone information to be able to fix the data without help from external vendors
there is a risk that the local time offset that the external system uses is not the same as what JCMS has.
That would lead to the fact that the transferred times do not match in local time in reality.
To be able to detect that situation the interface contain optional fields for time-zone offsets for scheduled departure and arrival times.
It is recommended to set these values if the data is transferred from a local-time based system to JCMS.
If the values are provided and if they differ from the values that JCMS has for the same airport at the same UTC time,
then this is regarded as an error and the data is not stored to the database.

## 18.3. Identification of flights and legs

In JCMS a dated flight is the set of all atoms that share the same IATA flight key (dateOfOrigin, carrier, flightNumber, suffix).
A single leg is the set of atoms that share the extended IATA leg key
(dateOfOrigin, carrier, flightNumber, suffix, startStation, endStation, scheduledStartTime, scheduledEndTime, assignedAircraft).
Within each leg the leg_atom_number is expected to be unique and the number 0 identifies the “main atom” - performing the actual flight segment.
Other atoms can be Return to Ramp events.
During the scheduling phase we do not expect to see any atoms with non-zero atom number.
When looking up a leg for processing the interface always first identifies all atoms of the flight, then filters them with the
matching properties given in the leg element. Although none of the matching properties are strictly mandatory, both stations and assignedAircraft (if provided)
must be matched identical. Also scheduledStartTime and scheduledEndTime are optional.
If provided, they are used for identification as well but there is an accepted deviation for the provided times to allow for robustness in the
face of rescheduling. Schedule times are however only used for matching in case there are more than one main atom with matching startStation and
endStation. The accepted deviation is not applicable for the ‘addLeg’ action, as it is assumed that if the source system issues an ‘addLeg’
action, the leg should be added, unless there already exist a leg, with the exact same scheduled times. The same logic applies when an existing
flight is replaced by means of issuing ‘replaceFlight’ actions. With the ‘putFlight’ action however, the ‘accepted deviation’ approach is applied
and furthermore the schedule times of the matched leg are updated in accordance with the provided scheduledStartTime/scheduledEndTime.
In case a unique best match cannot be identified based on the provided matching properties, then the leg with the most recent
scheduledStartTime is selected. The reasoning behind that is for operational flight update (MVT/MVA) messages to address the correct leg e.g. in
case of return from airborne scenarios, where a new leg may have been scheduled.

## 18.4. Rescheduling

For a rescheduling message the original stations must be specified, as a minimum, in order to identify the affected leg.
If a source system is not able to provide these the matching algorithm can be customized to cater for this, for example only using the IATA key.

When rescheduling in the operational time frame, the flag ‘isOperational’ should be specified in order for JCMS to mark the flight leg as
rescheduled in JCMS. Legs that get updated departure or arrival stations/times during the scheduling phase are not marked as rescheduled.
If scheduled departure/arrival times are updated, any existing aircraft assignment times are updated too, to reflect the new
schedule times of the leg.

## 18.5. Renaming flights

When a flight is renamed, the new flight identifier of the renamed leg(s) must not be in conflict with an already existing operating leg with the
same flight identifier.

## 18.6. Adhoc flight changes

In the context of IATA standard flight messages, an Adhoc Schedule Message (ASM) cannot be modified by a subsequent Standard Schedule Message (SSM)
unless an explicit ASM withdrawal indicator is provided. Furthermore IATA messages provide the possibility to re-instate the original schedule
of a flight, hence accepting any subsequent SSM messages updating that flight without the need to provide the ASM withdrawal indicator.
The standard Flight Input interface supports these mechanisms by means of three flags that may be specified on each flight action in a request message:

- isAdhoc: Indicates that the action is an adhoc change to the flight. Sets the internal adhoc indicator for the flight in the data model. Default false.
isAdhocOverride: Indicates that the action should override any previous adhoc change to the flight.
This flag does not however reset the internal adhoc indicator in the data model. Default false.

isAdhocReset: Resets the adhoc indicator for the flight in the data model. It has precedence over isAhoc if both of them are true.
Any updates on the flight are carried out according to the content of the message, in addition to resetting the adhoc indicator. Default false.

Note that the blocking of a Flight Input message due to a preceding adhoc change is part of the normal functionality and therefore not handled as an error.

## 18.7. Adjustment of Flight Times

### 18.7.1. Adjustment of Arrival Times

If the message contains no estimated or actual departure times, the estimated and actual landing and in-block times will be checked and
adjusted if necessary. If the landing or in-block times are earlier than the best known start time of the leg, they will be increased
in steps of 24 hours until they are later than the start time. This is because some sources are known to have insufficient information
to be able to set the date part of arrival times correctly. This will be the case for the following IATA movement messages, as specified
in the IATA Airport Handling Manual, sections AHM 780 and AHM 781:

- DIV
The following MVA/MVT message subtypes:

- Return from Airborne
- Revised Estimated Time of Arrival

### 18.7.2. Calculation of estimated times

If a new actual or estimated time is provided, the interface derives/adjusts all subsequent estimated times.
The same calculation is applied regardless if times are provided from ACARS/ARINC or IATA MVT messages. Note that
for native format messages this feature is switched off by default.
Calculation of an estimated time does not take place if a subsequent estimated time is provided in the message.
Calculation of an estimated time does not take place if a corresponding or subsequent actual time exists or is
provided in the message.

Estimated times are calculated slightly differently depending on whether or not a value already exists in the model:

If an estimated time doesn’t exist, the value is derived based on the best known preceding time and the nominal
difference between these times:

If an estimated time exists, the value is adjusted based on the delta of provided preceding time:

In the native format, calculation of estimated times is switched off by default. It can be switched on  on a per
message basis by setting attribute enableEstimatedTimeCalculation on *Flight element of the message.

### 18.7.3. Resetting of Internal times

Internal times of a leg is no longer needed when actual times become available.
Thus, the interface removes any Internal times when receiving actual times for a leg.

### 18.7.4. Resetting of Next Information time

Upon receiving of an actual off-block time, any Next Information time of the flight leg is cleared.

## 18.8. Aircraft flight assignment locks

The interface respects “tail locks” that may be active for flight legs. As long as a “tail lock” exists for a flight leg, the interface
will suppress any instruction from incoming messages to assign, reassign or deassign the aircraft of the flight leg. If a message contains
other information (in addition to the tail assignment), that information will however be processed as normal.

## 18.9. Rave definitions

The following Rave variables are defined in the CARMSYS and used by the Flight Input standard interface:

- interfaces_core.%default_taxi_out_time%: Defines default taxi time at departure airport
- interfaces_core.%default_taxi_in_time%: Defines default taxi time at arrival airport

The business logic behind these Rave variables need to be implemented in a CARMUSR to comply with the
expected behavior of each individual airline.

## 18.10. Error Handling

The interface conforms to the same error handling strategy as most standard interfaces, i.e. to reject a request message if it cannot be
entirely and completely processed. If processing of any flight action fails for whatever reason, an error message is generated and the request is discarded
in its entirety. The following errors can occur when processing a request:
