## 18.11. Using IATA flight messages

This interface supports receiving IATA flight messages of types SSM, ASM, MVT/MVA and DIV. IATA messages are automatically converted into an xml equivalent message
before being handled by the interface.
The usage of airline name in plain text (DEI 113/114/115) with letter “X” for aircraft owner/cabin crew employer/cockpit crew employer is not supported.
A letter “X” as airline identifier in DEI 2/3/4 is ignored.

### 18.11.1. Supported message sub-types

The following message sub-types are supported:

SSM

ASM

MVT/MVA

DIV

TIM

TIM

AD (Departure message)

DIV

NEW*

NEW

AA (Arrival message)

RPL*

RPL**

ED (Delay message)

CNL*

CNL

AD/EO (Delayed take-off message)

EQT

EQT

AD/RR (Return-to-ramp message)

CON

CON

FR (Return from Airborne message)

ADM

RIN

EA (Revised estimated time of arrival message)

RRT

AA/EB (Arrival taxi time variance information message)

FLT

* An SSM/CNL results in flights being deleted (a state represented internally as implicitly cancelled) as opposed to an AMS/CNL which results in a normal cancellation. Also an SSM/RPL may result in flight legs being deleted in case e.g. the routing of a multi-leg flight is changed.SSM/NEW is mapped to the ‘putFlight’ action meaning the flight will be created if it doesn’t exist and updated if it already exists.

** Note that ASM/RPL is mapped to a ‘putFlight’ action when converted to the internal xml equivalent message. See Identification of flights and legs for more information on what this means in terms of how existing legs are matched and updated.

### 18.11.2. ASM/SSM sub-message separation

Separation of sub-messages by means of ‘//’ is supported both when sub-messages are repeated from ASM/SSM Action and from Message Heading. However in the latter
case, all sub-messages must have the same time mode. Furthermore, also for sub-messages repeated from Message Heading, blank line is supported as alternative
separator.

### 18.11.3. SSM day of operation threshold

There is a threshold for the minimum allowed days between day of operation and the period of imported SSM messages. It is used to safeguard
that incoming SSM messages (also applies to SSIM) do not impact flight legs too close to the day of operation. The default threshold is 7 days.
The minimum value is 1 day, which means schedule changes starting the day after the day of operation can be imported. Schedule changes which
start earlier than that cannot be imported, regardless what the threshold is set to. To change the threshold, change Rave parameter interfaces_core.ssim_min_days_until_dop_p.

### 18.11.4. SSM and Date of Origin schemes

The date of origin (UDOR) for each rolled out flight is by default set to the UTC date of departure of the first leg in the flight.
However, by overriding class variable udor_is_based_on_utc of the SSMMapper class the behavior can be changed such that all
UDOR’s are based on the local departure date instead.

### 18.11.5. Support for MVT/MVA correction messages

MVT/MVA messages with a correction (COR) identifier on the first line are handled as any other MVT/MVA messages
except that the ‘eventType’ field is set to ‘COR-MVT’/’COR-MVA’ which allows for customization of the mapping
logic, in case it needs to be differentiated from ordinary MVT/MVA messages.

### 18.11.6. Identifying the flight in MVT/MVA messages

In IATA MVT/MVA messages the flight date is only given as a day, e.g. 14, without explicitly stating the month or year.
Normally, a message addresses a flight on the current day or a few days in the past. The standard behavior is to select
a flight date, using the given day, such that it is no more than a configurable number of days in the future. In the
core implementation the method std_interfaces.iata.mvt_parser.MVTParser.max_allowed_days_in_future() yields 1 for
Departure messages (sub-type = AD) and 3 for other MVT/MVA sub-types. See section Customization patterns for information
on how to override this method.

The flight date in MVT/MVA messages are supposed to be udor, but can sometimes (incorrectly) be replaced with scheduled date of departure.
This can cause problems with multi-leg flights that crosses midnight, where udor and scheduled date of departure will not be the same for all legs.
This is handled by the interface as followed.

If the field FLD (Flight Leg Date) is not given in the message; the interface will try to find legs, where either udor or
scheduled date of departure, matches provided flight date. In the case of multiple matches, the leg will be identified
using airport of movement, assigned aircraft, state of leg, now time, and message type. The flight date will then be adjusted to
correspond to the identified leg. If FLD is provided, we assume udor is flight date, and filter for legs with
scheduled date of departure as flight leg date and flight date as udor.

Similar to month and year not explicitly being stated, the date for actual and estimated times are not mandatory. In the MVT mapper,
the interface tries to identify the leg described in previous section. It will then adjust the dates for provided actual and estimated times to
the date closes to the best known leg start time for OUT and OFF times, and best known leg end time for ON and IN times.
These adjusted dates will then be used, if not the date is provided for the corresponding time.

### 18.11.7. Customization patterns

Inject custom parsing and mapping logic

In situations where certain aspects of the core mapping logic needs to be modified, it is possible to subclass any of the core
IATA parsers or mappers classes and override any of their methods. The core IATA classes are available in package std_interfaces.iata, modules are:

- asm_parser.py
- div_parser.py
- mvt_parser.py
- ssm_parser.py
- asm.py
- div.py
- mvt.py
- ssm.py

The parser classes are:

- ASMParser
- DIVParser
- MVTParser
- SSMParser

The master mapper classes are:

- ASMMapper
- DIVMapper
- MVTMapper
- SSMMapper

Furthermore, for ASM and SSM there are action mapper classes for each type of sub-message, e.g. ASM_NEW_Mapper, ASM_EQT_Mapper etc.

Below is an example that illustrates how to customize the mapping logic. The same principles apply also for parser customization. The
only difference is the class and method to override, e.g. in steps 1-2 below it would override class std_interfaces.iata.asm_parser.ASMParser
and in step 3 method get_ASM_Parser().

- In the core mapper (e.g. std_interfaces.iata.asm.py), identify the method you want to override.
Create a subclass of the core action mapper with an implementation of the overridden method.
E.g. if you want to override how onward flight data is mapped in ASM/NEW messages, create a class that inherits from the core ASM_NEW_Mapper
and implement your version of method map_onward_flight():

class MyASM_NEW_Mapper(std_interfaces.iata.asm.ASM_NEW_Mapper):

    def map_onward_flight(self, of, equipment, eqp):
      ...

- Create a subclass of std_interfaces.flight_types_mave2.FlightInterfaceHandler and override e.g. class method get_ASM_mapper():

class MyFlightInterfaceHandler(std_interfaces.flight_types_mave2.FlightInterfaceHandler):

    @classmethod
    def get_ASM_mapper(cls, service, plan):
        return std_interfaces.iata.asm.ASMMapper(service, plan, NEW=MyASM_NEW_Mapper())

Override the service mapping to use your custom MyFlightInterfaceHandler class for the pre-processor from_iata.
Create a custom mapping, e.g. $CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.ext.flight_input_5/my_mapping.xml with the following content
(assuming your custom classes were placed in a module called mymodule):

&lt;service-mapping xmlns=&quot;http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2&quot; language=&quot;Python&quot; target=&quot;air2_mave2&quot;&gt;
  &lt;include href=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/mapping.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;server-impl service_name=&quot;FlightInput&quot; service_version=&quot;5&quot;&gt;
    &lt;pre-process name=&quot;from_iata&quot; module=&quot;mymodule&quot; function=&quot;MyFlightInterfaceHandler.from_iata&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/server-impl&gt;
&lt;/service-mapping&gt;

- In $CARMUSR/data/config/ioservice_builder.xml, make sure your custom my_mapping.xml is used by the FlightInput service:

&lt;ioservice pattern=&quot;subscriber&quot; default_exception=&quot;TransientMsgError&quot;&gt;
  &lt;description&gt;Create/update flight information.&lt;/description&gt;
  &lt;smog-service name=&quot;FlightInput&quot; version=&quot;5&quot; protocol=&quot;plainxml&quot;&gt;
    &lt;service-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/services.xml&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;protocol-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/protocol.xml&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;service-mapping location=&quot;$CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.ext.flight_input_5/my_mapping.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/smog-service&gt;
&lt;/ioservice&gt;

Append custom mapping logic

In situations where logic needs to be added after each message of a certain IATA type, it is possible to override the pre-defined customization
point method custom_msg() that is called by the core mapper class after the parsing and mapping of the message is finalized.
This is similar to the previous example except that in this case a subclass is created of the core master mapper, e.g. std_interfaces.iata.mvt.MVTMapper.

- Create a subclass of the core master mapper with an implementation of the custom_msg() method, e.g.:

class MyMVTMapper(std_interfaces.iata.mvt.MVTMapper):

    def custom_msg(self, inmsg, outmsg):
      ...

- Create a subclass of std_interfaces.flight_types_mave2.FlightInterfaceHandler and override e.g. class method get_MVT_mapper():

class MyFlightInterfaceHandler(std_interfaces.flight_types_mave2.FlightInterfaceHandler):

    @classmethod
    def get_MVT_mapper(cls, service, plan):
        return MyMVTMapper(service, plan)

- See steps 4. and 5. in the previous example.

### 18.11.8. Ignored fields in SSM/ASM messages

Some information in the SSM/ASM messages is not deemed necessary for ops control, crew planning or crew tracking applications and is therefore
not passed on to the Flight Input interface.

Message reference

- Message Sequence Reference
- Creator Reference

Flight Information

- Joint Operation Airline Designators
- Operating Airline Disclosure - Code Share

Period/Frequency Information

- Joint Operation Airline Designators
- Operating Airline Disclosure - Code Share
- Operating Airline Disclosure - Shared Airline or Wet Lease Designation

Equipment Information

- Passenger Reservations Booking Modifier
- Operating Airline Disclosure - Code Share
- Operating Airline Disclosure - Shared Airline or Wet Lease Designation

Routing or Leg Information

- Scheduled Time of Passenger Departure
- Scheduled Time of Passenger Arrival
- Joint Operation Airline Designators
- Operating Airline Disclosure - Code Share
- Meal Service Note
- Operating Airline Disclosure - Shared Airline or Wet Lease Designation

Segment Information

- Traffic Restriction Note
- Operating Airline Disclosure - Code Share
- Operating Airline Disclosure - Shared Airline or Wet Lease Designation
Other Segment Information except the following:

- Duplicate Leg Cross Reference—Duplicate Leg Identification (DEI 10)
- Passenger Terminal Identifier (DEI 98/99)
- Passenger Reservations Booking Designator Segment Override (DEI 101)
- Departure/arrival Passenger Terminals Segment Overrides (DEI 198/199)

Sub-message Supplementary Information

- all fields

Supplementary Information for Whole Message

- all fields

Reject Information

- all fields

Repeat of Rejected Message

- all fields

### 18.11.9. Ignored fields in MVT/MVA messages

Some information in the MVT/MVA messages is not deemed necessary for ops control, crew planning or crew tracking applications and is therefore
not passed on to the Flight Input interface.

- Aircraft Registration - (Note: Passed on if system is JOC)
- Passenger Information Per Destination
- Reclearance Information
- Crew Report Time
- Movement After Pushback
- Take Off Fuel
- Take Off Weight
- Zero Fuel Weight
- Category of Operation
- Supplementary Information

### 18.11.10. Ignored fields in DIV messages

Some information in the DIV messages is not deemed necessary for ops control, crew planning or crew tracking applications and is therefore
not passed on to the Flight Input interface.

- Aircraft Registration
- Reason for Diversion
- Number of Passengers on Board
- Supplementary Information

(Even though the message contains some information about a possible continuation, no continuation flight leg will be created.)

## 18.12. Using ACARS ARINC 620-8 OOOI messages

This interface also supports receiving a subset of the ACARS OOOI messages from the ARINC 620-8 standard. These messages are transmitted by aircrafts on major events,
such as out of gate, off the ground, on the ground and into gate. It is assumed that ACARS messages are provided to this interface from some external source.
The actual transmission of messages via datalink or ground stations are not in the scope of this interface.
The interface automatically interpret supported ACARS messages and converts them into an xml equivalent message
before being handled by the interface.

### 18.12.1. Supported ACARS messages

The following messages from the ARINC 620-8 standard are currently supported:

SMI

Label

Description

Remark

ARR

QR

ON Report (ICAO Airport Code)

ARR

QS

IN Report (ICAO Airport Code)

Captain/first officer identifier (LA) and landing category (LA) TEI items are not supported.

DEP

QP

OUT Report (ICAO Airport Code)

DEP

QQ

OFF Report (ICAO Airport Code)

RTN

QT

OUT/Return IN report (ICAO Airport Code)

The ARINC standard specifies that the TEI items of a message can be split on multiple lines. This is currently not handled.

### 18.12.2. Ignoring ACARS messages

The interface contains logic for identifying ACARS messages that might be invalid or redundant
and should be ignored, without doing any updates in JCMS.
The logic is based on the event time, received time and now time of each ACARS message together
with a set of parameters that can be re-configured for each installation.

- Event time: Time of the main event in the message, for example the take-off time in an Off message.
- Received time: Time message was received by the ACARS server, before being sent to JCMS.
- Now time: The current time in JCMS.

Parameter

Description

Default value

max_event_time_deviation

Event time may not be older than this limit compared to the received time.

08:00

max_event_time_age

Event time in messages may not be older than this limit compared to now time.

24:00

lower_limit_out_time

Out time may not be more than this much before the estimated/scheduled departure time.

02:00

upper_limit_out_time

Out time may not be more than this much after the estimated/scheduled departure time.

12:00

lower_limit_off_time

Off time may not be more than this much before the latest known offblock time.

00:00

upper_limit_off_time

Off time may not be more than this much after the latest known offblock time.

04:00

lower_limit_on_time

On time may not be more than this much before the estimated/scheduled onblock time.

01:30

upper_limit_on_time

On time may not be more than this much after the estimated/scheduled onblock time.

03:00

lower_limit_in_time

In time may not be more than this much before the actual landing time.

00:00

upper_limit_in_time

In time may not be more than this much after the actual landing time.

05:00

lower_limit_return_time

Return-to-gate time may not be more than this much before the latest known offblock time.

00:00

upper_limit_return_time

Return-to-gate time may not be more than this much after the latest known offblock time.

06:00

### 18.12.3. Removal of invalid existing actual times

When receiving actual times from an ACARS OUT, OFF, ON or IN message the interface checks for subsequent existing actual times that
are inconsistent with the provided times. As an example, an existing actual landing time is removed if it is earlier than an actual
takeoff time provided in the ACARS message.

## 18.13. Using FAA SFDPS messages

This interface supports receiving FAA SFDPS (System-Wide Information Management (SWIM) Flight Data Publication Service)
messages in FIXM format.
The interface automatically interprets supported SFDPS messages and converts them into an xml equivalent message
before being handled by the interface.

### 18.13.1. Supported FAA SFDPS messages

There are various FAA SFDPS messages defined in FIXM format.
This interface currently supports EDCT (Estimated Departure Controlled Time) messages.

### 18.13.2. Identifying the flight

Estimated departure time in EDCT message is used for identifying flights in the database. There is a also a time window defined
around estimated departure time when trying to find the matching candidate. If no matching candidate is found, the message is discarded.

### 18.13.3. Clearing EDCT info

When a cancellation of EDCT is received, the interface clears the previously saved EDCT and set the EDCT status being “cancelled”.

## 18.14. Using NavBlue FlightPlan messages

This interface supports receiving http://aeec.aviation-ia.net/633 xml format FlightPlan messages.
The interface automatically interprets supported FlightPlan messages and converts them into an xml equivalent message
before being handled by the standard interface mapping. Only a small subset of the flight plan is supported by the data model.

### 18.14.1. Identifying the flight leg

Each FlightPlan message contains the flight plan for one flight leg. The leg is identified using the IATA flight key elements and the
IATA departure and arrival airport codes provided in the message.

### 18.14.2. Configuring extensions

The conversion of FlightPlan messages is done using an xslt style sheet located in $CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/navblue_flight_planning_1/schema/from_navblue_flightplan.xsl
In order to override the style sheet just place a custom style sheet in $CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/navblue_flight_planning_1/schema/from_navblue_flightplan.xsl

As a starting point for the following use cases we assume that no flight information for the given period is available.
To see the effect of update messages to existing trips, look in the section for operational input.
The result of the operations is described in tabular form as shown below.

- dep = departure airport
- arr = arrival airport
- sobt = scheduled departure time
- sibt = scheduled arrival time
state = type/status of the flight atom

- sched : scheduled leg
- canc  : cancelled leg
- rertd : rerouted leg (changed scheduled arrival station)
- retim : retimed leg (changed scheduled times)

- tail id = the assigned aircraft

This section provides examples how typical scheduling situations would be reflected using the flight based communication pattern.
That pattern uses the updateFlights operation and its subtypes, most often “updateFlight”, “setFlight” or “replaceFlight”.
In that case the source system only makes very few assumptions about the previous state in JCMS,
which is most suited for the publish/subscribe style.

### 18.15.1. Initial load

The initial load provides flight information for a certain scope for the first time. Note that for initial creation of flights
based on a given time table normally the Flight Schedule State interface is used. However, the Flight Input
interface may be better suited in cases where the source system holds each occurrence of a flight as individual objects.
This will normally be for a given time period, so the system will receive a set of messages listing flights
that occur at a certain date or (normally small) date range. For this purpose, the addFlight and putFlight message types would be used.
Special care must be taken for multileg flights if not all legs of the flight are always transferred together
(e.g. if the flight is not falling completely in the provided time period).
In that situation putFlight cannot be used, it would cancel the already transferred leg instead of just adding a new one.
A addFlight message for a flight with an existing leg will fail, so then updateFlight (or setFlight) can be used for the second leg.
Only setFlight can be used to transfer new legs separately for the same flight without relying on the existence of the others.

The following messages all create the same legs:

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;updateFlightsRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5&quot;
                      source=&quot;FLIGHTSCHEDULE&quot; created=&quot;2014-03-14T03:05:44&quot;
                      timeModeIsUTC=&quot;true&quot;
                      version=&quot;5&quot; &gt;
  &lt;action&gt;
    &lt;setFlight carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2014-05-14&quot; flightNumber=&quot;101&quot; &gt;
      &lt;setLegs&gt;
        &lt;setLeg startStation=&quot;GOT&quot; scheduledStartTime=&quot;2014-05-14T07:40:00&quot; startTimeOffset=&quot;PT2H&quot;
                endStation=&quot;FRA&quot; scheduledEndTime=&quot;2014-05-14T09:05:00&quot; endTimeOffset=&quot;PT2H&quot;&gt;
          &lt;equipment aircraftType=&quot;737&quot; /&gt;
        &lt;/setLeg&gt;
        &lt;setLeg startStation=&quot;FRA&quot; scheduledStartTime=&quot;2014-05-14T09:35:00&quot;  startTimeOffset=&quot;PT2H&quot;
                endStation=&quot;MUC&quot; scheduledEndTime=&quot;2014-05-14T10:13:00&quot; endTimeOffset=&quot;PT2H&quot;&gt;
          &lt;equipment aircraftType=&quot;737&quot; /&gt;
        &lt;/setLeg&gt;
      &lt;/setLegs&gt;
    &lt;/setFlight&gt;
  &lt;/action&gt;
&lt;/updateFlightsRequest&gt;

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;updateFlightsRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5&quot;

### 18.15.2. Cancellation

The following examples show the effect of cancellations.

If the whole flight is cancelled at once all legs in the flight are cancelled.
Any trips containing them become infeasible as they contain NOP (not operational) activities.
A message that contains explicit cancellation of all legs in the flight has the same effect.

  &lt;/action&gt;

### 18.16.1. State oriented communication

This section provides examples how typical operational situations would be reflected when using a state-oriented communication pattern.
That pattern uses the “setFlight(cancelLeg|setLeg)” messages and provide all available information.
The variation lies in how much information is provided in a single message and examples of this variation are given where relevant.

18.16.1.1. Regular operation
In the regular operation case JCMS receives a flow of updates to the legs that reflect the current state of operation.
The examples show the flow for the first leg GOT-FRA.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;

                      version=&quot;5&quot; &gt;

    &lt;setFlight carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2014-03-14&quot; flightNumber=&quot;101&quot; &gt;
      &lt;setLegs&gt;
        &lt;setLeg startStation=&quot;GOT&quot; scheduledStartTime=&quot;2014-03-14T07:40:00&quot; 
                endStation=&quot;FRA&quot; scheduledEndTime=&quot;2014-03-14T09:05:00&quot; &gt;
          &lt;operation&gt;
            &lt;estimatedTimes offBlock=&quot;2014-03-14T07:41:00&quot; /&gt;
          &lt;/operation&gt;
        &lt;/setLeg&gt;
      &lt;/setLegs&gt;
    &lt;/setFlight&gt;
  &lt;/action&gt;
&lt;/updateFlightsRequest&gt;

18.16.1.2. Return to Ramp
The following flow shows a scenario of return to ramp and crew change at the gate.
We assume that the flight has left the gate (after aobt.xml from the regular example)
The first message describes the intention to return to ramp, this would be communicated while the aircraft is not docked in again yet.

Note that only a return at the departure station is considerd a return event of the given leg.
If the aircraft moves at the destination after landing, this is either a return event of the next leg
or it can be handled as a separate operational leg of the current flight if this is the final destination.
The interface applies some checks on the provided times to detect this situation and will reject the message in that case.

18.16.1.3. Diversion and rerouting
The following examples show cases of diversion or rerouting.

In the first scenario we assume that the flight has not started yet when the information arrives that a landing in FRA is not possible.
The flight is rerouted (schedule update) through DUS instead.
The trip will be updated to contain the new leg, but cancelled legs are not automatically removed.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;updateFlightsRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5&quot;
                      source=&quot;SSM&quot; created=&quot;2014-03-14T07:05:44&quot;
                      timeModeIsUTC=&quot;true&quot; 
                      eventType=&quot;RPL&quot; 
                      version=&quot;5&quot; &gt;
  &lt;action&gt;
    &lt;setFlight carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2014-03-14&quot; flightNumber=&quot;101&quot; &gt;
      &lt;cancelLegs&gt;
        &lt;cancelLeg startStation=&quot;FRA&quot; scheduledStartTime=&quot;2014-03-14T09:35:00&quot; 
                endStation=&quot;MUC&quot; scheduledEndTime=&quot;2014-03-14T10:13:00&quot; /&gt;
      &lt;/cancelLegs&gt;
    &lt;/setFlight&gt;
  &lt;/action&gt;
  &lt;action&gt;
    &lt;setFlight carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2014-03-14&quot; flightNumber=&quot;101&quot; &gt;
      &lt;setLegs&gt;
        &lt;setLeg startStation=&quot;GOT&quot; scheduledStartTime=&quot;2014-03-14T07:40:00&quot; 
                endStation=&quot;FRA&quot; scheduledEndTime=&quot;2014-03-14T09:05:00&quot; &gt;
          &lt;reschedule startStation=&quot;GOT&quot; scheduledStartTime=&quot;2014-03-14T07:45:00&quot; 
                      endStation=&quot;DUS&quot; scheduledEndTime=&quot;2014-03-14T09:25:00&quot; isOperational=&quot;true&quot; /&gt;
        &lt;/setLeg&gt;
        &lt;setLeg startStation=&quot;DUS&quot; scheduledStartTime=&quot;2014-03-14T09:55:00&quot; 
                endStation=&quot;MUC&quot; scheduledEndTime=&quot;2014-03-14T10:58:00&quot; &gt;
        &lt;/setLeg&gt;
      &lt;/setLegs&gt;
    &lt;/setFlight&gt;
  &lt;/action&gt;
&lt;/updateFlightsRequest&gt;

If the information is sent in separate requests, the final result will be the same,
the trip gets infeasible as soon as the first change is handled but the type of the first alert might differ depending on the order of the emssages.
Typically the rerouting of the first leg would come first and break the connection at FRA, the cancellation of the second leg creates a “NOP” and
this is not fixed automatically by insertion of the DUS-MUC leg. The planner will have to remove the FRA-MUC leg manually.

In the next scenario we assume that the flight has started. Sending a reschedule at this point is an error, a started leg cannot be rescheduled.
The rerouting message will have the same effect as in the first scenario, only that the actuals for off block and take off are kept,
so that the update to the estimations doesnt impact the case.
Of course normally we would not expect to get a new estimated off block time for a started flight,
but that is not explicit handled as error since it doesn’t effect the application logic.

18.16.1.4. Cancellation and reinstation
The following examples show the effect of cancellations an reinstations.

If the whole flight is cancelled at once all legs in the flight are cancelled.
Any trips containing them become infeasible as they contain NOP (not operational) activities.
A message that contains explicit cancellation of all legs in the flight would have the same effect.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;

Reinstate both legs at once:

18.16.1.5. Equipment changes
The following examples show some options to provide equipment information for legs. During operation, normally that means providing actual tail names.
In the first of the following messages, a flight is created/updated with its both legs assigned to an aircraft  with the registration “LNBRH”.

The difference in behavior only shows when sending several legs at once, in the setLeg case the legs are grouped within the flight,
in the equipment request each leg is its own entity.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;updateFlightsRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5&quot;
                      source=&quot;SSM&quot; created=&quot;2014-03-14T07:36:44&quot;
                      timeModeIsUTC=&quot;true&quot; 
                      eventType=&quot;EQT&quot; 
                      version=&quot;5&quot; &gt;
  &lt;action&gt;
    &lt;setFlight carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2014-03-14&quot; flightNumber=&quot;101&quot; &gt;
      &lt;setLegs&gt;
        &lt;setLeg startStation=&quot;GOT&quot; scheduledStartTime=&quot;2014-03-14T07:40:00&quot; 
                endStation=&quot;FRA&quot; scheduledEndTime=&quot;2014-03-14T09:05:00&quot; &gt;
          &lt;equipment aircraft=&quot;LNBRH&quot; /&gt;
        &lt;/setLeg&gt;
        &lt;setLeg startStation=&quot;FRA&quot; scheduledStartTime=&quot;2014-03-14T09:35:00&quot; 
                endStation=&quot;MUC&quot; scheduledEndTime=&quot;2014-03-14T10:13:00&quot; &gt;
          &lt;equipment aircraft=&quot;LNBRH&quot; /&gt;
        &lt;/setLeg&gt;
      &lt;/setLegs&gt;
    &lt;/setFlight&gt;
  &lt;/action&gt;
&lt;/updateFlightsRequest&gt;

In the second message, the aircraft tail name is updated for all legs in the flight:

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;updateFlightsRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5&quot;
                      source=&quot;FLIGHTOPS&quot; created=&quot;2014-03-14T07:36:44&quot;
                      timeModeIsUTC=&quot;true&quot; 
                      eventType=&quot;EQT&quot;
                      version=&quot;5&quot; &gt;
  &lt;action&gt;
    &lt;updateFlight carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2014-03-14&quot; flightNumber=&quot;101&quot;&gt;
      &lt;setFlightEquipment aircraft=&quot;LNRCZ&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;/updateFlight&gt;
  &lt;/action&gt;
&lt;/updateFlightsRequest&gt;

The original tail assignment will be replaced, as the interface assumes that any leg is always planned to be operated by a single aircraft.

## 18.17. IOService builder configuration

Service FlightInput version 5 (see Note for IOService builder)

&lt;smog-service name=&quot;FlightInput&quot; version=&quot;5&quot; protocol=&quot;plainxml&quot;&gt;
  &lt;service-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/services.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;protocol-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/protocol.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;service-mapping location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/mapping.xml&quot;/&gt;
&lt;/smog-service&gt;

Note that with this version of the service also protocols openapi, soap and plainjson are supported.
However if the ioservice is used for importing NavBlue FlightPlan messages (see Using NavBlue FlightPlan messages),
then protocol plainxml must be used.

&lt;smog-service name=&quot;FlightInput&quot; version=&quot;1.0&quot; protocol=&quot;plainxml&quot;&gt;

--- SUBPAGE: flight_state.html ---

# 19. Flight State

This chapter describes the standard Flight State interface that can be used for retrieving the complete information about flights stored in JCMS.
This interface is strictly leg oriented, i.e. there is nothing in the structure of the messages that tie together individual legs in
multi-leg flights. Consequently, there is no guarantee that all legs in a multi-leg flight are contained in one and the same message.

The interface provides the full state of flight legs in terms of their properties and related entities such as delays, passenger data, flight plan
code shares and return events (as mentioned above). Properties and elements with undefined or non-existing information are output with “null”
values. Null values are represented differently depending on protocol.

Any flight leg instance within the data model is included, regardless if they are cancelled, code share duplicates or considered non-operational
due to any other reason. However wait-at-gate, return-to-ramp or airborne return events are not represented as flight legs in their own right (even
if stored as flight leg instances internally in the data model). Also, deleted flight leg instances are not included (internally represented
as implicitly cancelled).

The current version of this interface is 1.beta.
Link to FlightState_1_beta.xsd

## 19.1. Interface capabilities

Available operations are:

pingPings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).

getFlightsInPeriodGet complete flight leg information as a state for all flight legs within a given period.

updateFlightsOnly used as client i.e. when producing flight state messages based on a trigger in JCMS (see Flight State Events).

## 19.2. Supported time modes

All times are provided in UTC.

## 19.3. Selection of flight legs

Based on a requested period, the interface responds with all flight legs having scheduled departure time within the period. The period start
time counts as within the period while the end time is considered outside the period. Any flight legs regardless of operational status are included.

## 19.4. Customization patterns

In general terms, standard techniques for extending SMOG based interfaces apply for adding custom information to the interface or
changing the mapping of existing information in the standard interface. In situations where certain aspects of the core mapping logic needs to
be modified, typically the interface handler std_interfaces.flight_types_mave2.FlightStateOutputInterfaceHandler is subclassed in order to
override specific methods, e.g. find_legs_in_period for changing which flight legs are extracted based on a requested period.

## 19.5. IOService builder configuration

Service FlightState version 1.beta:

&lt;ioservice pattern=&quot;requestresponse&quot;&gt;
  &lt;smog-service name=&quot;FlightState&quot; version=&quot;1.beta&quot; protocol=&quot;plainxml|plainjson&quot;&gt;
    &lt;service-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/services.xml&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;protocol-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/protocol.xml&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;service-mapping location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/mapping_requested.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/smog-service&gt;
&lt;/ioservice&gt;

--- SUBPAGE: flight_state_events.html ---

# 20. Flight State Events

This chapter describes the standard interface for publishing flight leg state information to external systems when changes occur in JCMS to
flight leg properties or related entities such as delays, passenger data, flight plan code shares and return events. One message per flight
leg is published, therefore, since the trigger processes all changes in a changeset (a data model refresh cycle), one changeset may result
several messages.

The interface is prepared to be used with both Subscription Management and Message Receivers patterns, see Interface Implementation Patterns.
It uses the std_interfaces.common.NativeProtocolFormatter as default receiver.

See IOService builder configuration for an example how to use the Subscription Management pattern to set up the interface for a combined
batch/delta feed. Note that when a flight leg is deleted (internally represented with cancel status implicitly cancelled) this results in
a change in the delta feed. Deleted flight leg instances are however not included in the batch feed.

## 20.1. Formatters

### 20.1.1. Jeppesen FliteBrief Flights message formatter

This standard formatter generates messages on the Flitebrief SCH001 format from the Flight State interface.

Sink: defined in configuration (see ‘add_receiver’ in the ‘SMOG configuration’ section below)

Class: std_interfaces.jeppesen_flitebrief.formatters.FBFormatterFlight

Options:

Parameter

Type

Description

logger

Logger

Logger to use for debugging information.

carrier

string

Only generate messages for flights with this carrier code, optional.

aircraftOwner

string

Only generate messages for flights with this aircraft owner airline code, optional.

cockpitEmployer

string

Only generate messages for flights with this cockpit crew employer airline code, optional.

cabinEmployer

string

Only generate messages for flights with this cabin crew employer airline code, optional.

### 20.1.2. SMOG configuration

Example of SMOG configuration “$CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1.ext/mapping_flitebrief_delta.xml”
required to add receivers for FliteBrief delta messages.
In the example below, messages are filtered and formatted such that messages related to ‘AM’ flights are directed to queue
‘from.ioservice.CrewOnFlight_4_event.fb_AM’ and ‘5D’ flights messages are directed to queue ‘from.ioservice.CrewOnFlight_4_event.fb_5D’.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;service-mapping xmlns=&quot;http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2&quot; target=&quot;air2_mave2&quot; language=&quot;Python&quot;&gt;
  &lt;include href=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/mapping_event.xml&quot;/&gt;

  &lt;output-mapping struct=&quot;flight_state.FlightsStateMsg&quot;&gt;
    &lt;import alias=&quot;formatters&quot; name=&quot;std_interfaces.jeppesen_flitebrief.formatters&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;assign name=&quot;formatter_fb_5D&quot; expr=&quot;formatters.FBFormatterFlight(service_logger, aircraftOwner=&#39;5D&#39;, cabinEmployer=&#39;5D&#39;)&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;assign name=&quot;formatter_fb_AM&quot; expr=&quot;formatters.FBFormatterFlight(service_logger, carrier=&#39;AM&#39;)&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;call name=&quot;add_formatter_fb_5D&quot; expr=&quot;generator.add_receiver(&#39;from.ioservice.FlightState_1_event.fb_5D&#39;, formatter_fb_5D)&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;call name=&quot;add_formatter_fb_AM&quot; expr=&quot;generator.add_receiver(&#39;from.ioservice.FlightState_1_event.fb_AM&#39;, formatter_fb_AM)&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/output-mapping&gt;
&lt;/service-mapping&gt;

For the delta service, whenever flight information is updated in JCMS, a corresponding Flitebrief message
is emitted according to the table below:

SCH001

SCH001

SCH001

Flight renamed

SCH001

N/A

N/A

Tail assignment updated

SCH001

Scheduled times updated

SCH001

Scheduled departure station updated

SCH001

Scheduled arrival station updated

SCH001

Onward flight updated

N/A

Passenger terminal updated

N/A

Seat configuration updated

N/A

Estimated departure times updated

SCH001

Delay information updated

N/A

Actual departure times updated

N/A

Return to ramp

N/A

Estimated arrival times updated

SCH001

Actual arrival times updated

N/A

Internal times updated

N/A

N/A

N/A

Example of SMOG configuration “$CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1.ext/mapping_flitebrief_load.xml”
required to add receivers for FliteBrief load messages.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;service-mapping xmlns=&quot;http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2&quot; target=&quot;air2_mave2&quot; language=&quot;Python&quot;&gt;
  &lt;include href=&quot;$CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/mapping_requested.xml&quot;/&gt;

  &lt;server-impl service_name=&quot;FlightState&quot; service_version=&quot;1.beta&quot;&gt;
    &lt;post-process name=&quot;format&quot; module=&quot;std_interfaces.flight_types_mave2&quot; function=&quot;FlightMessageGenerator.format&quot; operation=&quot;getFlightsInPeriod&quot; process_struct=&quot;true&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/server-impl&gt;

  &lt;output-mapping struct=&quot;flight_state.FlightsStateMsg&quot;&gt;
    &lt;import alias=&quot;formatters&quot; name=&quot;std_interfaces.jeppesen_flitebrief.formatters&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;assign name=&quot;formatter_fb_5D&quot; expr=&quot;formatters.FBFormatterFlight(service_logger, aircraftOwner=&#39;5D&#39;, cabinEmployer=&#39;5D&#39;)&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;assign name=&quot;formatter_fb_AM&quot; expr=&quot;formatters.FBFormatterFlight(service_logger, carrier=&#39;AM&#39;)&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;call name=&quot;add_formatter_fb_5D&quot; expr=&quot;generator.add_receiver(&#39;from.ioservice.FlightState_1_event.fb_5D&#39;, formatter_fb_5D)&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;call name=&quot;add_formatter_fb_AM&quot; expr=&quot;generator.add_receiver(&#39;from.ioservice.FlightState_1_event.fb_AM&#39;, formatter_fb_AM)&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/output-mapping&gt;

&lt;/service-mapping&gt;

### 20.1.3. IOService builder configuration

With the example configuration below, every day at 0:30, the load service goes through all flight legs
with a scheduled departure time within the subscription period, 0:00 - 48:00 hours. Subsequent changes within the period
are picked up by the delta service configured with the subscription.

&lt;ioservice name=&quot;FliteBrief_flight_events&quot; pattern=&quot;trigger&quot; handler_module=&quot;std_interfaces.triggers.flight_state_events&quot;&gt;
  &lt;description&gt;Send flights to FliteBrief&lt;description&gt;
  &lt;subscription&gt;
    &lt;moving name=&quot;moving&quot; before=&quot;0:00&quot; after=&quot;48:00&quot; floor=&quot;day&quot; time_of_day=&quot;00:30&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;filter name=&quot;period&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/subscription&gt;
  &lt;delta-service name=&quot;FlightState&quot; version=&quot;1.beta&quot; protocol=&quot;plainjson&quot; &gt;
    &lt;service-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/services.xml&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;protocol-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/protocol.xml&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;service-mapping location=&quot;$CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1.ext/mapping_flitebrief_delta.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/delta-service&gt;
  &lt;load-service name=&quot;FlightState&quot; version=&quot;1.beta&quot; protocol=&quot;plainjson&quot; &gt;
    &lt;service-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/services.xml&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;protocol-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/protocol.xml&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;service-mapping location=&quot;$CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1.ext/mapping_flitebrief_load.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/load-service&gt;
&lt;/ioservice&gt;

### 20.1.4. Configuring a custom formatter

It’s possible to configure the formatter this interface should use when sending event messages by updating the default SMOG service-mapping
and call the generator.add_receiver method.

&lt;service-mapping xmlns=&quot;http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2&quot; target=&quot;air2_mave2&quot; language=&quot;Python&quot;&gt;
  &lt;include href=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/mapping_event.xml&quot;/&gt;

  &lt;output-mapping struct=&quot;flight_state.FlightsStateMsg&quot;&gt;
    &lt;call name=&quot;add_my_custom_receiver&quot; expr=&quot;generator.add_receiver(&#39;from_ioservice_FlightState_1_event.mycustom&#39;, std_interfaces.ext.MyCustomFormatter())&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;/output-mapping&gt;
&lt;/service-mapping&gt;

The generator.add_receiver method registers a new a receiver for messages on a specific format.
Each receiver is associated with a specific message queue and a formatter that determines the format
and formatting options of the generated messages for that receiver.

The custom formatter should be a subclass of std_interfaces.common.MessageFormatter and implement the format method.

from std_interfaces.common import MessageFormatter

class MyCustomFormatter(MessageFormatter):
    &quot;&quot;&quot;
    Formatter generating messages containing the flight number of updated flights.
    &quot;&quot;&quot;

    def format(self, payload, headers):
        &quot;&quot;&quot;
        @param payload: Request message(s) created by client mapping.
        @type payload:  Smog struct or list of Smog struct
        @param headers: Dictionary of headers passed with the incoming request message
        @type headers:  dict or list of dicts
        @return:        Tuple of two lists of equal length, one with output messages content and one with message header attributes
        @rtype:         (list of string, list of dict)
        &quot;&quot;&quot;
        :
        return contents, headers

## 20.2. Example messages

### 20.2.1. Landing

The following message is generated when flight, JJ 101 is scheduled on 2014-03-24 from OSL to CPH has performed a landing. The message provides
changes to the following properties:

- Arrival gate
- Arrival stand
- Autoland
- Actual touch-down time
- Estimated in-block time
- Actual landing fuel

# 21. Flight Schedule State

This chapter describes the interface used for importing and exporting complete flight schedules to/from JCMS.
A complete flight schedule comprises all flights operated by an administrative carrier for a given time period. The schedule itself
is not represented in JCMS as a unit of its own right, instead the interface rolls out the schedule and creates a set of
dated flight legs. When importing schedules, the interface is based on the principle that each message corresponds to a single database
transaction. This means that if an error is raised when processing a message, then the whole message is discarded and no flight legs have
been created.

In general the systems providing flight schedule information are regarded master relative to JCMS and the interface is implemented as
publish/subscribe.

The current version of this interface is 4.
Link to FlightScheduleState_4.xsd
Link to FlightScheduleState_4_schema.json
Link to FlightScheduleState_4_openapi.json

## 21.1. Interface capabilities

The Flight Schedule State interface is designed for importing schedules in future planning periods. It is not designed for importing
schedules within the operational time window while it doesn’t apply any operational checks on existing flight legs in the plan.
For schedule changes during day of operation please utilize the corresponding capabilities of the Flight Input interface.
The importing of a flight schedule is a state operation which means that any flights already existing in the data model within
the imported plan period are marked as deleted (a state represented internally as implicitly cancelled) if they don’t match any flight in
the imported schedule. By means of a custom flights layer (see Importing airport slots) it is possible to restrict
which flights are deleted, thus protecting e.g. flights that have been manually created or have been imported ad-hoc from another source.

Available operations are:

pingPings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).

putFlightScheduleStateSupersede all existing flight information covering schedules for the specified carriers and periods (one-way request without any response message).

putFlightScheduleStateWithAckSupersede all existing flight information covering schedules for the specified carriers and periods (with acknowledge response on successful update).
The acknowledge response message contains a summary describing number of flights that was affected in JCMS by the schedule.

getFlightScheduleStateExtract a flight schedule for the given carrier and period, optionally filtered by aircraft group/type and service type.

getSSIMExtract a flight schedule on IATA SSIM format for the given carrier and period, optionally filtered by aircraft group/type and service type.

putAirportSlotsUpdates airport slot information for given airport(s).

putAirportSlotsWithAckUpdates airport slot information for given airport(s) (with acknowledge response on successful update).

### 21.1.1. Supported time modes

The schedules can either be based on UTC time or local time. This is specified separately for each schedule.
Internally, JCMS always stores the arrival and departure times based on UTC. When importing a schedule based on
local time, all times are converted to UTC using the built-in time zone information. Conversely, when exporting
to a schedule based on local time, all times are converted from UTC.

Please note that if conversion from local time to UTC leads to duplicate flights on a UTC day (and thus breaking IATA rules),
import of such a schedule will fail. Therefore, schedules must include suffixes, e.g. ‘Z’ where needed in order to prevent
flight duplication in UTC time.

## 21.2. Importing schedules

The operation putFlightScheduleState replaces existing flights in JCMS with new data according to the flight schedules
defined in the request. Each schedule in the request specifies a number of schedule pattern records (period and weekdays)
during which a certain flight leg should be rolled out.
If a new period is scheduled, all legs are created new in JCMS. If the schedule replaces an already
scheduled period, or if the schedule period partly overlaps a previous schedule, then the interface
finds all existing flights for the carrier, having a scheduled departure date within the period. A flight is considered included
in the schedule period if its scheduled departure date (of the first leg in the flight), in the time mode (UTC or local time)
stated in the schedule, is between the period start date and end date (both start and end date inclusive). It updates the legs of
those flights that are still in the schedule with new information, creates new legs if needed and deletes (implicitly cancels)
legs which are no longer part of the schedule.
If scheduled departure/arrival times are updated, any existing aircraft assignment times are updated too, to reflect the new
schedule times of the leg.

The putFlightScheduleState operation is normally used in batch mode to provide initial or updated schedules for one
or more carriers, for a given period, in a similar way as sending a new IATA SSIM file would.
It is expected that no other updates for the flights in the same scope are coming in close to this batch,
i.e. there are no ordering or concurrency constraints.

### 21.2.1. Date of Origin schemes

The date of origin (UDOR) for each rolled out flight is by default set to the UTC date of departure
of the first leg in the flight. However, by means of a configuration setting (see below), the behavior
can be changed such that all UDOR’s are based on the local departure date instead.

### 21.2.2. Time offset checking

All time and date values are written in the UTC time zone. Local time
values are converted to UTC. If there is a mismatch between what the
message says is the time offset for a specific airport and what the
database says for the same airport, then an error is raised. This means that
the whole message is discarded. However, this behavior can be overridden by means of a configuration setting (see below).
By using this configuration feature a log warning message is issued if a
time offset mismatch is detected, and the processing of the message continues.
Time offsets are always checked whenever provided in the message, regardless if the schedule(s) in the incoming request
are based on UTC or local time.

In connection with DST switches, if the system detects that a specified local time departure or arrival time
of a flight leg is ambiguous or missing, then the interface falls back to calculating the UTC
departure/arrival time based on the specified local time and offset. This special case of using the
specified UTC offset only applies if the specified schedule pattern period only comprises ONE flight leg
instance. If an UTC offset is not explicitly specified for the departure/arrival time in question, or if
the schedule pattern period covers more than one day of operation, then an error is raised.

### 21.2.3. Data consistency checking

The following checks are made on the data in an incoming request message:

- No departure of the same flight at the same station on the same date are allowed.
- No arrival of the same flight at the same station on the same date are allowed.
- Elements of type ScheduledFlightLegPattern must be grouped by flightNumber in the incoming request.
An error is raised and the message is discarded if the scheduledStartTime is after the scheduledEndTime of a rolled
out leg (after converting the provided time to UTC, if necessary). Although negative activity durations are technically
supported in JCMS, it is enforced that flight legs are scheduled with a positive duration.

An error is raised and the message is discarded if the operating airline carrier of a ScheduledFlightLegPattern record
differs from the carrier stated in the header.

An error is raised and the message is discarded if the period stated in the header is invalid, i.e. if periodStart is
after periodEnd.

An error is raised and the message is discarded if the period stated in the header starts before a
configurable number of days after current day of operation (see Importing airport slots).
By default, if not overridden by custom configuration, this “Day of operation threshold” is set to 7 days.

A log warning message is issued if a ScheduledFlightLegPattern record doesn’t yield any flight leg instances. This may
happen if there are no weekdays in the daysOfOperation field that matches the given period of operation. Note however
that no warning or error is issued if there are any “unused” weekdays, i.e. some of the weekdays in the daysOfOperation
field don’t exist in the given period.

Note that there is no consistency check of the LegSchedulePeriodPattern period in relation to the period
stated in the header of a given schedule. The period in the header is only used when identifying existing legs and aircraft
rotations for canceling/removal.

### 21.2.4. Ordering of data

For multi-leg flights, the ScheduledFlightLegPattern records are assumed to be
ordered by leg sequence number. If not, the interface is not able to derive the correct UDOR if UDOR is
not based on the same time mode as the schedule data (see Importing airport slots).
E.g. if the schedule is based on local time but UDOR’s should be calculated based on UTC. If this situation
is detected, the interface will raise an error and reject the message.

### 21.2.5. Creation of Aircraft Rotations

This capability is disabled by default (see Importing airport slots for how to enable it).
Information in the LegScheduleOnwardFlightData element is used for constructing aircraft rotations in JCMS.
Each schedule in an incoming message is processed separately. For aircraft rotations this means that
an aircraft rotation cannot continue across different schedules. If the onward flight of a leg in one
schedule refers to a flight from another schedule, then the rotation will be discontinued and a new
rotation will begin with the referenced flight.
If the onward information is missing it is assumed that the onward flight reference is identical to the
flight identifier of the ScheduledFlightLegPattern record itself. This is the case for legs in multi-leg
flights (except for the last leg). Aircraft rotations are not written to the model on the fly. After all
ScheduleFlightLegPattern records in a message have been processed and thus all leg instances are
created, then the aircraft rotations are calculated and written to the model. Aircraft rotations only containing
one single leg are not written to the model. When constructing aircraft rotations, the following criteria
must be fulfilled for two legs to be linked to each other in the same aircraft rotation:

- The two legs must belong to the same schedule
- The first leg must have an onward reference that matches the flight identifier of the succeeding one
The arrival airport of the first leg must be the same as the departure airport of the succeeding one
(it is assumed that aircraft rotations never continue over co-located airports)

- Both legs must have the same planned aircraft type
- The scheduled end time of the first leg must be less than the scheduled start time of the succeeding one

In addition, if aircraftRotationLayover is specified, then there must be a time gap between the two legs
that corresponds to at least the specified aircraftRotationLayover. If there are several possible
succeeding legs that fulfill these criteria, then the best match is selected, i.e. the leg that gives
a gap that is closest to the specified aircraftRotationLayover.

The interface creates aircraft rotations for the given schedule period isolated. It makes no attempts to
merge with existing aircraft rotations from adjacent or overlapping schedule periods. Therefore, aircraft
rotations may not be correctly represented around borders between different schedule periods, something
that may result in incorrect connection time information when creating trips.

Before writing the aircraft rotations to the model for a given schedule, any existing aircraft rotation
assignments for the given carrier and within the
given schedule period is removed. All existing legs having a scheduled start time inside the period stated
in the header are thus detached from any existing aircraft rotation to which they may belong. After that,
all empty rotation objects having “dt” within the schedule period, are removed.

### 21.2.6. Importing IATA SSIM Schedule Data Set

This interface support receiving IATA messages of type SSIM. IATA messages are automatically converted into an xml equivalent message
before being handled by the interface. The implementation is based on the IATA Standard Schedules Information Manual issued March 2011.

21.2.6.1. Limitations
The following limitations apply when loading an SSIM message.

- Record 2 - Period of Schedule Validity must not be valid indefinitely using “00XXX00”.
All itineraries of SSIM file are processed, even if they start outside the Period of Schedule Validity
as specified in Record 2.

No support for using Duplicate Airline Designator Marker in Record 2 combined with stating the
identity (name) of the airline as free text in General Information.

- Code Sharing and Wet Lease Handling in Record 3 are ignored.
- Record 3 - Period of Operation must not be valid indefinitely using “00XXX00”.
- Joint Operation Airline Designators in Record 3 are ignored.

21.2.6.2. Ignored fields in SSIM messages
Some information in the SSIM message is not deemed necessary for ops control, crew planning or crew tracking applications and is
therefore not passed on to the Flight Schedule State standard interface:

- Passenger STD/STA
- Passenger Reservations Booking Modifier PRBM
- Meal Service Note
- Minimum Connecting Time International/Domestic Status
- Traffic Restriction Code.
- Traffic Restriction Code Leg Overflow Indicator.
- Secure Flight Indicator

21.2.6.3. Default values
The following default values are applied in accordance with IATA SSIM appendix H:

Data Element

Default value

Aircraft Owner

Airline designator (carrier) of the flight

Cabin Crew Employer

Aircraft Owner

Cockpit Crew Employer

Aircraft Owner

Frequency Rate

Weekly

21.2.6.4. Segment Data Record - Record Type 4
Except from the following Data Element Identifiers (DEI), the associated Data records are passed on to the Flight Schedule State service as
“additionalInformation”:

- DEI 10  - Duplicate Leg Identification, is mapped to the “codeShare” section of the Flight Schedule State schema.
- DEI 106 - Passenger Reservations Booking Designator Exceeding Maximum length
- DEI 108 - Aircraft Configuration/Version Exceeding Maximum length
- DEI 121 - Aircraft type publication override

The “additionalInformation” structure is a list of records, each one consisting of a type identifier and an associated data field.
In the configuration layer it is possible to register a callback function for custom handling of other DEI’s than the ones above.
Please see Importing airport slots for information on how to configure callback functions.

21.2.6.5. Configuration (deprecated, only applicable to FlightScheduleState version 3.0)
The transformation is invoked by adding the following uri in the route definition between the end points.

jython://std_interfaces_adaptors.camel.SSIM_to_putFlightScheduleStateRequest_3_0

Example route definition which polls a directory for SSIM file, transforms it to putFlightScheduleState request
and forwards the request to the IO-server:

&lt;route id=&quot;ssim_flightschedule&quot;&gt;
  &lt;from uri=&quot;file://ssim/import/&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;to uri=&quot;jython://std_interfaces_adaptors.camel.SSIM_to_putFlightScheduleStateRequest_3_0&quot; /&gt;
  &lt;to pattern=&quot;InOnly&quot; uri=&quot;jmsbroker:queue:cmsbroker:inbound.scheduled_based_input&quot;/&gt;
&lt;/route&gt;

Note that for interface versions newer than 3.0 the transformation step described above is obsolete.

## 21.3. Exporting schedules

Flight schedules can be extracted from JCMS based on existing flights in the plan. An export request specifies
an operating carrier and a time period as a minimum. As a consequence, if the plan contains flights with different
operating carriers, schedules for the different carriers must be exported separately one at a time. It is also possible
to specify whether the exported schedule should be based on UTC or local time mode. If not specified, UTC is default.
The export request may also optionally specify a list of aircraft groups or aircraft types and a list of service types in order to further
filter the extracted flights. For multi-leg flights, the interface only looks at the first leg of the flight to determine
if the flight matches the specified filter.

Export is carried out in a flight centric manner such that also multi-leg flights are always included or excluded in their entirety.
Flights with a scheduled departure date (of the first leg) within the given time period are included, where both the start and end
date of the period count as inclusive. Both the departure date and the time period are related to the specified time mode.
Deleted and cancelled flight legs are not included. Flight legs without any aircraft type or service type specified are also
excluded from export.
Note that there may be cases where a multi-leg flight is included in the exported schedule although parts of the flight stretches
beyond the schedule period. As an example, if a flight consists of two legs, the first departing in the evening the 25:th of March
and the second leg just after midnight on the 26:th of March. If the export request specifies the period end date to be the 25:th
of March then also the second leg of that flight will be represented in the exported schedule, even though its scheduled departure
date is outside the period.

The operation getFlightScheduleState extracts a flight schedule for the given carrier and period, optionally filtered
by aircraft group/type and service type.

### 21.3.1. Exporting IATA SSIM Schedule Data Set

The operation getSSIM extracts a flight schedule on IATA SSIM format for the given carrier and period, optionally
filtered by aircraft type and service type. The Days of Operation pattern specified for each itinerary is always repeated
in weekly intervals throughout the itinerary period. Fortnightly intervals are not used. The SSIM export is rejected if there
exists flights within the exported period that do not have any leg with sequence number 1 or multi-leg flights with inconsistent
routing with respect to their leg sequence numbers and departure/arrival stations.

It is also possible to turn off some grouping parameters of the flight legs, for example passenger terminals and code shares,
and thus get a more compact SSIM schedule. See current schema Flight Schedule State for more details.

21.3.1.1. Segment Data Record - Record Type 4
In the configuration layer it is possible to register a callback function for adding custom Record Type 4 Data Elements into
the exported SSIM. Please see Importing airport slots for information on how to configure callback functions.

## 21.4. Importing airport slots

This service allows external systems, typically flight scheduling systems or airport coordinators,
to communicate airport slots to JCMS by using operations putAirportSlots or putAirportSlotsWithAck.
Airport slot information in requests must be expressed according to format in SSIM chapter 6.4.3.
Each request must contain the complete state of all airport slots for the specified airports and in the given time period (e.g., season, month, or other defined period).
The operation only updates airport slots for the airports included in the request, making it possible to send request for one or multiple airports at a time.

The backend service in JCMS is configured to only operate on data within a specific data context period.
The service silently ignores to process the airport slots that is falling outside the data context period. More specifically JCMS only
handles the airport slots with a flight date after/before the start/end date of the data context period.

The backend service in JCMS is configured to operate only within a specific data context period.
The service cannot handle airport slots that fall outside the data context and such slots are silently ignored if included in requests.
Specifically, only slots whose flight date start/end after/before the data context period dates are processed.

## 21.5. Configuration

UDOR based on UTC or local timeConfigures the method for calculating UDOR for scheduled flight legs upon import, i.e. whether UDOR
of flight legs in JCMS should be based on the UTC date or local date of flight departure.
Default is UDOR based on UTC date. To change to UDOR based on local date, call class method
FlightScheduleInterfaceHandler.set_udor_is_based_on_localtime() from a custom mapping.xml.

Ignore time zone offset mismatchConfigures if incoming request should be rejected or not when there is a mismatch
between a provided start/end time offset and the offset that results from the
JCMS time zone information. Default is to reject incoming request upon mismatch.
To relax checking time zone offset mismatch, call class method
FlightScheduleInterfaceHandler.set_ignore_time_offset_mismatch() from a custom mapping.xml.

Day of operation thresholdConfigures the minimum allowed days between day of operation and the start of the time period of an
imported schedule. It is used to safeguard that incoming SSIM (also applies to SSM) do not impact
flights too close to the day of operation. The default threshold is 7 days. The minimum value is 1 day,
which means a schedule starting the day after the day of operation can be imported. A schedule which
starts earlier than that cannot be imported, regardless what the threshold is set to. To change the
threshold, change the Rave parameter interfaces_core.ssim_min_days_until_dop_p.

Exclude suffix from flight keyIf set to True, suffix is not considered part of the flight key when importing a schedule. This allows the
interface to handle legs with a given flight number both with and without suffixes as being part of the same
multileg flight. Default is True, to set to False, call class method
FlightScheduleInterfaceHandler.include_suffix_in_flight_key() from a custom mapping.xml.

Use employer defaultsIf set to True, aircraft owner is used as default for cockpit and cabin crew employer if missing in an
imported SSIM. Default is True, to set to False, call method FlightScheduleInterfaceHandler.skip_employer_defaults()
from a custom mapping xml.

Override of imported schedule periodIt is possible to override the original schedule period stated in the request when importing a schedule,
e.g. in order to only import a subset of an SSIM file.
The override is done on a per request basis by specifying message header attributes
‘period_start’ and/or ‘period_end’ in ISO-8601 (e.g. ‘2021-02-05’) or AbsDate (e.g. ‘5FEB2021’) format, and in
the same time mode as the imported schedule(s). If the override period does not overlap the original schedule
period, the override period is ignored and the schedule is imported according to its original period as defined
in the request.
If the override period restricts an imported schedule period, the same flight centric logic applies as when
importing a complete schedule. Therefore, multi-leg flights are either imported in their entirety or not imported
at all, depending on whether the departure date of the first leg is within the restricted period or not. This
applies even for multi-leg flights where all legs are not on the same scheduled departure date.
The same logic applies when deleting existing flights that are not in the imported schedule. Thus if a multi-
leg flight starts within the period, all legs of that flight will be deleted even if some of the legs depart on
days beyond the schedule period.
If an override period extends an imported schedule period (i.e. lower and/or upper boundary stretches beyond
the schedule period), it doesn’t affect the imported period but it does affect the period in which existing
flights are deleted if they don’t match any flight in the imported schedule.

Flights layerBy specifying a flights layer when importing a schedule it is possible to restrict which of the existing flight legs
are being marked implicitly cancelled if they don’t match any flight leg in the imported schedule. The purpose is to
protect e.g. flights that have been manually created or have been imported ad-hoc from another source. By default,
without any layer specified, all existing flight legs within the schedule period and with the same operating carrier
as the one specified with the imported schedule, are marked implicitly cancelled if they don’t exist in the
imported schedule.
A flights layer is specified in message header attribute ‘flights_layer’ as a comma-separated list of data sources.
Each data source is the name of the source from which flight legs are created. As an example, specifying
message header attribute ‘flights_layer’ with value ‘SSIM’ results in that only existing flight legs originating
from an SSIM import will be subject to being implicitly cancelled if they don’t match any leg in the imported schedule.
There exists a number of pre-defined data source id’s in JCMS: ‘ACARS’, ‘SSIM’, ‘SSM’.

Create AC RotationsConfigures if aircraft rotations should be created.
Default is disabled. To enable, call class method
FlightScheduleInterfaceHandler.enable_create_ac_rotations() from a custom mapping.xml.

Importing Sub-fleetsThe import of a flight schedule can be limited to only update flights corresponding to the specific aircraft
types (sub fleet) referenced in the imported schedule.
The purpose is to allow importing different schedules for same carrier and period but with flights for different sub fleets.
Importantly, this option prevents removal of already scheduled flights in JCMS having other aircraft types.
The option is activated by setting the message header ‘import_subfleet’ to ‘true’.

### 21.5.1. IOService builder configuration

Service FlightScheduleState version 4, example for the plainxml protocol:

&lt;smog-service name=&quot;FlightScheduleState&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; protocol=&quot;plainxml&quot;&gt;
  &lt;service-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_schedule_state_4/services.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;protocol-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_schedule_state_4/protocol.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;service-mapping location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_schedule_state_4/mapping.xml&quot;/&gt;
&lt;/smog-service&gt;

Note that with this version of the service also protocols openapi, soap and plainjson are supported.

### 21.5.2. Registration of callback functions

This section describes the configuration required for handling additional flight leg information (e.g. custom SSIM
Record Type 4 information), both when importing and exporting schedules.

For this purpose it is necessary to use a custom service-mapping, using the example for the plainxml protocol
from above for the IOService builder configuration:

&lt;smog-service name=&quot;FlightScheduleState&quot; version=&quot;4&quot; protocol=&quot;plainxml&quot;&gt;
  &lt;service-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_schedule_state_4/services.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;protocol-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_schedule_state_4/protocol.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;service-mapping location=&quot;$CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_schedule_state_4.ext/mapping.xml&quot;/&gt;
&lt;/smog-service&gt;

The file $CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_schedule_state_4.ext/mapping.xml should be configured as below:

&lt;service-mapping xmlns=&quot;http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2&quot; target=&quot;air2_mave2&quot; language=&quot;Python&quot;&gt;
   &lt;include href=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_schedule_state_4/mapping.xml&quot;/&gt;

   &lt;input-mapping struct=&quot;flight_schedule_state.FlightScheduleStateMsg&quot;&gt;
      &lt;import alias=&quot;custom_helper&quot; name=&quot;datafeeds.flight_schedule_state_4.custom_helper&quot;/&gt;
      &lt;assign name=&quot;set_callback_import_record4&quot; expr=&quot;if_handler.register_callback_import_additional_info(custom_helper.import_record4)&quot;/&gt;
   &lt;/input-mapping&gt;

   &lt;input-mapping struct=&quot;flight_schedule_state.FlightScheduleStateRequest&quot;&gt;
      &lt;assign name=&quot;set_callback_export_record4&quot; expr=&quot;if_handler.register_callback_export_additional_info(custom_helper.export_record4)&quot;/&gt;
   &lt;/input-mapping&gt;
&lt;/service-mapping&gt;

In this example the package “datafeeds.flight_schedule_state_4” would exist in the CARMUSR and it would be included in the PYTHONPATH.
Note that the names of the custom helper module and the callback functions can be chosen freely. Also, the “name” attribute in the “&lt;assign&gt;”
statements is not significant and has no correlation with the name of the callback function. Also note that if callbacks are registered
both for import and export as in this example, the “&lt;import&gt;” statement is only needed in one of the “&lt;input-mapping&gt;” sections.

Finally a simplistic example of implementation of the actual callback functions in the “datafeeds.flight_schedule_state_4.custom_helper”
Python module:

def import_record4(leg, records, plan, ravesession):
   for dei, data in records:
       chain = ravesupport.RaveChain.ofActivity(ravesession, leg)
       code = ara_core.AnnotationCode.findActivityAnnotationCode(&#39;PUBLIC&#39;, plan)
       if dei==&quot;505&quot;:
           typ = &quot;domestic&quot;
           if rave.eval(chain, &#39;leg.%is_international%&#39;)[0]:
               typ = &quot;international&quot;
           leg.createAnnotation(f&quot;Flight is {typ} {data}&quot;, code, &quot;me&quot;, AbsTime(&quot;15JUN2015 00:00&quot;))

def export_record4(leg, plan, ravesession):
   records = []
   chain = ravesupport.RaveChain.ofActivity(ravesession, leg)
   typ = &quot;domestic&quot;
   if rave.eval(chain, &#39;leg.%is_international%&#39;)[0]:
       typ = &quot;international&quot;
       records.append((&quot;506&quot;, &quot;Very expensive!&quot;))
   records.append((&quot;505&quot;, typ))
   return records

, where “leg” is an ARA FlightLeg object and “records” is a list of tuples [(type_identifier, data)]. In an SSIM context the
type_identifier would be the Data Element Identifier (DEI).

## 21.6. Use cases

The following paragraph describe specific use cases like:

- the usage of the date varation at departure and at arrival,
- the rollout of the onward flight information.

### 21.6.1. DateVariation

The use cases is based on an example extracted from the SSIM-2011 Standard Schedules Information Manual specification issued in March 2011.

SSIM format

The input file used for this example includes some lines as below:

3 XX 12340101J15AUG0615AUG061234567 ATL20002000-0500S LGW09000900+0000S 737         ...          01000000
3 XX 12340102J16AUG0616AUG061234567 LGW10301030+0000S FRA13301330+0100  737         ...          11000000
3 XX 12340103J16AUG0616AUG061234567 FRA16001600+0100  SIN04000400+0800  737  ...  XX  614   ...  12000000
3 XX   010101J15AUG0615AUG061234567 AKL10301030+1200  HNL21152115-1000  777         ...          0A000000
3 XX   010102J14AUG0614AUG061234567 HNL23002300-1000  LAX07000700-0700  777  ...  XX  022   ...  A0000000

Flight_schedule_state input format

The time mode in the input file it Local time.

The input file above shows that the two legs of a multi-leg flight number 0001 can have the following attributes:

Leg1 has an arrival in the previous day compared to udor,
which corresponds in the input SSIM file to a date variation at departure that equals to ‘0’ and at arrival that equals to ‘A’,

Leg2 has a departure in the previous day compared to udor
which corresponds in the input SSIM file to a date variation at departure that equals to ‘A’ and at arrival that equals to ‘0’.

It is shown as well that a multi-leg flight 1234 can create 3 legs with the following attributes:

Leg1 has an arrival in the next day compared to udor,
which corresponds in the input SSIM file to a date variation at departure that equals to ‘0’ and at arrival that equals to ‘1’,

Leg2 has a departure and an arrival in the next day compared to udor,
which corresponds in the input SSIM file to a date variation at departure that equals to ‘1’ and at arrival that equals to ‘1’,

Leg3 has a departure on the next day and an arrival 2 days after compared to udor
which corresponds in the input SSIM file to a date variation at departure that equals to ‘1’ and at arrival that equals to ‘2’.

The resulting transformation of the SSIM file into a flight schedule state input message is the following:

The parser is even compatible with older versions of the SSIM format, where the date variation field was not present. When the date variation field is not present (spaces) is assumed that, if the UTC arrival time is less than the UTC departure time, date variation for the arrival time is set to ‘1’, for arrival the next day.

### 21.6.2. Aircraft rotation roll-out

This use case consists of the loadings of two input files with periods that partially overlap. It assumes that the configuration
have overridden the default disabled creation of ac rotations by calling FlightScheduleInterfaceHandler.enable_ac_rotations().

This situation is similar to the boundary of 2 consecutive monthly loading for instance.

Loading for period 28JAN2015 to 12FEB2015

This initial loading is the precondition of the second part of the use case on the aircraft rotation update mechanism.

The corresponding flight schedule state input message is the following:

    &lt;ns1:header carrier=&quot;AX&quot; periodEnd=&quot;2015-03-05&quot; periodStart=&quot;2015-01-28&quot; timeModeIsUTC=&quot;true&quot; title=&quot;Express&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;ns1:scheduledLeg carrier=&quot;AX&quot; endStation=&quot;BWI&quot; flightNumber=&quot;101&quot; scheduledEndTime=&quot;21:15:00&quot; scheduledStartTime=&quot;10:30:00&quot; seqNumber=&quot;1&quot; startStation=&quot;AKL&quot;&gt;
     &lt;ns1:schedulePattern arrivalDateVariation=&quot;0&quot; daysOfOperation=&quot;1357&quot; departureDateVariation=&quot;0&quot; periodEnd=&quot;2015-02-07&quot; periodStart=&quot;2015-01-28&quot;/&gt;
