      &lt;ns1:schedulePattern arrivalDateVariation=&quot;0&quot; daysOfOperation=&quot;1357&quot; departureDateVariation=&quot;0&quot; periodEnd=&quot;2015-02-11&quot; periodStart=&quot;2015-02-07&quot;/&gt;

The following objects are created:

- During period from 28/01 to 07/02:
Pattern1 creates legs 101 running from AKL to BWI every second day during the period 28/01 to 06/02 with a planned aircraft type 737.
Legs 101 have an onward flight to flight 102 departing the same day of its departure.

Pattern2 creates legs 102 running from BWI to AKL every second day during the period 28/01 to 07/02 with a planned aircraft type 737.
Legs 102 have an onward flight to flight 101 departing the same day of its arrival.

Pattern1 and Pattern2 creates one aircraft rotation object, Rot1 on which each flight legs is assigned to.
The Aircraft rotation, Rot1 is linked to the aircraft type 737.

- During period from 08/02 to 12/02:
Pattern3 creates legs 101 running from AKL to BWI every second day during the period 08/02 to 11/02 with a planned aircraft type 777.
Legs 101 have an onward flight to flight 102 departing the same day of its departure.

Pattern4 creates legs 102 running from BWI to AKL every second day during the period 08/02 to 12/02 with a planned aircraft type 777.
Legs 102 have an onward flight to flight 101 departing the same day of its arrival.

Pattern3 and Pattern4 creates one second aircraft rotation object, Rot2 on which each flight legs is assigned to.
The Aircraft rotation, Rot2 is linked to the aircraft type 777.

Loading for period 01JAN2015 to 14FEB2015

This second part of the use cases is loading an input file with a period that overlaps with the previous input file.

One can verify the behavior on the aircraft rotation update mechanism.

The corresponding flight schedule state input message is the following:

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot;?&gt;
&lt;ns1:putFlightScheduleStateRequest xmlns:ns1=&quot;http://flight_schedule_state_3.service.jcms.jeppesen.com&quot; created=&quot;2015-01-28T00:00:00&quot; source=&quot;sourceA&quot; version=&quot;3.0&quot;&gt;
  &lt;ns1:schedule&gt;
    &lt;ns1:header carrier=&quot;AX&quot; periodEnd=&quot;2015-02-13&quot; periodStart=&quot;2015-02-01&quot; timeModeIsUTC=&quot;true&quot; title=&quot;Express&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;ns1:scheduledLeg carrier=&quot;AX&quot; endStation=&quot;BWI&quot; flightNumber=&quot;101&quot; scheduledEndTime=&quot;21:15:00&quot; scheduledStartTime=&quot;10:30:00&quot; seqNumber=&quot;1&quot; startStation=&quot;AKL&quot;&gt;

--- SUBPAGE: flightlog.html ---

# 22. Flightlog

This chapter describes the interface that can be used for providing flight log data to JCMS from external systems.
Flight log data is used for keeping records of flights pilots have flown. A Flight log record typically
include details of the actual flight times including landing details. This interface can be used for providing
flight log records for operational or training flights (real or simulated).

Using this interface, JCMS can receive flight times (off-block and in-block times) according to the pilot in command of operational flights. These times are normally used for
calculations of crew duty time.

The interface can also be used for providing details on flight events such as take-offs, landings and other flight events that occurred on operational or training flights as well as simulators.
Flight events are typically needed for keeping track of recency rules for upholding certain qualifications, for example low visibility procedures.
Events can be provided to JCMS using two different modes:

- Flight centric: Flight events are provided to JCMS per flight (real or simulated).
- Pilot centric: Flight events are provided to JCMS per pilot, regardless of flight.

The interface allows systems to provide flight events on either mode depending on the data at hand.

Latest version of this interface is 1.
Link to Flightlog_1.xsd
Link to Flightlog_1.wsdl
Link to Flightlog_1_schema.json
Link to Flightlog_1_openapi.json

Available operations are:

pingPings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).

setFlightlogUpdate flight log related information (one-way request without any response message).

setFlightlogWithAckUpdate flight log related information with acknowledge response on successful update.

## 22.1. Identification of flights

The interface must be able to identify the concerned flight leg in JCMS when flight log information is provided for a flight leg.
One flight might have multiple operational legs in JCMS, a multi-leg flight, and each leg might consist of multiple atoms due to return to ramps.
The properties of the leg element in the request message is used for identifying a unique flight leg atom in JCMS.
The returnCounter property of the leg element should be used for indicating that the flight log concerns a return to ramp and also what
return to ramp event (starting from 1 if multiple returns has been made).

The concerned flight leg atom must exist in JCMS when flight log data is provided on this interface, which means that aircraft
movement and operational flight messages must have been processed by JCMS before the flight log is provided to this interface for the concerned flight.
The interface ignores flight logs and produce an error response if no unique flight leg atom can be found in JCMS. Existing deleted flight leg instances
(represented internally as implicitly cancelled) are ignored and not matched against.

It’s possible to configure the interface to use airline specific logic for matching of flights.

## 22.2. Identification of simulator activities

The interface must be able to identify the concerned simulator activity in JCMS when flight log information is provided for a simulator activity.
The properties of the simulator element in the request message is used for identifying a unique simulator activity in JCMS.

Field name is normally used as business key for ground tasks in JCMS. However name is not mandatory and does not necessarily have to be
unique, if additional fields are also provided as selection criteria. In order to support systems where name is not used, basically any
combination of fields that together uniquely identifies a ground task, is allowed.

Unless name is provided, fields activityType and station must match if provided. Other fields are only used as selection criteria if needed
in order to find a unique match.
If identifierDate is used for matching, note that the identifierDate of the activity in JCMS is the UTC based date of the start time of
the activity as specified when the activity was first created in JCMS. That means, in case the start time has been updated the current start time
does not necessarily match the identifierDate.

The concerned simulator activity must exist in JCMS when flight log data is provided on this interface.
The interface ignores flight logs and produce an error response if no unique simulator activity can be found in JCMS.

It’s possible to configure the interface to use airline specific logic for matching of simulator activities.

## 22.3. Updating flight log data

The interface can be used for setting or updating individual properties of flight log records in JCMS.
Flight log records in JCMS are only updated with the values provided in the request message.
For example, if a flight log only includes the inBlock property in request message JCMS would only
update the in-block time and leave other properties of the flight log record untouched.

## 22.4. Removing flight log data

Once created in JCMS, flight log information is not typically removed or updated. The interface still supports removal
of flight logs and related events trough usage of the deleteFlightlog and clearEvents elements in request message.
The main usage of the deleteFlightlog and clearEvents elements is for allowing an external system to provide flight log
data as a state, allowing the flight log records in JCMS to exactly match the provided information of the request message.

## 22.5. Error handling

If a flightlog record contains a pilotInCommand that is not assigned to the designated flight leg then that record is discarded
and the interface continues processing the next record.
If the eventsForFlight or eventsForPilot contains an event for which the activePilot is not assigned to the designated activity
or the designated activity is not recognized then that event record is discarded and the interface continues processing the next record.
In all other cases where a pilot, an activity or a catalog data item is not recognized, the entire message is discarded.

## 22.6. Examples

The following example provides a flight log for flight JJ 123 on the 15th of April including information
on pilot in command, take-off and landing.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;setFlightlogRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;example&quot; created=&quot;2016-04-15T12:05:00Z&quot;&gt;
    &lt;flightlog offBlock=&quot;2016-04-15T07:53:00Z&quot; inBlock=&quot;2016-04-15T11:58:00Z&quot; pilotInCommand=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
        &lt;leg carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2016-04-15&quot; flightNumber=&quot;123&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;/flightlog&gt;
    &lt;eventsForFlight&gt;
        &lt;leg carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2016-04-15&quot; flightNumber=&quot;123&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;T&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-15T08:03:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;FRA&quot; activePilot=&quot;123456&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;L&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-15T11:54:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;GOT&quot; activePilot=&quot;123456&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;/eventsForFlight&gt;
&lt;/setFlightlogRequest&gt;

The message below updates the in-block time of the flight log. The off-block time is not changed or removed in JCMS since it’s not provided in the request.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;setFlightlogRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;example&quot; created=&quot;2016-04-15T12:05:00Z&quot;&gt;
    &lt;flightlog inBlock=&quot;2016-04-15T12:05:00Z&quot; pilotInCommand=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
        &lt;leg carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2016-04-15&quot; flightNumber=&quot;123&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;/flightlog&gt;
&lt;/setFlightlogRequest&gt;

Events such as take-off and landings can be updated individually without any flightlog element in the request message.
Events are identified by using properties (type, airport, eventTime) as a key for the given flight leg.
JCMS creates a new event record if no existing record in JCMS matches the key.

The following message doesn’t update the eventTime of existing landing event (created by the first example request), instead a new event record is created in JCMS.
After processing this message, JCMS contains one take-off record and two landing records for this flight leg.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;setFlightlogRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;example&quot; created=&quot;2016-04-15T12:05:00Z&quot;&gt;
    &lt;eventsForFlight&gt;
        &lt;leg carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2016-04-15&quot; flightNumber=&quot;123&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;T&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-15T08:03:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;FRA&quot; activePilot=&quot;123456&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;!--  updated eventTime for the landing event --&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;L&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-15T11:58:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;GOT&quot; activePilot=&quot;123456&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;/eventsForFlight&gt;
&lt;/setFlightlogRequest&gt;

The request message must contain the clearEvents element if the intention was to update the eventTime of the existing landing event (instead of creating another landing event).
The clearEvents element indicates that existing event records for that flight leg should be removed before adding the events in the request message.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;setFlightlogRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;example&quot; created=&quot;2016-04-15T12:05:00Z&quot;&gt;
    &lt;eventsForFlight&gt;
        &lt;leg carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2016-04-15&quot; flightNumber=&quot;123&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;clearEvents /&gt; &lt;!-- removes existing events for this flight leg before adding new ones--&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;T&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-15T08:03:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;FRA&quot; activePilot=&quot;123456&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;L&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-15T11:54:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;GOT&quot; activePilot=&quot;123456&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;/eventsForFlight&gt;
&lt;/setFlightlogRequest&gt;

The clearEvent element removes all events that are not also provided in the request message.
The clearEvent element can further specify what type of flight log events that should be removed, for instance, only
removing events for a specific period, allowing to keep records that exist in JCMS but is not
provided in the request message.

Below is an example where flight log events are provided for a simulator activity on the 18th of April including information
on pilot in command, take-off and landing.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;setFlightlogRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;example&quot; created=&quot;2016-04-18T12:05:00Z&quot;&gt;
    &lt;eventsForFlight&gt;
        &lt;simulator name=&quot;MD80_XYZ123&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;T&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-18T08:03:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;FRA&quot; activePilot=&quot;987654&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;L&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-18T11:54:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;GOT&quot; activePilot=&quot;987654&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;/eventsForFlight&gt;
&lt;/setFlightlogRequest&gt;

In the next message another flight log event is added to the simulator activity. The message illustrates alternative ways to specify
the simulator activity associated with the flight log events. In this case the simulator activity can be uniquely identified with the
combination of identifierDate and activityType.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;setFlightlogRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;example&quot; created=&quot;2016-04-18T12:05:00Z&quot;&gt;
    &lt;eventsForFlight&gt;
        &lt;simulator startTime=&quot;2016-04-18T07:00:00Z&quot; activityType=&quot;P8&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;T&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-18T08:03:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;FRA&quot; activePilot=&quot;987654&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;L&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-18T11:58:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;GOT&quot; activePilot=&quot;123456&quot;/&gt;
    &lt;/eventsForFlight&gt;
&lt;/setFlightlogRequest&gt;

The interface also support the pilot centric mode, where events instead are provided per pilot instead of per flight leg.
The example message below provides a landing event performed by a specific pilot.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;setFlightlogRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;TestFlightLog&quot; created=&quot;2014-03-01T00:01:00Z&quot;&gt;
    &lt;eventsForPilot activePilot=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;L&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-15T08:03:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;FRA&quot; equipment=&quot;777&quot;&gt;
            &lt;simulator name=&quot;SIM1&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;/event&gt;
    &lt;/eventsForPilot&gt;
&lt;/setFlightlogRequest&gt;

The message above adds a new landing events in the flight log for crew member with id “123456”.
As in the flight centric mode, events can be updated individually by using properties (type, airport, eventTime) as a key
for the given pilot.

The crew centric mode also provides the clearEvents element for external systems to update events as a state as shown in the example below.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;setFlightlogRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;TestFlightLog&quot; created=&quot;2014-03-01T00:01:00Z&quot;&gt;
    &lt;eventsForPilot activePilot=&quot;123456&quot;&gt;
        &lt;!-- all landing events performed by this pilot in April 2016 --&gt;
        &lt;clearEvents removeFrom=&quot;2016-04-01T00:00:00Z&quot; removeTo=&quot;2016-05-01T00:00:00Z&quot; type=&quot;L&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;L&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-02T08:05:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;FRA&quot; equipment=&quot;777&quot; visibility=&quot;ILS-1&quot;&gt;
            &lt;simulator name=&quot;SIM1&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;/event&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;L&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-04T02:29:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;GOT&quot; equipment=&quot;777&quot;&gt;
            &lt;simulator name=&quot;SIM1&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;/event&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;L&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-10T12:17:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;FRA&quot; equipment=&quot;777&quot; visibility=&quot;ILS-2&quot;&gt;
            &lt;simulator name=&quot;SIM1&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;/event&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;L&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-14T06:11:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;GOT&quot; equipment=&quot;777&quot;&gt;
            &lt;simulator name=&quot;SIM1&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;/event&gt;
    &lt;/eventsForPilot&gt;
&lt;/setFlightlogRequest&gt;

## 22.7. Providing invalid enumeration values in request message

Some values in the request message refer to catalog data defined by various tables in JCMS. Example of such properties
are visibility, equipment (code of aircraft group) and airport. The complete message
is rejected in case of providing enumeration values which don’t match the catalog data in JCMS.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;setFlightlogRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;example&quot; created=&quot;2016-04-15T12:05:00Z&quot;&gt;
    &lt;eventsForFlight&gt;
        &lt;leg carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2016-04-15&quot; flightNumber=&quot;123&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;clearEvents type=&quot;L&quot;/&gt; &lt;!-- removes existing landing events for this flight leg before adding new ones--&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;L&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-15T11:54:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;GOT&quot; activePilot=&quot;123456&quot; visibility=&quot;ILS-A&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;/eventsForFlight&gt;
&lt;/setFlightlogRequest&gt;

The message above provides invalid enumeration value for visibility element. The message is rejected and no changes are saved in JCMS.
An error message with the following content is provided as response by the interface

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;setFlightlogFault xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;Flightlog&quot; code=&quot;MessageError&quot; subcode=&quot;ReferenceNotFound&quot; requestId=&quot;1&quot;&gt;
  &lt;reason&gt;visibility_type with key &#39;id=ILS-A&#39; not found in FlightLogEvent.visibility&lt;/reason&gt;
  &lt;sourceMessage&gt;&lt;![CDATA[&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;setFlightlogRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;example&quot; created=&quot;2016-04-15T12:05:00Z&quot;&gt;
    &lt;eventsForFlight&gt;
        &lt;leg carrier=&quot;JJ&quot; dateOfOrigin=&quot;2016-04-15&quot; flightNumber=&quot;123&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;clearEvents type=&quot;L&quot;/&gt; &lt;!-- removes existing landing events for this flight leg before adding new ones--&gt;
        &lt;event type=&quot;L&quot; eventTime=&quot;2016-04-15T11:54:00Z&quot; airport=&quot;GOT&quot; activePilot=&quot;123456&quot; visibility=&quot;ILS-A&quot; /&gt;
    &lt;/eventsForFlight&gt;
&lt;/setFlightlogRequest&gt;]]&gt;&lt;/sourceMessage&gt;
&lt;/setFlightlogFault&gt;

The error message states the reason for rejecting the message. In this case the provided value ISL-A for property visibility
is not found in JCMS catalog data table visibility_type.

## 22.8. IOService builder configuration

Service Flightlog version 1 (see Note for IOService builder), example for the plainxml protocol:

&lt;smog-service name=&quot;Flightlog&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; protocol=&quot;plainxml&quot;&gt;
  &lt;service-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flightlog_1/services.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;protocol-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flightlog_1/protocol.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;service-mapping location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flightlog_1/mapping.xml&quot;/&gt;
&lt;/smog-service&gt;

Note that with this version of the service also protocols openapi, soap and plainjson are supported.

--- SUBPAGE: ground_input.html ---

# 23. Ground activity input

Deprecated, please refer to the Crew Ground Tasks standard interface that handles both ground tasks and their crew assignments.

This chapter describes the interface that can be used for providing information about stationary ground tasks to JCMS from external systems.
Some ground tasks, for example flight simulators and other training activities, are usually planned and maintained by other systems.
This interface provides capabilities for keeping such ground tasks synchronized and up to date in JCMS throughout planning and operational phases.
The interface should only be used for managing ground tasks that can be assigned to one or more crew members, for example a simulator training where 3 crew members must attend.
Personal activities, designated for a specific crew member, that cannot to be shared or assigned to other crew members are typically not managed with this interface.
The interface doesn’t manage assignment of crew members to ground tasks, crew assignments are instead managed as part of a crew rostering or crew tracking process.
Examples of such personal activities are office duty, medical check-up, vacation, sick leave etc.

Latest version of this interface is 1.
Link to GroundInput_1.xsd
Link to GroundInput_1.wsdl
Link to GroundInput_1_schema.json
Link to GroundInput_1_openapi.json

Available operations are:

pingPings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).

setCrewGroundTasksUpdate ground tasks for crew (one-way request without any response message).

setCrewGroundTasksWithAckUpdate ground tasks for crew with acknowledge response on successful update.

## 23.1. Ownership of data

It’s important to have a clear data ownership of ground tasks for the involved systems, i.e. what system or process that owns and master
what ground tasks for different planning and operational phases.
The recommendation is that each master system owns ground tasks with specific activityType codes.

## 23.2. Identification of ground tasks

Systems must use a business key as identifier for ground tasks managed with this interface.
The field name serves as business key and is used for identifying ground tasks in communication between involved systems.
For ground tasks that are owned or mastered by an external system, the name shall contain the business key used by that system.
The business key should be set up in such a way that every key value is unique, or that it is unique within a certain time period,
like within a calendar year.

## 23.3. Providing ground tasks as a state

The interface can be used for synchronizing a set of ground tasks for a specific time period.
For example, if all ground tasks with activityType SIM are mastered by an external system, that system can provide
JCMS with all SIM activities for a specific month, year, or planning period. The interface would then create, update or cancel ground
activities in JCMS to match the state of the message provided by the source system.
The time period that can be updated in JCMS is limited by the IOServer data context.
It’s not possible to create ground tasks outside the data context period used by the IOServer.
By using the &lt;setGroundTask&gt; element, the ground task is updated if it already exists else it is created.
A state update is achieved by combining &lt;clearGroundTasks&gt; (see below) and &lt;setGroundTask&gt; elements in the same setCrewGroundTasks operation,
providing &lt;setGroundTask&gt; elements for all ground tasks matching the periods and activity types given in &lt;clearGroundTasks&gt;.

## 23.4. Updating a specific ground task

The interface can be used for setting or updating individual properties of existing ground tasks in JCMS by using the &lt;updateGroundTask&gt; element.
Ground tasks in JCMS are only updated with the values provided in the request message.
For example, if a an &lt;updateGroundTask&gt; element only includes the startTime property JCMS would only
update the start time and leave other properties of the ground task untouched.
An error is raised if the ground task specified by the &lt;updateGroundTask&gt; element is not found in JCMS.

## 23.5. Removing ground tasks

It’s possible to remove all ground tasks with a specific activityType and starting within a specific time period by using the &lt;clearGroundTasks&gt; element.
Only ground tasks within the IOServer data context can be removed, i.e. if the specified period stretches beyond the IOServer data context then any task starting
outside the data context period are left untouched.
The interface does not actually delete or remove any ground tasks in JCMS. Instead the ground tasks change status to Cancelled.

The &lt;updateGroundTask&gt; element can be used for removing (cancelling) individual ground tasks by providing the property isCancelled as true.

## 23.6. Examples

The following example illustrates how an external source system can provide all ground tasks with activityType R3 and SIM starting within October as a complete state.
The &lt;clearGroundTasks&gt; element is used for clearing all existing ground tasks starting at or after 2016-10-01T00:00:00Z but before 2016-11-01T00:00:00Z.

The complete state of each ground task is then provided in a separate &lt;setGroundTask&gt; element within same message.
A real message would potentially contain hundreds of ground tasks depending on the period and data being managed.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;setCrewGroundTasksRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/GroundInput/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;TMS&quot; created=&quot;2016-10-15T12:32:55Z&quot;&gt;

## 23.7. Providing invalid enumeration values in request message

Some values in the request message refer to catalog data defined by various tables in JCMS. Example of such properties
are type and station. The complete message
is rejected in case of providing enumeration values which don’t match the catalog data in JCMS.

The default configuration of this interface is to automatically create new types for trainingTag.

&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;setCrewGroundTasksRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/GroundInput/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;TMS&quot; created=&quot;2016-10-15T12:32:55Z&quot;&gt;
    &lt;setGroundTask name=&quot;AVD-OCT19#1&quot; type=&quot;GND-TRNG&quot; station=&quot;GOT&quot; startTime=&quot;2016-10-02T10:00:00Z&quot; endTime=&quot;2016-10-02T16:00:00Z&quot; venue=&quot;Aniara&quot;&gt;
        &lt;need&gt;
            &lt;position name=&quot;FC&quot; count=&quot;1&quot;/&gt;
            &lt;position name=&quot;FP&quot; count=&quot;1&quot;/&gt;
            &lt;position name=&quot;TR&quot; count=&quot;1&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;/need&gt;
        &lt;trainingTag&gt;AVD&lt;/trainingTag&gt;
    &lt;/setGroundTask&gt;
&lt;/setCrewGroundTasksRequest&gt;

The message above provides invalid enumeration value for type element. The message is rejected and no changes are saved in JCMS.
A fault message with the following content is provided as response by the interface.

&lt;?xml version=&#39;1.0&#39; encoding=&#39;UTF-8&#39;?&gt;
&lt;setCrewGroundTasksFault xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/GroundInput/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;GroundInput&quot; code=&quot;MessageError&quot; subcode=&quot;ReferenceNotFound&quot; requestId=&quot;1&quot;&gt;
  &lt;reason&gt;GroundTask.type, could not find any GroundActivityType with key &#39;(&#39;GND-TRNG&#39;,)&#39;&lt;/reason&gt;
  &lt;sourceMessage&gt;&lt;![CDATA[&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;
&lt;setCrewGroundTasksRequest xmlns=&quot;http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/GroundInput/v1&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; source=&quot;TMS&quot; created=&quot;2016-10-15T12:32:55Z&quot;&gt;
    &lt;setGroundTask name=&quot;AVD-OCT19#1&quot; type=&quot;GND-TRNG&quot; station=&quot;GOT&quot; startTime=&quot;2016-10-02T10:00:00Z&quot; endTime=&quot;2016-10-02T16:00:00Z&quot; venue=&quot;Aniara&quot;&gt;
        &lt;need&gt;
            &lt;position name=&quot;FC&quot; count=&quot;1&quot;/&gt;
            &lt;position name=&quot;FP&quot; count=&quot;1&quot;/&gt;
            &lt;position name=&quot;TR&quot; count=&quot;1&quot;/&gt;
        &lt;/need&gt;
        &lt;trainingTag&gt;AVD&lt;/trainingTag&gt;
    &lt;/setGroundTask&gt;
&lt;/setCrewGroundTasksRequest&gt;
]]&gt;&lt;/sourceMessage&gt;
&lt;/setCrewGroundTasksFault&gt;

The fault message states the reason for rejecting the message. In this case the provided value GND-TRNG for property type
is not found in JCMS catalog data table GroundActivityType.

## 23.8. IOService builder configuration

Service GroundInput version 1 (see Note for IOService builder), example for the plainxml protocol:

&lt;smog-service name=&quot;GroundInput&quot; version=&quot;1&quot; protocol=&quot;plainxml&quot;&gt;
  &lt;service-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.ground_input_1/services.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;protocol-spec location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.ground_input_1/protocol.xml&quot;/&gt;
  &lt;service-mapping location=&quot;$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.ground_input_1/mapping.xml&quot;/&gt;
&lt;/smog-service&gt;

Note that with this version of the service also protocols openapi, soap and plainjson are supported.

# 24. Crew Ground Tasks

This chapter describes a standard interface that can be used for providing information about stationary ground tasks and their crew assignments to
JCMS from external systems. Some ground tasks, for example flight simulators and other training activities, are usually planned and maintained
in dedicated systems separately from the ordinary trip planning and rostering process.
This interface provides capabilities for keeping such ground assignments synchronized and up to date in JCMS throughout planning and operational
phases. Unlike the Ground activity input standard interface, which is specialized in maintaining a state of ground tasks, this interface
can also handle the crew assignments to these tasks. Therefore it is typically used with Training Management systems (TMS) capable to manage not
only ground training activities, but the trainee and/or instructor assignments as well. In addition, this interface is also able to provide the
state of ground tasks (with crew assignments) as output, to be used with request-response or based on changes in JCMS. Both the input and output
uses a similar data structure for representing a ground task and its crew assignments, although there are minor differences in how
crew assignments are structured. The crew assignments, if provided by a source system, are handled as a state. This means that the set of
assignments attached to a task when sent FROM the TMS replaces whichever assignments that may previously exist in the data model for that task.

Latest version of this interface is 1.
Link to CrewGroundTask_1_schema.json
Link to CrewGroundTask_1_openapi.json

Available operations are:

pingPings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).

setGroundTaskCreate/Update/Cancel ground task(s), optionally with assignments, for crew (one-way request without any response message).

setGroundTaskWithAckCreate/Update/Cancel ground task(s), optionally with assignments, for crew with acknowledge response on successful update.

getGroundTaskByRangeGet ground tasks with crew assignments information for a given time range.

getGroundTaskByIdGet ground tasks with crew assignments information for given ground task id.

## 24.1. Ownership of data

It’s important to have a clear data ownership of ground tasks for the involved systems, i.e. what system or process that owns and master
what ground tasks for different planning and operational phases.
The recommendation is that each master system owns ground tasks with specific activityType codes.

## 24.2. Identification of ground tasks

Systems must use a business key as identifier for ground tasks managed with this interface.
The field id serves as business key and is used for identifying ground tasks in communication between involved systems.
For ground tasks that are owned or mastered by an external system, the id shall contain the business key used by that system.
The business key should be set up in such a way that every key value is unique, or that it is unique within a certain
time period, like within a calendar year.

## 24.3. Handling crew assignments

When an existing ground task is updated by the interface, crew assignments are handled as a state, i.e. any existing assignments are
replaced by the set of assignments specified for that ground task in the message. If the source system has not specified any assignment
information then the existing assignments are left unchanged by the interface. Crew members are assigned by the interface via personal trips,
i.e. one trip is created for each crew member’s assignment to a given ground task. Any assignment training tags are also attached to this crew-trip
assignment object in the data model. However, if for some reason a crew member is already assigned directly to a ground task in the
data model, this assignment is preserved by the interface and no personal trip is created.

## 24.4. Creating and updating ground tasks

Using the setGroundTask operation, the interface creates the ground tasks specified in the message, if they don’t already exist, and
updates those that exists to match the state of the ground task as specified in the message, including the provided set of assignments,
training tags and annotations. It is possible to cancel a ground task by specifying the flag isCancelled with value true. With the
setGroundTask operation it is also possible to provide a list of ground task id:s to cancel using the cancelGroundTasks element.
When canceling the tasks, the interface will delete the crew need of the task and any associated training tags and annotations. It will also
remove all assigned crew members and delete the personal trips through which crew is assigned. See interface schema for details.

## 24.5. Examples

The following example illustrates that this interface can be used to maintain ground tasks both with and without crew assignments.
Two different messages are used here to illustrate the two different use cases. First, a message from source system “A” is processed in order
to create ground tasks and crew assignments initially. It is then assumed that there is a TMS source system “B” without any knowledge of
crew assignments, sending a message to update some properties of one of the ground tasks. It is then verified that the update from system “B”
did not touch the existing crew assignments of the updated ground task. By omitting the element putAssignedCrew in that second message, any
existing crew assignments are left untouched by the interface. Thus, there is an important semantic difference between an omitted putAssignedCrew
element and one that contains an empty list of crew assignments. In the latter case the interface would deassign any existing crew assignments
from the ground task.

{

    &quot;version&quot;: &quot;1&quot;,

# 25. Plan synchronization

This chapter describes the standard interface that can be used for synchronizing the state (snapshot) of a complete plan
(rosters, trips, flights etc. for a certain period) in JCMS with external systems.
The interface is used for both importing and exporting the state of a plan to/from JCMS. Synchronization typically occurs periodically, for example
the plan from the tracking system might be synchronized on a daily basis to a rostering system as carry-in and pre-assignment data,
while the plan from a roster system might be synchronized on a monthly basis to the tracking system when rosters are to be published.
This interface is intended to be used for synchronizing the full state of a complete plan (or a well defined sub set of a plan) and can not
be used for synchronizing delta changes or changes of individual planning entities, for instance a change to a specific flight, trip or a roster.
It is however possible to import individual rosters by using import option ‘scope_rosters_crewid’ (see Import options).
The interface is bidirectional and uses the same message format for importing/exporting data to/from JCMS.

The current version of this interface is 3.
Link to PlanSync_3.xsd
Link to PlanSync_3_schema.json

Previous versions of this interface
Link to PlanSync_2.xsd (version 2)
Link to PlanSync_1_0.xsd (version 1.0)

## 25.1. Interface capabilities

The interface can export the current state of the live plan from JCMS to a message, which external systems can consume for synchronizing the plan.
It can also import a message from external system into the live plan in JCMS. The message contains the following planning entities for describing the plan:

Flight legs

Carries basic flight leg properties (departure/arrival airports, scheduled/operational times, etc.),
including return-to-ramp, wait-at-gate and other flight duty related events for all (non-deleted) leg instances.

Tasks

Carries information for representation of various stationary activities that doesn’t involve flying but must be planned,
for example personal activities (vacation, sick leave, etc.), ground tasks (simulator training, stand-by, etc.).
A task can optionally have a crew need, specifying the number of crew positions required for performing the activity.
In general, all ground tasks have a crew need, while personal activities don’t. Personal activities should not be included in any trips, but assigned directly to the crew member while ground tasks should be included in trips.
Each activity must have a code that describes the type of activity, i.e. what kind of training, standby, office duty, etc.,
the task represents. It’s recommended that the activity type codes are shared between the systems that are synchronized, but it’s possible
to configure custom specific mapping of activity types as part of an implementation project (see also Catalog data).

A ground task is “wrapped” inside a trip internally in JCMS, and the crew member is assigned to the wrapper trip instead of to the activity
directly. The interface creates the wrapper trip automatically for ground tasks.

- A personal activity is directly assigned to the crew member without being “wrapped” inside a trip.

Ground transports
Represents ground transport activities for crew (taxi, bus, train, shuttle etc.) that doesn’t involve flying. Ground transport activities are always
included in trips and can not be assigned directly to a roster.

Trips

Basic representation of the crew pairings in the plan. This entity contains a list of activities (flight legs, ground tasks and ground transports)
that makes up the pairing. Derived values, such as duty start, report times, rest time before/after etc. are not included since it’s assumed that
each system can derive these values separately.
The interface requires each trip to have a unique business key
which is known by the systems that are synchronized. The business key is used for matching trips when importing a message.
The business key to use can be configured, see Matching of Planning Objects for default behavior.

Rosters

Basic representation of crew member rosters. This entity contains a list of the trips and tasks assigned
to the crew member.

The plan in a message is always fully self contained, i.e. if the message contains a trip entity with five legs, it must also contain all five
flight leg entities in that trip. Likewise, all trips referenced from all rosters in a message must also be contained in the message.

The interface is not intended to be used for synchronizing crew data (addresses, passports, qualifications, etc.).
As with all standard interfaces, it’s possible to add or extend the message format with additional planning entities by configuration
as part of an implementation project.

Available operations are:

loadPlanUpdates the plan in the data model in JCMS with information from the provided message. Additional import options can be specified as message headers
for defining the import scope, detailing what information in data model that should be synchronized (see Import options).
The provided message might contain more information than actually is being updated in the data model.
This operation returns a response message providing the status of the import, i.e. if the import was successful or not, how many objects that were
created, updated or deleted in the data model. The whole message is always rejected and no changes are applied to the data model if the import
fails.

getPlanStateExports the plan from the data model in JCMS for a given time period. Additional export options can be specified as message headers for
defining the export scope, detailing what information in data model that should be exported.
This operation returns a message which can be processed by the loadPlan operation.

## 25.2. Catalog data

The plan data sent through this interface contains references to Catalog data (a.k.a Master data). However the PlanSync interface doesn’t provide
any mechanism for synchronizing the catalog data itself between JCTE and the external system, instead the Catalog data
standard interface can be used for that purpose. Routines also need to be established for keeping catalog data up-to-date between systems but that is
outside the scope of the interface itself. Also, the interface doesn’t contain any standard support for translating catalog data between systems.
Should such translation or mapping be needed as part of an implementation project, it is recommended to be implemented in the adaptors of the external
system, preferably in a way that can be shared and reused between the sending and receiving adaptors.

The following catalog data is used:

- Activity type codes
- Activity group codes
- Roster assignment Roles
- Airlines (normally IATA or ICAO codes)
- Airports (normally IATA or ICAO codes)
- Trip categories*
- Crew homebases
- Aircraft types (normally IATA or ICAO codes)
- Crew categories
- Activity training types* (training tags for flight legs and ground tasks)
- Trip training types* (training tags for trips)
- Crew assignment training types* (training tags specific for crew members assigned to a certain trip or activity)
- Crew assignment tag types* (roster tags used to indicate some additional information on a crew assignment)

* Note that trip categories, training types and crew assignment tag types are optional properties in the data model
and thus only relevant for the interface if such data is actually used in a specific implementation project.

When exporting Tasks, additional attributes describing whether is is a personal activity, on-duty or a transport, are also exported.
These are defined in the Activity group codes catalog data.

## 25.3. Supported time modes

The interface supports only UTC time mode. All times in the message must be in UTC time zone.

## 25.4. PlanSync scope

The concept of scope is valid both when importing and exporting a plan although there are details in how the scope is defined and
how it is applied that differ slightly between the two use cases. In general the scope is what defines and delimits the state of
the plan data. At both import and export, as a minimum the scope always consists of at least a period and may optionally be extended
with e.g. home base, crew category and planning area. For details on how to specify the scope parameters, see sections
Import options and Export options respectively. When several parameters are
specified they are always combined with logical AND to define the resulting scope.

When importing a plan the scope determines which part of the imported plan should be synchronized with which part of the plan that
may already exist in the data model. As an example if a planning area scope is specified, only those rosters belonging to the
specified planning area are synchronized. If a crew member only belongs to the specified planning area for a part of the scope period,
then the roster is only synchronized for that part of the period. Rosters in the imported plan for crew members that don’t belong to
the specified planning area are not imported. Another example/consequence of the same general scope logic is when specifying a scope
period that is “wider” than the trip and roster data contained in the imported plan. Since rosters are synchronized within the scope
period then any existing assignment not in the imported plan within that period will be cleared (unless they are locked).

When importing a plan there are also a couple of options that
control how the scope is applied when synchronizing plan data. The default logic is to replace everything on the roster, within the
specified scope, in the data model with that in the imported roster, for all rosters in the imported plan. By specifying option
‘delete_assignments=True’, the scope is also applied to those rosters that exist in the data model but not in the imported plan.
This means all assignments of such rosters, that matches the scope, will be removed (unless they are locked). By specifying option
‘clean_rosters=False’, the scope is not applied to existing assignments of the rosters in the imported plan. This means that any
assignment already existing in the data model of the imported rosters are left unchanged even if there is no matching assignment in
the imported plan. This can be used to make sure new assignments (unknown to the source system) in JCMS are kept even when a new plan
is loaded, regardless of their locked status. Enabling the option can for example be used when a previously loaded plan should be
replaced in JCMS.

When exporting a plan the scope simply defines which trips and rosters are extracted from the model.

## 25.5. Importing a plan

When importing a plan, the data model in JCMS is updated to match the planning entities in a given message.
Changes are only applied for the specified time period, defining the period scope of the import.
By providing additional options, it’s possible to further detail the scope of the import. This means it is possible
to control what planning entities in the data model that should be synchronized when importing a given message,
e.g. to only import rosters for a certain crew category.

Entities in JCMS data model are either created, updated, deleted or left unchanged when importing a plan. It’s important that
entities in the data model and entities in the message can be matched by the interface in order to decide whether a specific
entity should be created, updated, deleted or remain unchanged in JCMS data model. See sections below for for further details
on matching of planning entities.

### 25.5.1. Import options

The following options apply when importing a given plan file/message in JCMS. Some options control the scope of the imported data,
others control the way the imported plan data is synchronized with existing plan data in the data model.
If more than one scope option is specified a logical AND is applied to define a resulting scope.
Additional options for further detailing the import scope, can be added as part of an implementation project.
All scope parameters can be specified as message header parameters (using the option names in the table below).
Most scope parameters (period, home base, crew category and planning area) may alternatively be specified as
attributes in the imported plan file/message itself (see interface xsd schema). Message headers always takes
precedence in case a scope parameter is specified in both places.

Option

Description

Default value

Comment

scope_period_start

Optional. Defines the period start of data to be
imported from message to data model. Activities and
assignments starting at or after this value are
synchronized with the data model.

periodStart defined
in message
(mandatory)

Date time or AbsTime value in UTC, e.g.
‘2017-03-01T00:00:00Z’, ‘01MAR2017 00:00’.
Import fails if the scope period doesn’t overlap
with the period defined in the message.

scope_period_end

Optional. Defines the period end of data to be
imported from message to data model. Activities and
assignments starting before this value are
synchronized with the data model.

in message

Date time or AbsTime value in UTC, e.g.

with the period defined in the message.

### 25.5.2. Synchronization of flight legs

Flight legs are matched by the extended IATA leg key (dateOfOrigin, carrier, flightNumber, suffix, startStation, endStation) plus eventNumber.
Existing deleted flight leg instances (represented internally as implicitly cancelled) are ignored and not matched against.
If no match is found using this key, an extended match is made allowing some time deviation (1 hour by default) for the scheduled times.
The default time deviation is defined as class variable scheduledTimesMatchSlack in std_interfaces.common.RequestHolder, available
for override if needed.
JCMS is assumed to be the one of the two synchronized systems that holds the most recent state of flight legs. As a consequence, existing
flight legs in JCMS are not updated if schedule times or other attributes differ from the corresponding flight leg in the message. Nevertheless,
for various reasons, the external system may contain flight activities that were not included in the original flight plan. Therefore,
JCMS will create such missing flight legs and by default mark them as ‘non operational’ (operational status ‘N’).
If a carrier in a flight leg is not in own_carrier, it is treated as OAG flights, and AirTransport is matched/created instead of a FlightLeg. The own_carrier
is defined by Rave definitions, see Rave definitions. If an AirTransport was created from the interface, it will not be removed by the interface,
even though a new load without the FlightLeg not matching own_carier is made for the same period.
Only flight legs referenced by trips within the import scope, are synchronized.

### 25.5.3. Synchronization of tasks and ground transports

Ground activities are matched primarily by their name. Activities without name are matched by the alternative key (activityType, startStation,
endStation, scheduledStartTime, scheduledEndTime). If no match is found using this key, an extended match is made allowing some time deviation
(1 hour by default) for the scheduled times. The default time deviation is defined as class variable scheduledTimesMatchSlack in std_interfaces.common.RequestHolder, available
for override if needed. Only tasks and ground transports referenced by trips or rosters within the import scope, are synchronized.

The external system is assumed to be the master of tasks. Therefore tasks are always created if missing in the data model, and updated
if any attribute differ from what is specified in the message.

The data model in JCMS is updated to only contain one instance per task entity refId in the message. This means that it’s possible to express
that the same task should be used in different trips or rosters, for example if several crew participates on same training or transport activity.
It also means that identical tasks entities in the message must be duplicated, with different refId, if they should be represented as more than one
instance in JCMS. For example, two identical task entities, with different refId, are needed in the message if two crew members have vacation during
same period since each vacation instance in JCMS should be personal and it should be possible to update one without affecting the vacation of the other
crew member. In general, one task entity with unique refId, is needed in the message for each activity that is personal and should not be shared among
several rosters.

If option ‘delete_trips’ is ‘true’, tasks contained in a deleted trip may become orphans, i.e. if not assigned to any other trips or rosters.
Such activities are automatically deleted in JCMS, unless they are ground tasks (ground duties), if option ‘delete_orphan_tasks’ is set to ‘true’ otherwise such orphan activities
are left untouched in JCMS. Tasks spanning over the planning period are split into planning period chunks. The planning period is defined by Rave definitions,
see Rave definitions.

### 25.5.4. Synchronization of trips

It is assumed that each trip in the message has a unique business key which can be used for matching.
Trips are not matched based on the activities in the trip. By default, matching of trips follows the general rules described in the introduction,
see Matching of Planning Objects.

Missing trips are created in JCMS. Conflicting trips are updated according to the imported version of the trip. A conflicting trip is one where the set of
assigned activities in the trip differ between the message and the data model.

Properties of a trip are updated in JCMS to match what is specified in the message. By default, existing trips within the given scope, that are not
included in the message, are deleted in JCMS (see option delete_trips). Trips starting between scope_period_start and scope_period_end are synchronized by default.

The option update_carryin_trips can be used for also including carry-in trips, i.e. trips overlapping scope_period_start.
The following logic applies for synchronizing carry-in trips:

- Carry-in trips are matched using the trip business key. If no matching trip is found, the interface tries to match carry-in trips using trip activities and crew composition.
- Carry-in trips matching a carry-in trip in the message are updated to match the imported version of the trip for activities starting after scope_period_start.
- Carry-in trips in the plan not matching any carry-in trip in the message are not updated or deleted.
- Carry-in trips in the message not matching any carry-in trip in the plan are partly created as new trips, only containing the trip activities starting after scope_period_start.

### 25.5.5. Synchronization of rosters

Rosters are matched by crewId which is assumed to be the same in JCMS and the external system. It is also assumed that the crewId is not changing
over time for crew members. Each roster in a message is regarded as the complete state for the specified period and scope, i.e.
all existing assignments (and volunteer periods) on the roster in the data model are replaced with the roster in the message within the specified period
and scope by default. The roster layering concept described in Roster layer concept applies and it can be used for configuring how roster
updates should be applied, e.g. to define a filter for certain activity types. By default, without any configuration, the entire roster is replaced,
unless the option clean_roster is False.
Rosters that exists in JCMS data model, but not in a given message are never cleared (deleted), even if the roster belongs to the specified scope in
the data model, unless the option delete_assignments is True. Locked assignments are never deleted by PlanSync.

Rosters in JCMS are updated to contain the tasks assignments as specified in the message. The same activity is assigned to different rosters in JCMS if
the different rosters in the message refer to the same task, regardless if the activity type of the task is personal or not.
It is possible to mark an assignment as locked, and thereby it will be updated in the plan as a locked assignment.

The option update_carryin_trips can be used for synchronizing crew assignments to carry-in trips, overlapping scope_period_start.
Note that scope_period_start in this context may be individual per roster if using import option scope_planning_area.
The following logic applies for synchronizing crew assignments to carry-in trips:

- Assignments to carry-in trips are not created, updated or deleted if a matching trip is found in the plan.
- Assignments to carry-in trips are created if no matching trip is found in the plan.

### 25.5.6. Rave definitions

The following Rave variables are defined in the CARMSYS and used by the PlanSync standard interface:

- interfaces_core.%plansync_in_pp_start_at_time_utc%(AbsTime t): Defines the start time of the planning period at time t, used for splitting long tasks into planning period chunks.
- interfaces_core.%plansync_in_pp_end_at_time_utc%(AbsTime t): Defines the end time of the planning period at time t.
- interfaces_core.%plansync_in_split_margin%: Defines a margin the task have to start before planning period start or end after planning period end, for it to be split. Used to avoid splitting tasks that only exceeds planning period with this margin.
- interfaces_core.%is_own_carrier%(String carrier): Defines the carriers that belongs to this Airline. If a carrier from a flightLeg does not belong to own_carrier, an AirTransport is searched/created instead of a FlightLeg.
- interfaces_core.%crew_belongs_to_planning_area_from_utc%(String planningArea, AbsTime periodStart, AbsTime periodEnd): Returns start of interval within the given period, in which the crew member belongs to the given planning area. Default periodStart.
- interfaces_core.%crew_belongs_to_planning_area_to_utc%(String planningArea, AbsTime periodStart, AbsTime periodEnd): Returns end of interval within the given period, in which the crew member belongs to the given planning area. Default periodEnd.
- interfaces_core.%trip_belongs_to_planning_area%(String planningArea): Returns True if the trip belongs to the planning area with the given name. Default True.
- interfaces_core.%planning_areas%: Returns a comma separated list of available planning areas. Default “”.

The business logic behind these Rave variables need to be implemented in a CARMUSR to comply with the
expected behavior of each individual airline.

### 25.5.7. Error handling

The interface conforms to the same error handling strategy as most of the standard interfaces, i.e. to reject
the incoming message if it cannot be entirely and completely processed. In such cases one or more error
messages are also issued in the log file, containing detailed information about the error.

If the interface encounters several errors, all errors belonging to the same message are collected before
the processing is terminated.

## 25.6. Exporting a plan

The full state of the plan in JCMS is exported to as a single message. The plan is exported
for the specified scope (see Export options).
As a minimum, the scope is defined by the exported period. By providing additional scope options, it’s possible to further detail the scope of the export.
This means it is possible to control what planning entities in the data model that should be exported to the message, e.g. export only rosters that
belong to a given homebase or crew category.
In addition, the roster layering concept described in Roster layer concept applies and it can be used for e.g. defining a filter to only export
certain activity types. By default, without any configuration, the entire roster is exported.

All activities (trips, flight legs, ground tasks etc.) within a given eport scope are exported irrespective of activity status, i.e. regardless if
cancelled or not. Open time tasks (i.e. ground tasks with unfulfilled need) are always exported, if within the exported period.

### 25.6.1. Export options

The following options apply when exporting the plan from JCMS data model to a message. Additional options can be added as part of an implementation project.
All options are specified as attributes in the request message, see the XSD.

Note that for the options controlling the exported scope, roster scope overrides trip scope such that a trip that is outside the scope is included in the
export anyway if assigned to a roster that is within the scope.

Option

Description

Default value

Comment

periodStart

Mandatory scope parameter. Defines the period start
of data to be  exported from data model to message.
Activities and assignments starting at or after this
value are exported. May be overridden by specifying
header parameter ‘scope_period_start’.

Date time or AbsTime value in UTC, e.g.
‘2017-03-01T00:00:00Z’, ‘01MAR2017 00:00’
Export fails if value doesn’t fall within the
plan period of the data context.

periodEnd

Mandatory scope parameter. Defines the period end of
data to be exported from data model to message.
Activities and assignments starting before this
value are exported. May be overridden by specifying
header parameter ‘scope_period_end’.

Date time or AbsTime value in UTC, e.g.
‘2017-03-01T00:00:00Z’, ‘01MAR2017 00:00’
Export fails if value doesn’t fall within the
plan period of the data context or if value is
before scope-period-start.

homeBase

Optional scope parameter. Defines the rosters/trips
to be exported from data model by home base.
Don’t consider homebase if value is empty.

empty

Homebase code, e.g. ‘ZHR’ or ‘GNV’.
Fails if the data model
doesn’t contain the specified homebase.
Homebase in data model is used for deciding if
roster should be exported or not. Criterion
for exporting a roster is that crew is based at
the provided homebase at the start of the
scope-period. A crew’s roster is imported for the
full scope-period even if crew is based at
the provided homebase for a part of the
scope-period.

crewCategory

Optional scope parameter. Defines the rosters/trips
to be exported from data model by crew category.
Don’t consider crew category if value is empty.

empty

Comma separates string of crew categories,
e.g. ‘COC, CAB’. Fails if the data model doesn’t
contain the provided crew categories.
Crew category in data model is used for deciding if
roster/trip should be exported or not. Criterion
for exporting a roster is that crew belongs to
the provided category at the start of the
scope-period. When applied to a trip, crewcategory
is derived from the trip’s crew complement.
A crew’s roster is exported for the
full scope-period even if crew belongs to
the provided category for a part of the
scope-period.

planningArea
(added in version 3)

Optional scope parameter. Defines the rosters/trips
to be exported from the data model by planning area.
Don’t consider planning area if value is empty.

empty

Name of planning area, e.g. ‘FD_737’
Only rosters/trips belonging to the specified
planning area are exported. The exported planning
area is specified as a property ‘planningArea’ of
the plan element in the exported data.
N.B. The entire roster for the exported period is
included even if the crew member only belongs to
the specified planning area for a part of the
exported period.

exportRosters

Optional. Specifies whether or not to export
rosters.

true

By setting this option to ‘false’, only trips are
synchronized. If set to ‘false’, the scope
parameters for period, home base and crew category
control the subset of trips being
imported/synchronized.

However, by setting option allow-missing-rosters=true rosters for missing crew members are ignored but the rest of the
message content is processed as normal.
In this case it would result in creation of the same objects as in example Importing trips and rosters,
given that none of these objects existed before importing the message.
This option is not recommended to use in a production environment as it may lead to inconsistent plan state between JCMS
and the external system.

# 26. Trip Input

This chapter describes the interfaces that can be used to provide trip data to JCMS.
The information can be transferred via publish/subscribe if the sending system is considered master of the provided information.
The same kind of messages can be used for inbound service with “ack” or state response if JCMS is regarded master.
It is in this case strongly recommended for the sending system to attach the state indicator for conflict detection purposes.

The current version of this interface is 3.
Link to TripStateInput_3.xsd
Link to TripStateInput_3.wsdl
Link to TripStateInput_3_schema.json
Link to TripStateInput_3_openapi.json

## 26.1. Interface capabilities

Since trips are business objects with a fixed scope of data content they are most commonly updated based on new state information.
A message provides the new state of a (set of) trip(s). The “setTrips” operation can be used in batch or online mode.
Whether an online flow can be parallelized depends on the presence of a state reference,
either the cid (in case of a service) or a corresponding attribute from the source system (custom attribute).
When a state reference is present then the messages can be handled in parallel and out of order conditions will be detected.

Available operations are:

pingPings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).

setTripsCreates or updates trips in JCMS with information from the provided message (one-way request without any response message).

setTripsWithAckSame as setTrips but with an acknowledge response on successful operation (request/response).

For the matching of trips, general rules described in the introduction apply, see Matching of Planning Objects.
By default, only “name” and “dateOfOrigin” in TripMatch elements are used for trip matching, other attributes (“category”, “homeBase”
“startStation”, “endStation”, “startTime”, “endTime”) are not used for matching and will be removed in future version of this interface.

A trip always has a home base (where it starts and ends) and a set of roles to be filled (the CrewComplement).
A trip can have a category, which is a classification inside JCMS to distinguish different types of trips, e.g. production trips from simulator setups.
The category can be to indicate e.g. ownership or source of the trip. It is a static enumeration, so it can’t be used to indicate dynamic grouping of trips.

The trip then consists of a set of activity (e.g. flight leg, ground task, etc.) assignments,
a role is only given per activity if it deviates from the trip’s CrewComplement (typically set to DH, deadhead).
For each activity it is possible to provide the stations and times that are the planned status of this activity in this trip.
If these are given they are represented in JCMS as so called “planned assignment attributes” and they are used to detect deviation from planned state
(e.g. for alert generation) as well as for some rules.
JCMS will use the current state (at time of the message evaluation) of the assigned activities to fill the assignment attributes (stations and times),
i.e. JCMS will assume that the current state of the activities defines the planned state of the trip.
In the same manner also planned stations on the trip level itself can be included and will be used if present.
At the initial trip creation, the date attribute dateOfOrigin is used as an original value for times. Later when processing the message,
JCMS will use the current state (at time of the message evaluation) of the assigned activities to fill the trip times.
For example, the start time of a trip will be derived from the start time of the first flight leg.

The following assumptions are made regarding existence of activities referenced in a trip message:

Flight legs are expected to exist, regardless whether they are of the own carrier or of some other carrier (e.g. OAG deadheads).
However if a leg is missing, the trip is still accepted and the leg is created but marked cancelled. Scheduled leg times are optional
as parameters. They are not used for matching of flight legs but they are needed when creating new flight legs.

Any non-flight activity (task) without name will be created if it is not already assigned to the trip. For tasks requiring a need, the need will be
derived from the trip’s crew composition. If several trips share the same task, e.g. a simulator activity, one instance of the task
is created for each trip, i.e. the crew need of a particular task instance only reflects the crew composition of the trip it belongs to.

If name is provided for a task, only name will be used to identify the task, regardless if it is already assigned to the trip or not. If it exists more than
one task with the same name, it will be handled as a task without name.

- It is considered as an error when an activity in a trip has the start time after the end time. As a result, the message is disregarded.
- The interface is primarily designed for planning usage. Flight legs’ return or wait events are not supported by the interface.

It is possible to configure the interface so that any changes to a trip, which is assigned to crew, are also acknowledged automatically
for each crew.

Training information can optionally be provided to indicate that a trip is used for training, and possibly also
what kind of training is performed. This is done by providing training tags that are defined in the customization layer.
Training tags are updated as a state, i.e. the trip in JCMS is updated to match the training tags in the inbound message.
All training tags are removed from the trip in JCMS if the inbound message doesn’t have any training tags, even if the tags
were added by some other user or process.

All other information is normally calculated, but published (frozen) information can be provided in customizations.
How to do that depends on the type of information.
In many cases there are custom attributes on the assignment or trip object level that are used as overrides.
In other cases separate elements are needed.

## 26.2. Use cases

### 26.2.1. Create a new trip

If the trip provided in a setTrips message doesn’t exist it is created. The status code of the trip activity is scheduled.
Times of the trip or assignment level are derived from the actual flight content.
If a referenced flight doesn’t exist, it is represented as a non-operating leg.

### 26.2.2. Cancel a trip

If the trip provided in a cancelTrip message exists:
* The trip is marked as cancelled (Not Operating any longer but NOT removed).
* The work coverage provided by the given trip is reset which means the crew complement is set to Null. The consequence is that the corresponding crew need is now shown in Open time.
If the trip provided in a cancelTrip message doesn’t exist an error is generated.

### 26.2.4. Update a cancelled trip

The original trip is marked as Cancelled. This trip could have been marked as cancelled from a cancelTrip message or from the UI.

If the input provided is a setTrip or updateTrip then the existing cancelled trip will be marked as scheduled again and updated accordingly.
If the input provided is an addTrip message of the same matching trip then it will fail and an error will be generated.

Note that trip annotations created from this interface are always given the predefined annotation code PUBLIC.
The PUBLIC annotation code has attribute ‘is_public’ set to True in the data model, meaning that it is visible
to crew members. There may be other annotation codes defined in the system with attribute ‘is_public’ set to True,
but in the Trip Input interface it is currently not possible to specify an annotation code, hence the default
code PUBLIC is assigned.

### 26.2.6. Update a trip with annotation

Note that all trip annotations for crew (PUBLIC), will be replaced by the updated annotation.
